patterns.name: Albie Whore
patterns.description: Richard Reagan's pearlescent bay anchovy and silverside imitation for false albacore, bonito, and striped bass. Built with sparse white bucktail and flash over a slender hook, its tight, low-profile design cuts through fast rip current. Swing or strip through tidal seams; the Northeast coastal standard from Cape Cod to the Outer Banks during fall blitzes.
patterns.image_source: Bear's Den Fly Fishing Co. product photo — clean square background, clear side profile

regional_usage.notes: One of the definitive OBX albie flies — saltwaterflies.com specifically cites North Carolina among the top regions for this pattern when silversides are the dominant forage during the Cape Lookout fall blitz.

patterns.name: Alphlexo Crab
patterns.description: Designed by Seychelles guide James Christmas, refined by Umpqua's Alec Gerbec, the Alphlexo Crab uses an open mesh body with orange latex innards over a weighted hook to mimic a crab tumbling across the flat. Sink fast, dead-drift or short strips. The top-ranked Indo-Pacific permit and triggerfish pattern at Alphonse, Astove, and Cosmoledo.
patterns.image_source: Superflies.com product photo — Alphlexo Crab Original, clean side profile on white background

regional_usage.notes: Developed by Alphonse Island guide James Christmas from the Flexo Crab and further refined by Alec Gerbec; the mesh-body crab with orange innards is documented as the top permit and triggerfish pattern at Alphonse, Astove, and Cosmoledo.
The Indian Ocean's defining crab pattern; tan and olive variants are the go-to for tailing triggers on Nubian sand and turtle-grass flats where colour-matching the substrate is critical.
Oman's Shuwaymiyah area holds permit that patrol sardine baitballs (unique behaviour documented by Mark Harris); an Alphlexo dropped ahead of them covers the crab-eating instinct.
Mozambique bonefish on the Benguerra/Bazaruto channel flats respond to small crab imitations; the tan Alphlexo is the starting point for any Indian Ocean bonefish flat exploration.

Nylon-mesh body crab with orange bead eyes; dominant permit and triggerfish pattern across all Indian Ocean flats including the Maldives; key pattern for the lagoon and sandy-flat triggerfish at Huvadhoo Atoll. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Alphlexo Crab'.

Dominant permit pattern for St Brandon's Indo-Pacific permit; FlyCastaway brochure and multiple St Brandon's reports specifically list this as the go-to permit fly for the atoll's prolific permit fishery. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Alphlexo Crab'.

patterns.name: Andino Deceiver
patterns.description: Bob Popovics and Jimmy Andino's large streamer with a distinctive muddler-style diving/pushing head and long feather tail, originally tied in Argentina to imitate river dorado baitfish. Crossed over to saltwater as a Baja roosterfish and jack crevalle pattern. Fast, erratic strips make the bulky head push water and create turbulence mimicking panicked baitfish.
patterns.image_source: Big Y Fly Co product photo, clean background, clear side profile of weighted Andino Deceiver

regional_usage.notes: Originally an Argentine dorado pattern, the Andino Deceiver with its muddler-style diving head has crossed over as a primary Baja roosterfish fly; its erratic action on fast strips mimics panicked baitfish.

Hollow-tied bucktail-and-synthetic variant of the Deceiver that maintains a large profile while remaining lightweight to cast; proven on Pacific roosterfish, Pacific sailfish, and large inshore species throughout the Costa Rica Pacific.

patterns.name: Apte II Tarpon Fly
patterns.description: A Keys-style hackle-and-saddle fly imitating the shrimp and baitfish that large tarpon feed on in the Lower and Middle Keys. Distinguished from the original Stu Apte Tarpon Fly by adjusted material proportions and hook size. Fished dead-drifted or with a slow strip on incoming tide paths. Sold commercially by Reel Flies.
patterns.image_source: reelflies.com — commercial product photo, white background, fly on hook

regional_usage.notes: A Keys-style hackle-and-saddle fly tied in the Stu Apte tradition, distinct from the original Stu Apte Tarpon Fly in its material proportions and hook size; sold commercially by Reel Flies and Jackson Hole Fly Company as a separate pattern.

patterns.name: Articulated Baitfish
patterns.description: Imitates a wide range of small baitfish without matching a specific species, relying on a jointed profile at 11.5 cm (4/0) to trigger ambush predators. Developed by Stephen Chatterton (fishonfly.com.au), the two-section articulated design pulses realistically on the strip. Primary pattern for sighted GTs, barramundi, mangrove jack, and queenfish around Australian structure and PNG river systems.
patterns.image_source: fishonfly.com.au — Stephen Chatterton's articulated baitfish pattern page

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Large jointed baitfish at 11.5 cm (4/0) developed by Stephen Chatterton (fishonfly.com.au) as a 'go-to' for sighted ambush predators and pelagics; documented for GT, barra, mangrove jack, and queenfish around Central Queensland and Gulf structure.

Stephen Chatterton documents this articulated pattern as his primary sighted-ambush-predator fly; its large jointed profile is exactly the profile used by Australian guides targeting PNG black bass and barramundi around timber and undercuts.

patterns.name: Atlantic Sardine Baitfish
patterns.description: Imitates Atlantic sardines and engraulids—primary forage in Gabon's Ndogo estuary. Tied EP-fiber or Puglisi style in silver/olive on 3/0–5/0, with a flat baitfish profile 8–12 cm long. Fished on floating or intermediate lines through crashing tarpon and threadfin schools. Distinct from Indo-Pacific sardine imitations used in Seychelles.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; West African sardine baitfish patterns are not commercially photographed

regional_usage.notes: EP-style or Puglisi-style sardine imitation in silver/olive tied on 3/0–5/0 to match the Atlantic sardines and engraulids that schools of tarpon and threadfin crash in the Ndogo estuary; a distinct bait profile from Indo-Pacific sardines used in Seychelles/Christmas Island patterns.

patterns.name: Avalon Permit Fly
patterns.description: Mauro Ginevri's shrimp imitation developed at Cayo Largo, Cuba, credited with over 134 Cuban permit. Weighted keel and clicking bead system orient the hook up and sink fast. Its large shrimp profile and rattle action trigger permit on hard-bottom flat edges. Cast to tailing fish, let it sink, and strip slowly.
patterns.image_source: Pacific Fly Fishers fly shop product photo, clean square image

regional_usage.notes: Fast-sinking shrimp imitation that orients hook-up; listed by Blue Bonefish Belize as a strong deep-water permit pattern in addition to its Cuban origins.

Originally developed for Cuban permit at Cayo Largo by Mauro Ginevri; its weighted keel, clicking bead system, and large shrimp profile have crossed over to Keys permit guides who fish it on the same shrimp-rich flat edges permit favor.

Shrimp imitation designed by the Avalon lodge manager to sink quickly and orient hook-up; Fly Fisherman Magazine and Fly Tyer document it as the pattern behind Cuba's Grand Slam boom, with over 134 permit credited to it on Cuba's southern coast alone.

Originally developed for Atlantic permit in Cuba, the Avalon is used by Seychelles guides for the multi-species flats; confirmed catches of triggerfish, bonefish, and bluefin trevally on Alphonse flats.

Directly observed in use by Los Roques guides on permit in a January 2025 trip report (Go Fishing Worldwide); a guide shouted to grab the rod with the 'Avalon on' when permit were spotted tailing — this keel-weighted shrimp from Cuba has become the go-to permit fly across the Caribbean including Los Roques.

Designed by Avalon's Mauro Ginevri at Cayo Largo and tested in a swimming pool to ensure correct hook-up orientation at all retrieve speeds; Fly Fisherman Magazine (2016) documents it accounting for 134 permit in Cuba alone and Cuban Fishing Centers states it 'has been responsible for the majority of the permit captures' at both Cayo Largo and Jardines de la Reina.

patterns.name: Avalon Tarpon Fly
patterns.description: A slim, Keys-influenced hackle-and-saddle streamer developed by guide Mauro Ginevri at Avalon Fly Fishing Lodge in Cuba's Cayo Largo. Designed as a tarpon companion to Ginevri's Avalon permit fly, with a reduced hackle profile suited to the clear channels of Jardines de la Reina. Fished on a slow intermediate strip in current seams where large tarpon hold.
patterns.image_source: blog.saltyflytying.com — tying authority blog credited to Mauro Ginevri; note this image may show the Avalon permit variant rather than the specific tarpon version

regional_usage.notes: A Keys-style tarpon pattern developed at the Avalon Fly Fishing Lodge in Cayo Largo by Italian-Cuban guide Mauro Ginevri as a companion to his permit fly, with a slim hackle profile designed for large tarpon in the clear channels of Jardines de la Reina.

patterns.name: Bauer Crab
patterns.description: Will Bauer's 1980s fur-and-rubber-leg crab imitation, developed for Belize permit with guide Lincoln Westby. Dense, compact profile tied on weighted hooks — lands quietly and sinks hook-point-up, imitating a fleeing blue crab. Dead-drifted or twitched on Belizean turtle-grass flats; Belizean guides consider it the most consistently effective permit pattern in the country.
patterns.image_source: Fulling Mill product photo — Tungsten Bauer Crab Tan, high-resolution clean white background

regional_usage.notes: Developed specifically for Belize permit in the 1980s in collaboration with guide Lincoln Westby; considered by Belizean guides to be the most consistently effective permit fly on the country's turtle-grass flats.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Listed by Pesca Maya as 'Bauer's Fur Crab' for permit on Ascension Bay flats; its compact profile works well on the sandy and grass mixed bottom of the Sian Ka'an.

patterns.name: Beast Fleye
patterns.description: A large-profile bucktail-over-monofilament baitfish pattern built for giant trevally on Indo-Pacific atolls. Its sparse construction allows long aerodynamic casts to cruising GT on exposed reef edges; the profile fills out when wet to suggest a substantial baitfish. Strip aggressively in short, hard pulls to trigger predatory strikes from fast-moving fish.
patterns.image_source: AOS fly shop product photo — clean white background, clear side profile of olive Beast Fleye

regional_usage.notes: Sparse bucktail-over-monofilament fly noted for Astove and Cosmoledo GT fishing; its slim profile fills in when wet, allowing long casts necessary when targeting fast-cruising GTs on exposed reef edges.

patterns.name: Bedhead
patterns.description: Imitates the dense-bodied sand crabs that permit and triggerfish feed on across Indian Ocean flats. Named for its weighted, compressed EP-fiber crab profile that sinks fast and sits low on the bottom. Developed by Alphonse Fishing Co. guides circa 2015, it features rubberleg movement and a wide silhouette. Deadlocked permit and trigger staple in Seychelles, Maldives, and Rodrigues.
patterns.image_source: No specific Bedhead crab image found in searched sources (Alphonse FC, SaltFlyPro, BigTimeFLies, Fulling Mill)

regional_usage.notes: Dense-bodied EP-style crab with a weighted 'bedhead' profile; listed in the Complete Seychelles Fly Assortment as a key permit/triggerfish pattern; directly applicable to the Maldives flats where triggerfish are a principal target on guide-led trips.
Dense-body crab for the Indian Ocean permit fishery; confirmed in the Complete Seychelles Fly Assortment as a permit/trigger standard, directly applicable to St Brandon's permit-focused fishing.

patterns.name: Big Eye Tarpon
patterns.description: Bob LeMay's sparsely tied Keys tarpon fly features oversized 3D eyes, palmered hackle body, and a light flash accent that creates shrimp-like undulation on the strip. The exaggerated eye is a visual trigger for shallow-water tarpon. Typically fished with a slow-medium strip on 10–12 weight rods along the Florida Keys migration flats.
patterns.image_source: floridakeysoutfitters.com — specialist fly shop, clean product photo, correctly named

regional_usage.notes: A sparsely tied Keys-style fly by Bob LeMay featuring prominent eyes, palmered hackle, and a light flash accent that creates shrimp-like movement; sold by Umpqua Feather Merchants specifically for the Florida Keys destination.

patterns.name: Big Eye Tuna Fly
patterns.description: A large synthetic baitfish imitation dressed with layered EP or craft fibers and dominated by oversized 3D resin eyes that trigger a tuna's hard-wired predator response. Cast to daisy-chaining billfish or teased yellowfin and dorado off Baja. Strip fast and erratically to keep pace with pelagic targets in open water.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants product photo — Big Eye Baitfish, closest commercially available match with prominent 3D eyes

regional_usage.notes: A large-profile synthetic baitfish imitation with oversized 3D eyes that trigger the tuna's visual predator response; critical for daisy-chaining billfish and chunking tuna off East Cape and La Paz.
Sardine/anchovy-profile baitfish fly with prominent epoxy big-eye that imitates the sardines and blue runners yellowfin tuna key on under spinner-dolphin schools throughout the Costa Rica Pacific.

patterns.name: Big Game Brush Fly
patterns.originator: Flymen Fishing Company (based on Seychelles GT patterns)
patterns.description: A large, durable brush-style baitfish imitation tied by Flymen Fishing Company for giant trevally, Hawaiian ulua, and GT-class fish worldwide. Built from Fish-Skull Fish-Brush material on a 6/0 hook, available in high-contrast colors like black/purple and grey. Fished with aggressive single or double strips in the breaking surf zone where GT and bluefin trevally ambush bait.
patterns.image_source: flymenfishingcompany.com — manufacturer product photo, white background, correct pattern

regional_usage.notes: A large, durable brush-style fly designed for GT worldwide, including Hawaiian ulua; tied in black or dark colors for high contrast in the Pacific surf zone.

Library universal (existing #11); oversized brush-fly construction in 6/0–8/0 required for the large, aggressive GTs around PNG reef systems; Fly Odyssey PNG describes Portlock Reef GTs as requiring the heaviest GT tackle and largest flies.
Library universal (existing #11); extra-large brush fly in 6/0–8/0 for the largest GTs and dogtooth tuna encountered in Raja Ampat's deep passes and offshore seamount systems.

patterns.name: Bird Dog (Captain Sullivan's)
patterns.description: Captain Jason Sullivan's searching baitfish pattern built with white and red EP Ze-Brush fibers for a full, translucent profile. Designed for blind-casting Everglades backcountry when sight-fishing conditions fail. The pulsing synthetic fibers breathe on the pause, triggering snook and redfish holding in low-visibility tannin-stained channels and mangrove edges.
patterns.image_source: Orvis News editorial article — '3 Guide-Tested Patterns for Everglades National Park'

regional_usage.notes: Orvis News-documented guide pattern by Capt. Jason Sullivan (2018 Endorsed Saltwater Guide); a white/red EP Ze-Brush baitfish used as a searching pattern in the Everglades when sight-fishing isn't possible.

patterns.name: Black & Purple Tarpon Toad
patterns.description: A colour-specific variant of the Tarpon Toad, substituting black and purple materials throughout for maximum silhouette contrast in Gabon's dark, turbid beach surf. The wide, palmered body pushes water and gives a breathing action on the strip. Universally cited in Sette Cama trip reports as the most-effective tarpon colour in off-coloured Atlantic surf.
patterns.image_source: bigtimeflies.com — Tarpon Toad Purple/Black product photo

regional_usage.notes: The go-to colour variant of the Tarpon Toad for Gabon beach fishing; black and purple colouration is the most-referenced combination in all Sette Cama trip reports for tarpon in dark/turbid surf. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Tarpon Toad' — Gabon colour variant only.

patterns.name: Black 'n' Barred
patterns.description: Black variant of Australia's Pink Thing with barred grizzly hackle saddles over a white belly creating high-contrast fright stripes. Documented by Saltwater Flyrodders Australia as one of Australia's most popular multi-species tropical flies. Particularly effective in tannin-stained water for barramundi, GT, and queenfish across northern Australia and the Gulf of Carpentaria.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; this Australian regional variant is not commercially catalogued

regional_usage.notes: Black variant of the Pink Thing with barred grizzly hackle fright stripes, documented by Saltwater Flyrodders Australia as one of Australia's most popular multi-species tropical flies; effective on trevally and queenfish across all Northern Australian saltwater environments.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Black version of the Pink Thing with barred-grizzly fright stripes; documented by Saltwater Flyrodders Australia (Stephen Bradbury, Perth) as one of Australia's most popular tropical multi-species flies; particularly effective in dirty or tannin-stained water.

patterns.name: Black Brush Fly
patterns.description: All-black palmered brush-fiber streamer regarded by Alphonse Fishing Co. guides as the single most productive Seychelles GT fly ever. Tied large on heavy hooks with optional purple or olive accent fibers. Two-handed fast strip through the surf zone; the bulk and dark silhouette trigger aggressive GT charges on Cosmoledo and Alphonse atolls.
patterns.image_source: Superflies.com professional GT fly shop product shot, clean background

regional_usage.notes: Described by Alphonse Fishing Co. guides as the single fly that has taken more Seychelles GTs than any other; combinations with purple, red, or olive accents are particularly effective on Cosmoledo and Alphonse.
All-black brush fly for low-light dawn/dusk GT hunting on the Nubian reef edges and surf zones; silhouette visibility is key when GTs patrol in poor light.
All-black craft-fur brush on 8/0 hook for dawn/dusk sessions along the rocky Hallaniyat shoreline; the dark silhouette is visible even in white-water surf where Oman's biggest GTs hunt.
Black silhouette brush fly for early-morning and cloudy-day GT sessions along Bazaruto's deeper channel edges where large fish patrol in low-light conditions.

Library universal (existing #13); described by Brett Wolf in FlyLife as the most reliable fly for Ningaloo Reef GT around coral and mangroves, and the fly used on the 80–90 lb GT described in the article.

Library universal (existing #13); black-on-black brush flies are consistently rated by Indo-Pacific GT guides for low-light and early-morning conditions; particularly effective on the reef edges and passes of the Bismarck Archipelago.

Library universal (existing #13); black is universally noted by Indo-Pacific GT guides as the most productive color in any depth or light condition; Raja Ampat's varied micro-environments from mangroves to open ocean passages all see GTs responding to this fly.

patterns.name: Black Death
patterns.description: Stu Apte's all-black tarpon streamer, a Florida Keys classic tied with black saddle hackle and a hint of purple. The dark, high-contrast silhouette excels in low-light conditions, overcast days, and in the deeper, darker channels of the Lower Keys. Presented on a slow strip-pause retrieve to laid-up or rolling tarpon; also effective for Belize and Cuba tarpon.
patterns.image_source: BigTime Flies shop — Black Death tarpon fly, clean square product photo

regional_usage.notes: Designed by Keys guide legend Stu Apte; the all-black pattern with purple hackle is especially deadly for Keys tarpon in low-light conditions, overcast days, and in the darker water of the lower channels.
Dark, heavily dressed tarpon streamer with a high-contrast silhouette; listed by El Pescador and Turneffe Flats for both baby tarpon in canals and migratory fish.
Fishmaster lists Black Death as a primary Cuba tarpon pattern for Jardines de la Reina; its dark silhouette is effective for the large JDR tarpon in clear-water flats conditions.

Explicitly named for Los Roques tarpon by French angler/writer Jean-Baptiste Vidal in a 2025 Fishing.news article, specifically for low-light conditions and when tarpon are feeding on fish guts discarded by local fishermen — a documented feeding behaviour unique to the Gran Roque harbour area.
Classic black-and-purple tarpon/snook streamer; recommended by Xcalak and Sian Ka'an guides for baby tarpon in low-light and tannic mangrove water.

High-contrast dark tarpon streamer confirmed by fishcostarica.com and Flymen guides as a top pattern for Costa Rica's tannin-stained jungle rivers where a bold silhouette is critical for triggering strikes.
High-contrast dark tarpon streamer recommended by Tapam Lodge guides for Nicaragua's turbid river and lagoon systems where silhouette is more important than color detail.

Named explicitly in the Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras tarpon fly list alongside Purple Death and Cockroach for the resident and migratory tarpon in the channels and river mouths around Guanaja and the Mosquitia coast.

Dark silhouette tarpon streamer effective in Bocas del Toro's turbid mixing zones during peak September–October tarpon season when hundreds of rolling fish congregate near the Changuinola and Sixaola river mouths.
Standard dark tarpon streamer used for flats and channel tarpon at Cayo Cruz; its dark silhouette is highly visible in the clear blue water of Cuba's northern coast fisheries.
Black-and-red tarpon fly that performs in Tampa Bay's variable light conditions and darker water around passes during the May–June migration — already in library.

patterns.name: Black Magic
patterns.description: A dark-toned shrimp or attractor pattern tied in black, dark earth, and root beer tones for redfish and speckled trout. Its dark silhouette is most effective in tannin-stained Louisiana marsh water and on Texas flats under low-light conditions when predators are feeding with reduced wariness. Fish slow with minimal movement near bottom structure.
patterns.image_source: Etsy seller product photo of black saltwater shrimp/redfish fly on white background

regional_usage.notes: A dark-colored shrimp or attractor pattern tied in black or dark earth tones; proven effective in the chocolate-brown, tannin-stained waters of Louisiana's interior marsh on overcast days.
Dark attractor shrimp patterns in black and root beer are particularly effective on the Laguna under low-light conditions and on overcast days when redfish feed with reduced wariness.

patterns.name: Blue/White Pacific Billfish Streamer
patterns.description: A generic class of large blue-and-white tube fly tied in the round on a 6/0–8/0 hook, imitating the mackerel and flying fish that Pacific billfish target. The blue-over-white color scheme is second only to pink/white in Costa Rica, particularly effective under overcast skies and low-light conditions. Teased to the boat's wake before presenting the fly.
patterns.image_source: etsy.com — representative blue/white billfish tube fly; generic class pattern, no single originator

regional_usage.notes: Second most popular billfish color scheme after pink/white; particularly effective in cloudy conditions and early/late in the day when light penetration is lower.

patterns.name: Bonefish Bitters
patterns.description: Craig Mathews' 1980s crab-shrimp hybrid with a low-riding, wide-bodied profile, rubber legs, and bead-chain eyes that keep the hook point riding up. Tied in tan, olive, and pink to match Caribbean flats forage. Sinks slowly into grass and can be twitched in place for tailing bonefish. Also effective on permit.
patterns.image_source: Orvis product photo, clean white background, clear side profile of Bonefish Bitters

regional_usage.notes: Originally named Pop's Bonefish Bitters after a Belizean guide; its epoxy/UV-resin crab-shrimp hybrid profile with tinted bead-chain eyes is a versatile Caribbean-wide bonefish pattern that carries over well to Andros flats.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Getaway Fly Fishing's Acklins guide recommends 'Puffs' — the same style as Bitters — for the out islands' sandflats; the tan Bitters profile matches the pale coloration that Abaco guides say is essential for Marls fishing.

Amber and natural variants appear in the Fulling Mill Los Roques selection; the lightly weighted, rubber-legged silhouette is highly effective on the pancake flats where bones are feeding in very shallow water with little current.
Amber and tan Bitters is universally recommended for Bahamas clear-water flats and is an excellent neutral-profile option when fish are selective.
Neutral amber profile in sizes #4-#8 works across T&C's varied bottom substrates; recommended as a standard Bahamas-style flat fly by multiple sources.
Proven neutral profile for pressured flats fish; amber version mimics the common snapping shrimp found on Cayman grass flats.
Soft-hackle neutral-profile shrimp excellent for cautious Bonaire bones on clear, calm lagoon flats; amber body mimics common Caribbean mantis shrimp coloration.
Top choice for Yucatan bones in sizes #6-#8 per Xcalak-area guides; a touch of orange or pink hotspot in the tan version performs especially well.

A standard flats bonefish pattern used in Cuba for Cayo Cruz's extensive wadeable white-sand flats; the Bitters' slow sink rate and crab-like legs work well on the hard-packed sand and mottled bottom where bonefish tail in 1–2 ft.

patterns.name: Bonefish Scampi
patterns.description: Slim mantis-shrimp silhouette tied with sparse craft fur or rabbit, banded rubber legs, and bead-chain eyes. Sinks steadily without splash — ideal for Christmas Island's deeper channels and faster tidal water where bonefish feed aggressively. Fish with a short, sharp strip retrieve. Henry Cowen's recipe is the most widely tied version.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com side-profile product shot, clean background

regional_usage.notes: Slim mantis-shrimp style imitation recommended alongside the Christmas Island Special by multiple guides; effective in deeper channels and faster water where bonefish are more aggressive.

patterns.name: Bonefish Special
patterns.description: A generic attractor-shrimp imitation tied in sand/light-brown on hooks #4–#6, effective across varied bonefish flats including the mixed sand and grass bottom of Jardines de la Reina. Sparse profile and weighted eyes produce a quick, quiet sink. Fished on a short, slow strip with pauses; the neutral coloration covers most flat types when a more specific imitation isn't required.
patterns.image_source: Bear's Den Fly Shop — Bonefish Special product page

regional_usage.notes: Listed by Fishmaster as a recommended bonefish pattern for JDR in sand/light-brown on hooks #4–#6; a generic attractor shrimp useful on the varied JDR bonefish flats.

patterns.name: Bonefish Toad
patterns.description: A lightweight, unweighted flats pattern with a polypropylene yarn body and rubber legs designed to imitate small crustaceans and worms on mixed sand and grass bottoms. Its neutral buoyancy and soft splash entry make it ideal for skittish fish in shallow Biscayne Bay and Everglades flats. Fish on a dead-drift or minimal strip retrieve.
patterns.image_source: FlyFishBonehead dedicated Bonefish Toad page — clear close-up photo of the tied fly

regional_usage.notes: Capt. Raul Montoro specifically recommends 'bonefish toads' for Biscayne Bay bonefish; his chartreuse-and-tan version with polypropylene yarn body is a guide-developed pattern optimized for the bay's light conditions and mixed bottoms.

patterns.name: Borski Slider
patterns.description: Tim Borski's wide-bodied, foam-head slider rides hook-point-up on a weedless rig. The bulky deer-hair or foam collar pushes water while the marabou tail breathes on the pause. An unweighted, soft-landing presentation ideal for shallow turtle-grass flats and redfish potholes. Created in the Florida Keys, now used from Andros to the Laguna Madre.
patterns.image_source: Orvis product photo, white background, clean side profile of Borski Bonefish Slider

regional_usage.notes: Tim Borski's compact slider adapted for redfish; its weed-resistant profile and soft entry allow it to be worked through Louisiana's floating vegetation without fouling. Tim Borski's wide-body slider rides hook-point-up through Louisiana's matted grass and slides enticingly into potholes where redfish ambush prey.

Adapted directly from a bonefish pattern to Texas redfish, this compact slider crosses easily across the Laguna's hyper-saline flats, which share bonefish-flat characteristics of clarity and shallow depth. Tim Borski's wide-bodied slider glides through the Laguna's sparse Halodule grass without fouling, presenting a broadside shrimp silhouette to sight-fished redfish and large trout.
Designed by Florida Keys-based artist and tier Tim Borski; its weedless, sliding presentation is ideal for the turtle-grass edges and mangrove marl creeks throughout Andros's vast flat system.
Created by Keys-based artist Tim Borski; the Borski Slider was designed specifically for Keys and South Florida flats conditions and has become one of the best-known Florida Keys bonefish patterns.
Tim Borski created this pattern for Florida flats fishing; its weedless design is suited to the grassy Biscayne Bay bonefish flats and the redfish habitat in the Everglades mangrove edges.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Foam-head unweighted slider pattern; Palometa Club references 'sliders' as part of the bonefish selection for flats where a slow-sinking or surface-swimming presentation is preferred.

The neutral-density deer hair head and translucent shrimp body make the Slider highly effective for spooky bonefish on the clear, flat-calm pancake flats; also productive in the mangrove lagoons for snook that hold in shallow water.
Deerhair head with rabbit strip tail creates a sliding action through the water; confirmed effective for both bonefish and the jack crevalle encountered on Bonaire flats.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Weedless, slow-sinking slider designed for shallow clear-water reds and snook in the southern IRL; effective across the full SE inshore spectrum — already in library.
Weedless slider that can be skated into spartina roots and retrieved through tailing fish — widely used by Lowcountry guides when reds are rooting for fiddlers in heavy grass — already in library.
Weedless subsurface slider for navigating dense spartina grass on GA flood-tide flats; works equally well poled through creeks at low tide — already in library.
Weedless slider works throughout the Pine Island Sound and Matlacha backcountry where redfish and snook share shallow grass-flat habitat — already in library.

patterns.name: Borski's Orange Butt Tarpon
patterns.description: Tim Borski's Florida Keys tarpon streamer with a distinctive orange butt and palmered hackle collar over a rabbit or craft-fur body. Fished subsurface on a floating or intermediate line with a slow, steady strip through mangrove lagoons and backcountry channels. Color contrast and pulsing hackle action draw strikes from tarpon holding tight to structure.
patterns.image_source: RiverBum.com large side-profile product image on white background

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Pesca Maya explicitly lists 'Borski's Orange Butt Tarpon' as a recommended tarpon pattern for the backcountry and mangrove lagoons of Ascension Bay.

patterns.name: Brewer's Amber Shrimp
patterns.description: Classic Bahamian shrimp imitation in amber and tan with a wood-duck tail that matches the mangrove-edge shrimp bonefish key on in tidal cuts and flat edges. A long-standing must-have pattern for Bahamian flats including Bimini, listed by Angler Adventures as a Bahamas essential. Bead-chain eyes give controlled sink rate for skinny water.
patterns.image_source: No specific Brewer's Amber Shrimp image found in searched fly shop databases or editorial sources

regional_usage.notes: Classic Bahamas shrimp in amber/tan with wood-duck tail; listed by Angler Adventures as a must-have pattern for Bahamian flats including Bimini — amber colorway matches mangrove-edge shrimp.

patterns.name: Brown Special Crab
patterns.description: A local-style brown crab imitation in hook sizes #2–#8, built to match the dark crabs of the Bay Islands' turtle-grass and coral flats. Photographed directly in a Fly Fishing Caribe Guanaja Honduras fly box with the caption 'Crab Fly Brown Special Crab.' Presented on a dead-drift or slow strip to permit tailing on the Honduras Mosquitia flats.
patterns.image_source: No specific named-pattern photo found; search returned generic permit crab patterns only

regional_usage.notes: Photographed directly in Fly Fishing Caribe's Guanaja Honduras fly box with a caption 'Crab Fly Brown Special Crab #2, 4, 6, 8'; a local-style brown crab imitation effective on the turtle-grass and coral flats of the Bay Islands.

patterns.name: Brush Popper
patterns.description: A hard-foam-bodied surface popper with a cupped face and brush-style collar, designed for aggressive saltwater species. Stripped fast along Baja California beach breaks, the popping face displaces water with an audible splash that imitates panicked baitfish — the trigger that draws roosterfish and jack crevalle from the wave zone to the surface for explosive strikes.
patterns.image_source: Orvis product photo — Mylar Popper saltwater fly, clean white background (closest generic saltwater popper available)

regional_usage.notes: A hard-foam-bodied popper with a cupped face stripped aggressively along Baja's beach breaks; the popping sound and spray imitate fleeing baitfish and draw aggressive surface strikes from roosterfish patrolling just beyond the wave zone.

patterns.name: Bunny Anchovy
patterns.description: Rabbit-strip anchovy imitation on 1/0–3/0 in white/olive with a pulsing zonker tail replicating schooling baitfish action. Used around Honduras Mosquitia river mouths for tarpon and jack crevalle. Photographed in the Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras fly box as 'Wet Fly Bunny Anchovy'; supple rabbit fur maintains action at low strip speed.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; Honduras regional pattern not commercially sold

regional_usage.notes: Photographed in the Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras fly box image gallery as 'Wet Fly Bunny Anchovy #1, 2, 1/0, 2/0, 3/0'; a rabbit-strip anchovy imitation used for tarpon and jacks around the Mosquitia river mouths and mangrove edges.

patterns.name: Bunny Bone
patterns.description: An unweighted bonefish shrimp pattern built with a crosscut rabbit fur body that undulates naturally with each twitch of the line. Its minimal splash entry and soft landing are essential for presenting to tailing fish in ultra-skinny Andros and Bahamian out-island water. Fish with a slow, barely-there strip on big hard-sand flats.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com dedicated Bunny Bone product page — clean side profile photo

regional_usage.notes: Unweighted rabbit-fur pattern recommended for tailing fish in skinny Andros water; its soft landing and natural movement make it ideal for the super-shallow presentations required on large, exposed Andros sand flats.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: An unweighted rabbit-fur fly for tailing and ultra-shallow fish; recommended by Angler Adventures for any Bahamian out-island situation requiring soft presentations and minimal splash.
Rabbit-fur skinny-water fly recommended by Angler Adventures for tailing fish in 6-18 inches; the soft landing is essential in calm Bimini Sound conditions.

patterns.name: Cam Sigler Big Game Tube Fly (Tandem Rigged)
patterns.description: The definitive Pacific billfish tube fly by Cam Sigler, first tied in the 1990s. Two large tubes slid on a single leader create a 9-inch profile in pink/white — the dominant color on boats out of Quepos and Los Sueños. Bucktail and hackle tied in the round give 360° water movement. Teased to the wake before presenting under the rod tip.
patterns.image_source: royaltreatmentflyfishing.com — fly shop commercial product photo of actual Cam Sigler Big Game Tube Flies

regional_usage.notes: The defining Pacific billfish tube fly — two big-game tubes slid together on a single leader creating a 9-inch profile; pink/white is the overwhelming favorite color scheme and is standard on boats out of Quepos and Los Sueños.

patterns.name: Cam Sigler Mega Marlin Tube Fly
patterns.description: Cam Sigler's extended-profile marlin fly, developed in the 2000s for large-boat billfish operations. Tied in the round on a heavy 2¾-inch tube with dual hackle sets and large doll eyes, reaching 10.5–12 inches in length. Designed to track straight and push significant water in rough-sea conditions off Golfito and Drake Bay when targeting blue and black marlin.
patterns.image_source: camsigler.com — originator's own website, correctly labeled Mega Marlin fly

regional_usage.notes: A 10.5-12 inch tube fly tied in the round on a heavy 2¾-inch tube with dual hackle sets and doll eyes, designed for large-boat wakes and rough-sea marlin fishing from Golfito and Drake Bay.

patterns.name: Candy — Pelagic
patterns.description: Match-the-hatch unweighted baitfish imitation designed by Stephen Chatterton (fishonfly.com.au) to replicate the slim schooling baitfish — hardyheads, herrings, anchovies — that pelagics key on. Sparse synthetic-fiber body provides translucency and flash. Stripped fast across breaking schools of queenfish, longtail tuna, and Spanish mackerel off Cape York and the Gulf of Carpentaria.
patterns.image_source: fishonfly.com.au — Stephen Chatterton's own fly tying website, article titled 'Candy – pelagic'

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Match-the-hatch unweighted baitfish fly for Australian pelagics documented by Stephen Chatterton (fishonfly.com.au) specifically for queenfish and tuna targeting baitfish schools; a slim schooling-baitfish imitation effective on Cape York queenfish.

patterns.name: Casa Blanca Crab (Cuban)
patterns.description: A crab imitation developed in the Casa Blanca flat area of Cuba, tied with local color variations for the turtle-grass and coral-sand flats of Jardines de la Reina. Distinct from the Yucatan-origin Casa Blanca Raghead. Presented with a weighted hook for rapid descent to permit feeding depth; fished with minimal movement once settled near the bottom.
patterns.image_source: fishtalesflyshop.com — fly shop commercial product photo of Casa Blanca Crab; note this is a generic variant, not verified as the specific Cuban version

regional_usage.notes: A crab imitation developed at the Casa Blanca lodge area in Cuba, distinct from the Yucatan-origin Casa Blanca Raghead already in the library; tied with local color variations for the turtle-grass and coral-sand flats of Jardines de la Reina.

patterns.name: Casa Blanca Raghead
patterns.description: A Rainy's-produced crab fly developed at Casa Blanca Lodge on Ascension Bay. Stacked deer-hair legs and a buoyant raghead body land softly and sink slowly over the turtle-grass and sand flats of the Yucatán. Tan and olive colorways dominate; fished dead-drift or with minimal twitches in front of tailing permit.
patterns.image_source: Red's Fly Shop product photo — Casa Blanca Raghead Crab by Rainy's, clean side profile

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Lodge-developed variant of the Raghead Crab tied specifically for the conditions at Casa Blanca Lodge on Ascension Bay; the Palometa Club's outfitter carries it as a 'secret weapon' only available through lodge channels.

patterns.name: Cayman Sleek
patterns.description: Developed after Cayman bonefish refused standard Crazy Charlies and Gotchas, the Cayman Sleek features a pearl Mylar body, golden bead-chain eyes, brown-and-tan craft-fur tail, and rubber legs. The slim, shrimp-like silhouette sinks quickly on Cayman's shallow grass flats. Effective across the full size range of Grand Cayman bonefish on a slow-twitch strip.
patterns.image_source: No verifiable photo found for this specific named pattern

regional_usage.notes: Pearl mylar body, golden bead-chain eyes, brown/tan craft-fur tail, rubber legs; developed specifically after Cayman bonefish refused standard Gotchas and Crazy Charlies — effective on both small and large fish across size range.

patterns.name: CF Baitfish
patterns.description: A simple, lightweight craft-fur baitfish pattern tied in two or three layers of stacked fur over a hook with optional flash. Extremely castable and versatile. The craft fur breathes naturally on the retrieve, imitating mullet, sardines, and glass minnows. Effective on redfish and trout inshore, and on roosterfish and dorado along Baja beaches.
patterns.image_source: The Fly Fishers shop product photo of CF Baitfish fly on plain background

regional_usage.notes: Rainy's craft-fur baitfish pattern in mullet and chartreuse-white imitates the numerous schooling baitfish species along Texas's passes and nearshore jetty systems.
Rainy's craft-fur baitfish in mullet and sardine colors is a reliable Baja beach pattern; its lightweight construction reduces casting fatigue on long, repetitive beach-walking sessions for roosters.

patterns.name: Chatto's Baitfish
patterns.description: Reef-minnow baitfish developed by Central Queensland tier Stephen Chatterton. Dumbbell eyes on 2/0–4/0 orient it hook-point up through Cape York mangrove structure. Craft fur or EP fibers in white/olive represent tropical inshore baitfish. Full recipe documented at fishonfly.com.au; effective on barramundi, GT, and mangrove jack in the Gulf of Carpentaria.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; regional Queensland tier pattern with limited online presence

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Reef-minnow style dumbbell-eye baitfish developed by Central Queensland tier Stephen Chatterton for tropical inshore species; swims hook-point up to reduce snags around Cape York structure; documented with full recipe on fishonfly.com.au.

patterns.name: Chernobyl Crab
patterns.description: Foam-bodied, rubber-legged crab that floats or slow-sinks, imitating small blue and stone crabs that redfish and drum crush on shell flats. Dense rubber-leg array provides realistic movement. Present with a soft landing on tailing fish and let the legs flutter without stripping. Highly effective on Louisiana marsh edges and Texas Laguna Madre.
patterns.image_source: Jackson Hole Fly Company overhead product shot on neutral background

regional_usage.notes: A foam-bodied, rubber-legged crab that floats or suspends in the water column; widely used along Louisiana's shell flats and marsh edges where crab-feeding redfish are common.

A foam crab with rubber legs that suspends in the water column; its versatility in representing the varied crab species of the Laguna's sandy and grass flats earns it a permanent place in Texas guide boxes.

patterns.name: Chicone's Crusher Leg Gotcha
patterns.description: Drew Chicone's rubber-legged variant of the classic Gotcha, from his 'Bonefish Flies Abaco' series. Realistic jointed legs tied with Chicone's Crusher Leg material add micro-movement that sells the shrimp imitation to pressured, educated Abaco bonefish. Bead-chain eyes for a quiet entry; fished with short strips on the white sand and turtle-grass flats of the Abaco Marls.
patterns.image_source: SaltyFlyTying.com — Chicone's Crusher Legs fly finished product, clean square background

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: One of ten patterns in the verified 'Bonefish Flies Abaco' ebook by Drew Chicone; a rubber-legged Gotcha variant tuned for Abaco's spooky fish that see a lot of pressure from knowledgeable anglers.

patterns.name: Chicone's Disco Shrimp
patterns.description: Topwater shrimp attractor with a concave gurgler-style disc face and built-in rattle that mimics a snapping, fleeing shrimp. Created by Drew Chicone for the Indian River Lagoon backcountry, it pushes a noisy wake on the surface. Standard Mosquito Lagoon attractor for tailing redfish, snook, and juvenile tarpon; fished with short, erratic strips to trigger violent surface eats.
patterns.image_source: Salt Fly Pro (saltflypro.com) — Umpqua Disco Shrimp Chicone Tan product listing

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Topwater shrimp with a gurgler-style disc face and built-in rattle mimicking a snapping fleeing shrimp; a Space Coast / IRL backcountry staple recommended by Capt. Frank Catino for Mosquito Lagoon.

patterns.name: Chicone's Optical Illusion
patterns.description: Drew Chicone's subtle shrimp pattern developed specifically for hard-fished Abaco bonefish. Built with fine synthetic fibers and minimal bulk, its sparse profile and translucent triggers appeal to pressure-wise fish that reject standard patterns. Presented on a long leader with a light tippet on clear hard-sand Abaco flats; documented in Chicone's Bonefish Flies Abaco ebook.
patterns.image_source: SaltyFlyTying blog — Drew Chicone fly tying photo (Chicone pattern, not confirmed as Optical Illusion specifically)

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Documented Abaco-specific pattern from the 'Bonefish Flies Abaco' ebook; designed by Drew Chicone to fool hard-fished Abaco bonefish with subtle triggers that standard patterns lack.

patterns.name: Chili Pepper
patterns.description: Developed by Christmas Island guide Moana Koffe for full-moon bonefish gatherings on Paris Flat. Features a red-hot-colored body with bead-chain or lead eyes and sparse fiber or calf-tail wing. Sinks quickly to intercept feeding bones. Fished with short strips along the bottom on sand flats; the name references its signature color.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com — Moana's Chili Pepper bonefish fly, side profile with bead-chain eyes

regional_usage.notes: Developed by legendary Kiritimati guide Moana Koffe specifically for bonefish gathering on Paris Flat during full-moon spawning; remains a guide-preferred pattern on the island.

patterns.name: Christmas Island Special
patterns.description: Randall Kaufmann's shrimp-baitfish attractor, tied with a palmered body, bead-chain eyes, and a wing of calf tail or craft fur over a sparse body in orange, pink, or tan. Named for Kiritimati's legendary flats where local guides consider it the top pattern. Fished in sizes 4–8 with a slow strip-pause cadence to imitate fleeing mantis shrimp.
patterns.image_source: Alaska Fly Fishing Goods product photo, orange Christmas Island Special on plain background

regional_usage.notes: A small-profile, quiet-entry gold/orange shrimp pattern recommended by Deep Water Cay (Grand Bahama) for spooky Bahamian bonefish; its lack of splash makes it useful for tailing fish on shallow Andros sand.
Bright-eyed shrimp attractor listed by El Pescador in pink/tan and orange/tan for lead-eye and bead-chain presentations on Belize's varied flats depths.
Named after and developed for the legendary flats of Kiritimati, this weighted shrimp-baitfish hybrid is the single most-recommended pattern by local guides in multiple sizes (4, 6, 8) and colors.
A Pacific-origin pattern well-matched to Hawaiian conditions; the orange/pink color scheme works for winter bonefish in Hawaii, and the pattern is referenced in Hawaii fly shop recommendations.

Orange and pink variants appear directly in the Fulling Mill Los Roques fly selection; a proven attractor for feeding bonefish in gin-clear Caribbean water, particularly effective on overcast days when the flash element draws attention.
Listed by Christmas Island guides as a top trigger shrimp and confirmed effective on Nubian bonefish; the tan/pink variant works the sandy-bottom flats between coral heads.
Recommended by Deep Water Cay guides (Orvis article) for quiet entry on spooky fish; gold or orange colorway works year-round on Bahamian sand.
Small profile with quiet water entry makes it excellent for the calm, clear conditions on Provo flats and Bottle Creek wading areas.
Quiet entry, small profile, and versatile gold/orange colorway suit the calm Bonaire lagoon conditions; easy to tie for DIY fly tyers preparing for the trip.
Gold and orange variants are recommended for Mexican Yucatan bonefish in shallow, calm conditions; the unweighted or plastic-eye version lands softly on spooky flats.

Bonefish are present on some Solomon Islands flats (notably around Marovo Lagoon perimeter flats) though not a primary target; the Christmas Island Special in orange/pearl covers the basic bonefish need. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Christmas Island Special'.

patterns.name: Clouser Deep Minnow
patterns.description: Bob Clouser's dumbbell-eyed bucktail streamer, developed mid-1980s, fishes hook-point-up to reduce snags. Lead or brass eyes drive a darting jig action on the retrieve. Tied in tan/white for bonefish and flats species; chartreuse/white for stripers, jacks, and redfish. Cast, count down, then strip-strip-pause. Effective in virtually every saltwater environment worldwide.
patterns.image_source: Clouser's own fly fishing shop — Clouser Minnow for Bonefish, source shop

regional_usage.notes: Tan-and-white Clouser is listed by Angler Adventures as one of the two most effective Bahamas bonefish flies; the inverted hook and dumbbell eyes get it deep in the channels of Andros's extensive tidal creek system.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: A Bahamas-wide workhorse; on Acklins and Long Island the tan-and-white Clouser is fished for bonefish in deeper water and switched to heavy-wire hooks with a stinger for barracuda and jacks.
A Keys guide staple across multiple species; used in tan-white for Keys bonefish and in white-chartreuse with heavy eyes for the jack crevalle and barracuda that patrol the same flats as tarpon.

A universal South Florida staple; guide sources (Everglades Fly Fishing Charters) list the Clouser for Everglades snook in white-chartreuse and tan configurations; the weight gets it down in the deeper Biscayne Bay flats.

The dumbbell-eyed Clouser is the single most important fly for Pamlico Sound red drum; in chartreuse/white or tan/orange it imitates the crabs, shrimp, and minnows that bull redfish push against shoals in September. A tan-over-orange or chartreuse-over-white Clouser in size 2–1/0 is the most-used pattern for wade-fishing sight-cast red drum on Pamlico Sound flats, sinking quickly to the fish's feeding zone.
Weighted dumbbell-eye baitfish pattern listed by El Pescador for jacks, snook, and secondary bonefish use in Belize's varied depths.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Palometa Club and Pesca Maya both list red/white Clousers and chartreuse/white for snook; jack crevalle are opportunistic and attack Clousers stripped fast along mangrove edges.
Standard baitfish pattern for deeper-water species at JDR; its weighted dumbbell eyes make it effective for jacks, cubera snapper, and bonefish in the deeper channels around the cays.
Larger baitfish-profile Clouser variants in 1/0–4/0 are effective for trevally species cruising the reef edges and channel drop-offs around Christmas Island.
The dumbbell-eyed Clouser digs deep in Louisiana's marsh channels and tidal cuts, imitating the abundant mud minnows and small baitfish that redfish pursue.
The Clouser Minnow remains a versatile Texas-coast workhorse, imitating the mullet, croakers, and silversides across the full spectrum of Gulf flats from the Laguna to the Rockport bay systems.
The Clouser in olive-white or chartreuse-white is a standard Baja inshore pattern for jacks, ladyfish, and sierra mackerel over rocky structure and reefs near La Paz and East Cape.
A universal staple used in Hawaii for GT, omilu, and papio targeting rocky drop-offs; the dumbbell eyes drive quick sinking on steep-edged Hawaiian flats.

Crocodile Bay Resort explicitly lists Clousers as one of their primary recommended flies; weighted dumbbell eyes get the fly down quickly in the deep-dropping Golfo Dulce waters and work for all Costa Rica inshore species.

Grey-over-white in size 6 is specifically recommended by trip report anglers for imitating the sardina forage on Gran Roque beaches; also the go-to for jacks and barracuda around the reef edges and boat harbours.
Heavy dumbbell eyes sink the Clouser below baitballs to reach the trevally species that feed sub-surface; chartreuse-white and blue-white proven across Indian Ocean trevally fisheries.

FishBazaruto.com explicitly recommends heavily-weighted Clousers in chartreuse, white, and dark for dredging over deep offshore pinnacles (6–40 m), which is the primary fly-fishing method for offshore Bazaruto species.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Library universal (existing #35); swoffa.com lists Clousers among essential Australian barramundi fly patterns; synthetic Clouser variants (Stephen Chatterton's Clouser Synthetic MKII) are documented for Gulf pelagics including queenfish and GT.

Library universal (existing #35); dumbbell-weighted Clousers in 2/0–4/0 are documented by PNG freshwater guides for Niugini black bass in deeper river pools and are a staple carry on PNG expeditions for both salt and freshwater targets.
Library universal (existing #35); dumbbell-eye Clousers in 2/0–4/0 produce on Indonesian snapper, mangrove jack, and smaller GT that hold in deeper current seams around Raja Ampat's reef structures.
Tan-and-white Clouser with lead eyes is the go-to deep-water pattern when Bimini bones hold in 3-5 ft channels adjacent to the flats.
Lead-eye Clouser in tan/white handles the deeper Caicos Bank channels where large bonefish cruise; also takes barracuda and jacks incidentally.
Lead-eye Fox-and-Bunny Clouser variant is the Fish-Bones go-to for deeper water cruising bones; also targets Cayman tarpon and cuda in channels.
Lead-eye Clouser covers deeper Lac Bay edges and channel margins; also the most versatile choice for barracuda and jacks frequently encountered by wading anglers.

Weighted dumbbell-eye baitfish for the secondary species at Barra del Colorado; Silver King Lodge guides use it for jacks, snook, and cubera snapper when non-tarpon species are being targeted in the same river systems.

Weighted dumbbell-eye baitfish for snook and jacks that are secondary catches during Nicaragua tarpon sessions; gets down quickly in the deep river channels and works on the retrieve with a jigging action.

Listed by Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras in sizes #2–#8 for bonefish and as a multi-species pattern; the weighted dumbbell eyes get the fly into the strike zone for large bonefish and jacks in deeper flat pockets.

Listed twice in Fly Fishing Caribe's Bocas fly selection (both as 'Clouser Minow #4–2/0' and 'Clouser Minnow #2–3/0'); weighted dumbbell gets the fly into the deeper mixing zone below the fresh/saltwater halocline where cubera snapper and jacks hold.

Heavy Clouser in chartreuse/white or red/white for river and lagoon presentations; mangrove jack and spot-tail bass in Solomon river systems eat Clousers stripped near structure. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Clouser Deep Minnow'.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Universal workhorse recommended by every IRL guide for fish tucked on grass edges and in channels; ties chartreuse/white and white/chartreuse for the light-stained IRL water — already in library.
Indispensable subsurface search pattern for SC tidal creek mouths, mud-flat edges, and low-tide channel fish — recommended by Charleston guides alongside crab patterns — already in library.
All-purpose jig-fly for Georgia creek mouths and channel edges where trout and reds stack on outgoing tides; equally effective for jacks in the sound — already in library.
Deep-diving chartreuse Clouser is a workhorse for Tampa Bay passes and bridges where snook stack on current seams during tidal movement — already in library.

patterns.name: Clouser Swimming Nymph / Bendback
patterns.description: Bob Clouser's soft-hackle subsurface nymph adapted into a bendback hook configuration for weedless presentation. In saltwater use along the Outer Banks, the bent hook prevents fouling on Pamlico Sound's dense grass when targeting tailing red drum along flat edges. Moderate sink rate and pulsing hen-hackle legs mimic a shrimp or small baitfish; fished with slow strips near vegetation.
patterns.image_source: Clouser's Fly Shop — Clouser Swimming Nymph, the originator's own shop photo

regional_usage.notes: Weedless bendback-style Clousers are used in the grassy Pamlico Sound shallows where standard hook-point-up Clousers foul on vegetation when working tight to red drum feeding edges.

patterns.name: Cockroach
patterns.description: Norman Duncan's early-1960s Keys tarpon streamer featuring a brown-over-grizzly hackle collar and mixed hackle wing — the defining tarpon fly of the Florida Keys. Its muted natural tones produce reflex strikes from tailing and rolling tarpon in gin-clear water. Swing or slow-strip on intermediate or floating line; the single most widely carried tarpon pattern from the Keys to Cuba.
patterns.image_source: The Fly Shop catalog — clean square product photo of the Cockroach on white background

regional_usage.notes: Norman Duncan's classic tarpon streamer using grizzly and brown hackles is recommended by Andros South lodge for the resident and migratory tarpon found in Andros's creek systems and west-side flats.

Originated by Norman Duncan fishing the Keys in the early 1960s alongside Flip Pallot and Chico Fernandez; the brown/grizzly hackle streamer remains the single most widely used tarpon fly in the Keys and is in every serious guide's box.

A standard for juvenile and resident Everglades tarpon; although Norman Duncan developed it in Miami/upper Keys, it translates directly to the Everglades creek and bay tarpon fishery as the go-to dark streamer.
One of the oldest tarpon standards; grizzly-hackle natural-color streamer listed by El Pescador as a dependable pattern in clear-water conditions for Belizean tarpon.
Classic grizzly-hackle tarpon fly listed by Fishmaster for JDR tarpon; the Cockroach's natural brown-grizzly tones are highly effective in gin-clear Cuban waters.

Classic Caribbean tarpon fly confirmed essential for Los Roques by multiple sources; resident tarpon of 10-80 lb roll in the channels off Gran Roque and around the deeper flats, and this bucktail-and-grizzly saddle pattern remains the most universal tarpon producer in the region.

One of the oldest Atlantic tarpon standards, explicitly cited by Flymen Fishing Company's Costa Rica jungle tarpon guide as a core pattern for Barra del Colorado and the Tortuguero canal system in sizes 4/0–6/0.

Standard Atlantic tarpon streamer used in the clearer side lagoons and channels of the Nicaraguan jungle system; natural grizzly color profile effective when water visibility allows fish to see the fly clearly.

Classic grizzly tarpon streamer listed by Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras for clear-water tarpon encounters; the Cockroach's natural tones are highly effective when Bay Islands tarpon are sight-fished in clean water.

Standard Atlantic tarpon streamer used in clearer water situations around Bocas del Toro; effective when tarpon have moved out of the turbid river mouth zone into the cleaner inshore waters of the archipelago.

Classic tarpon standard effective in the gin-clear flats and channels of Cayo Cruz and Cayo Romano; the natural grizzly tones work well when Cuba's tarpon are sight-cast on shallow flats near the cays.

The classic Atlantic tarpon fly travels well to Gabon; on calm days and clear lagoon water the Cockroach profile is used by Sette Cama guides as a lighter-water alternative to the heavier baitfish patterns. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Cockroach'.
Classic grizzly-and-orange tarpon streamer; Tampa Bay rolling-school tarpon historically eat the Cockroach as reliably as any Keys fly — overlaps with tarpon universal patterns — already in library.

patterns.name: Cowen's Coyote
patterns.description: Henry Cowen's attractor fly from the early 2000s combines a bucktail body with a Colorado-style spinner blade that generates both flash and lateral-line vibration. The blade's sound triggers strikes from dorado, jack crevalle, tuna, and snook in Costa Rica's inshore and mixed offshore water. Fished with variable retrieves — the blade spins on the pause as well as the strip.
patterns.image_source: umpqua.com — commercial manufacturer product photo, white background, correctly labeled Cowen's Coyote

regional_usage.notes: Spinner-blade attractor fly that combines bucktail and a Colorado-style blade to generate both flash and sound vibration; documented to catch snook, tarpon, tuna, and Spanish mackerel — making it a versatile searching pattern for Costa Rica's mixed offshore and inshore species.

patterns.name: Cowen's Magnum Baitfish
patterns.description: Henry Cowen's large synthetic-fiber baitfish matching adult menhaden or herring — the pattern set a striper world tippet record. Layered craft-fur or synthetic fibers over a long-shank hook create a naturally translucent, full-bodied profile. Stripped aggressively for trophy striped bass from Cape Cod to Montauk and for school bluefin near Cape Hatteras.
patterns.image_source: HenryCowenFlyfishing.com — originator's own site, direct photo of Cowen's Baitfish

regional_usage.notes: Cowen's large synthetic menhaden imitation is used for trophy stripers in the winter OBX surf and for school-class bluefin tuna when they push menhaden against Cape Hatteras shoals.

8-inch Icelandic-sheep or Flash-N-Slinky offshore baitfish held a striped bass tippet world record and is used on Costa Rica blue-water trips for dorado and yellowfin tuna feeding on large bait schools; the hot-pink fluorofibre throat is a trigger element.

patterns.name: Craven's Bonefish Junk
patterns.description: Charlie Craven's evolution of the Gotcha adds rubber legs, epoxy-coated bead-chain eyes, and a bright orange hotspot to a tan craft-fur body. Tied on 1/0–2/0, its oversized profile and triggering action suit the large, wary bonefish of Bimini and Turks & Caicos. Fished with sharp short strips, letting it flutter and settle between pulls.
patterns.image_source: charliesflybox.com — Charlie Craven's own fly shop product photo

regional_usage.notes: Evolved from the Gotcha with rubber legs, epoxy eyes, and a bright orange hotspot; large profile (#2-#4) appeals to Bimini's big, adult bones that key on size.
Rubber legs and hot-orange accent trigger large T&C bones; widely recommended for Bahamas-family destinations including T&C flats.

patterns.name: Crazy Charlie
patterns.description: Developed on Andros Island around 1977 by guide Charlie Smith and popularized by Bob Nauheim, the Crazy Charlie was the first bonefish fly to use bead-chain eyes to invert the hook and create a jigging action. Sparse calf-tail wing over a mono-wrapped body. Strip-pause on sandy flats. The universal bonefish standard across the Caribbean, Pacific, and Indian Ocean.
patterns.image_source: Wikipedia commons high-resolution white Crazy Charlie fly on clean background, authoritative reference

regional_usage.notes: Originated on Andros Island's flats by guide Charlie Smith and popularized by Bob Nauheim; the first bonefish fly to use bead-chain eyes, making it ride hook-point-up and giving it a jigging action that Andros bonefish find irresistible.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Getaway Fly Fishing's Acklins guide explicitly lists Crazy Charlies as one of the core patterns for the island's extensive sandflats; the fly's long history on these waters makes it a baseline for the Out Islands.

Foundational Bahamian pattern carried into the Keys bonefish fishery; particularly effective on the shallower, sandy ocean-side flats of the Middle Keys where bonefish forage on similar prey to their Bahamian counterparts.
A standard Biscayne Bay bonefish pattern recommended by guide sources; the bay's bonefish feed on similar glass minnow and shrimp prey that the Charlie was designed to imitate on the Bahamian flats.
Universal bonefish standard; El Pescador and Turneffe Flats both list it as a core bonefish pattern in multiple colors for varying flat depths and bottom types.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Palometa Club lists Charlies as a staple bonefish pattern for Ascension Bay in sizes #6–#8; smaller and lighter versions preferred on Yucatán's wadeable sand-and-grass flats.
Fishmaster lists Crazy Charlie among the core JDR bonefish patterns; works well on Cuba's extensive white-sand flats in sand and light-brown colors.
The archetypal bead-chain bonefish fly works reliably on Christmas Island's sandy flats; guides favor sparse ties to match the clear-water preference of the fish.
A reliable universal bonefish pattern that works across Seychelles atolls; the sparse bead-chain-eye profile suits the clear, skinny-water conditions on Alphonse and Astove sand flats.
A universal must-have endorsed across all Hawaii guide resources; effective stripped quickly as a fast-action attractor for Hawaiian oio.

Pink and tan variants are listed in the Fulling Mill Los Roques selection and confirmed by multiple trip reports; bead-chain or light-dumbbell version in size 6-8 suits the clear, shallow pancake flats where delicate presentation is critical.
Mozambique bonefish in the Bazaruto channels are described as aggressive feeders; the Crazy Charlie in tan or pink provides a highly visible, fast-sinking shrimp that provokes quick takes.
Universal Bahamas staple — bead-chain eye weight and pearl/tan body match Bimini sand-flat shrimp and land softly enough for pressured fish.
Foundational T&C flat fly; bead-chain weight perfectly suited to 2-3 ft flats; pearl and tan variants cover sand and grass bottoms alike.
Foundation pattern used on all three Cayman islands; the Hot-Legs variant is preferred locally, but the standard Charlie remains a reliable fallback on cooperative fish.
Easy to tie and widely available; ideal for DIY anglers self-supplying flies for Bonaire — multiple color and weight variants cover all Lac Bay conditions.
Xcalak and Boca Paila guides consistently recommend Crazy Charlie in tan and pearl for Yucatan bonefish on both sandy and grassy bottoms.

Listed by Fly Fishing Caribe for Honduras as a top bonefish pattern in sizes #2–#8; the Bay Islands' bonefish range to 10 lbs and the Crazy Charlie's flash and silhouette work on both sand and turtle-grass bottoms.
Standard Cuba bonefish shrimp; Cuban Fishing Centers recommends it for bonefish on the shallow sand 'bajos' of Cayo Cruz where the fishery's generally unpressured fish show strong take rates.

patterns.name: Crease Fly
patterns.description: Joe Blados's folded-foam popper designed to imitate peanut bunker for blitzing gamefish off Long Island. Cut from foam sheet, folded over the hook shank, and trimmed to a baitfish silhouette. Strips with a gurgling surface commotion. Generates explosive topwater strikes from false albacore, stripers, and bluefish in fall blitz conditions at Montauk and Cape Cod.
patterns.image_source: Bear's Den Fly Fishing — Umpqua Blados' Crease Fly, clean white background

regional_usage.notes: Folded foam surface popper that creates a commotion and splash; noted in multiple Christmas Island packing lists as a surface option for trevally species on the flats and reef edges.
The Crease Fly's mullet-like surface profile is a top choice at Cape Lookout and Harkers Island during the October false albacore and little tunny blitz, producing explosive surface strikes.
Library pattern (existing #42); documented surface fly for Ningaloo GT and pelagic species; the folded-foam surface disturbance attracts GTs on both Ningaloo and Gulf-side flats.

Library universal (existing #42); folded-foam surface popper documented across Indo-Pacific GT destinations; effective for PNG GTs over reef structure where the splashing action imitates panicking baitfish.

Library universal (existing #42); surface popper documented for Indo-Pacific GT and trevally species; Raja Ampat guides carry surface flies for working mangrove edges and reef passes where GT ambush in shallow water.

The Crease Fly's skipping surface action is particularly suited to queenfish, which are abundant and aggressive in the Solomon Islands lagoons and reef margins; the medium (2/0–3/0) size targets queenfish in the 5–20 lb class. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Crease Fly'.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Foam-and-mylar topwater baitfish pattern that generates explosive surface strikes from snook on IRL shorelines and schooling redfish pushing glass minnows — already in library.
Topwater baitfish/popper widely used by West Florida snook guides for casting into mangrove pockets and beach troughs; Yellow Dog recommends it as a top Florida snook fly — already in library.

patterns.name: Crystal Popper
patterns.description: Bob Popovics' hard-bodied cupped-face popper with a clear translucent body and crystal flash collar, producing a loud surface disruption on the strip. Used in Ascension Bay's back lagoons for snook, juvenile tarpon, and jack crevalle. Fast, aggressive strips with short pauses trigger savage surface strikes from predators hunting shallow mangrove systems.
patterns.image_source: Caddis Fly Shop — Crystal Popper from Solitude Fly Co., product photo transparent background

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Pesca Maya notes Mini Crystal Poppers produce 'savage topwater strikes' in the fall in the back lagoons of Ascension Bay, particularly for snook and juvenile tarpon.
Used by Hawaii saltwater anglers for surface GT and omilu presentations; the hard-body popper creates consistent splash and noise effective in Hawaiian surf and reef passes.

patterns.name: Crystal Schminnow
patterns.description: Capt. Norm Zeigler's shrimp-minnow hybrid tied with an Estaz body and marabou tail. Its slow sink rate and pulsing marabou action imitate small glass minnows and juvenile shrimp in Louisiana marsh passes and Texas ICW dock-light situations. Fish on a floating or intermediate line with a slow strip-pause retrieve; a versatile year-round inshore option.
patterns.image_source: Superflies.com product photo of Norm's Crystal Schminnow — clear side profile on neutral background

regional_usage.notes: Capt. Norm Zeigler's shrimp-minnow hybrid tied with Estaz and marabou; its simple profile and slow sink make it a versatile, year-round option for Louisiana's brackish marsh.
Capt. Norm Zeigler's simple marabou-and-Estaz pattern imitates the glass minnows and juvenile shrimp that concentrate on the Lower Texas Coast near ICW structures and dock lights at night.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Half-shrimp, half-minnow marabou-and-chenille pattern originated at Sanibel but fishes superbly throughout the IRL for snook on structure and seatrout on grass edges — already in library.

The definitive Sanibel fly — half shrimp, half minnow marabou-and-chenille pattern originated for snook in beach troughs and under mangroves on Sanibel Island; Norm Zeigler's signature, catches 60+ species — already in library.

patterns.name: Cuban Mantis Shrimp
patterns.description: A mantis shrimp imitation tied in Cuban color variations — tan-olive over cream — distinct from the Veverka Mantis Shrimp. Used by Jardines de la Reina guides on the open flats for permit and bonefish, and near coral edges for large cubera snapper. The articulated claws and weighted eyes produce a realistic rocking descent that triggers flat-refusing permit.
patterns.image_source: saltwaterflies.com — authoritative fly retailer; shows Veverka Mantis Shrimp, a closely related Cuban mantis pattern; no specific Cuban Mantis Shrimp product photo found

regional_usage.notes: A mantis-shrimp imitation in Cuban color variations (tan-olive over cream) distinct from the Veverka Mantis Shrimp already in the library; popular among Jardines guides targeting both permit on the flats and large snapper around coral edges.

patterns.name: Cubera Diver (Dahlberg Style)
patterns.description: Dahlberg Diver with spun deerhair diving head and heavy zonker-strip tail on 4/0–8/0. Built heavier than standard Caribbean versions for Gabon's surf and estuary currents. Recommended by African Waters guide Ed Truter for Sette Cama cubera snapper on sink-tip to Di5 lines. The collapsing deerhair head creates pronounced dive-and-flash action.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants — Dahlberg Diving Bug (Frog)

regional_usage.notes: Dahlberg Diver with long heavy zonker-strip tail and beefed-up deerhair diving head on 4/0–8/0; African Waters' founding guide Ed Truter specifically recommended this over foam versions for Gabon's cubera snapper, fished on sink-tip to Di5 line. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Dahlberg Diver' — Gabon heavy/oversize variant recommended by Ed Truter.

patterns.name: Cuda Fly
patterns.description: A long tandem-hook needlefish imitation rigged on wire to prevent bite-offs; typically tied in green or blue-over-white with Mylar tubing or synthetic fibers that create an elongated, slender profile. Fished with a near-instant, full-speed strip — barracuda key on fast-fleeing needlefish and will refuse any pattern that hesitates.
patterns.image_source: The Fly Fishers shop — Nightmare Needlefish, closest named-pattern commercial needlefish fly with clean presentation

regional_usage.notes: Long green double-hook tandem wire-rigged needlefish imitation; listed by El Pescador specifically for Belize barracuda to prevent bite-offs and maximize hook-up rate.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Pesca Maya lists the Fly Shop's Cuda Fly with wire trace for the abundant barracuda of Ascension Bay, fished with a very fast strip.

patterns.name: Dahlberg Diver
patterns.description: Larry Dahlberg's deer-hair surface fly with a spun-and-clipped collar that forces the head underwater on a strip, creating a diving bubble trail, then resurfaces on the pause. Red/white is the signature saltwater color. Ideal for snook holding near mangrove roots and juvenile tarpon in the Everglades backcountry where its erratic dive-and-rise triggers explosive strikes.
patterns.image_source: Ahrex Hooks Dahlberg Diver tying article, high-quality photo of finished deer-hair diver

regional_usage.notes: Guide sources (Guide Recommended) call the Dahlberg Diver 'a must-have for the countless grown, branched-up Everglades areas' where snook ambush prey near mangrove roots; its deer-hair diving head produces a bubble trail that triggers strikes.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Pesca Maya specifically lists Dahlberg Rabbit Strip Divers in red/white for snook and baby tarpon in the mangrove systems of Ascension Bay.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Library universal (existing #46); the deer-hair diving head makes this a primary surface-to-subsurface fly for Cape York barramundi around structure and snags; swoffa.com lists it as one of the top Australian barramundi patterns.

Library universal (existing #46); the deer-hair diving head is one of the most documented fly types for Papuan black bass in jungle river systems; Fly Odyssey PNG describes these bass as attacking big surface divers around timber and undercut banks.
Rabbit-strip diver in red/white or black/red; proven for large snook at the forest-margin canal edges throughout Tortuguero where fish ambush prey near overhanging vegetation.

patterns.name: Deceiver (Heavy Wire / Bluefish Variant)
patterns.description: Lefty Kreh's Deceiver tied on heavy-wire hooks, often pre-rigged with short wire bite guards for bluefish. Bucktail over saddle hackle tail creates a slim, pulsing baitfish profile. Strip fast and erratically through bluefish blitzes and striper rips at Montauk and the Outer Banks. Durability against bluefish teeth is the defining modification over standard Deceiver builds.
patterns.image_source: Big Y Fly Co — Lefty's Deceiver professional product photo

regional_usage.notes: Large olive-back Deceivers imitating finger mullet are effective in Pamlico Sound for red drum and winter stripers, and also along the Cape Hatteras surf when bluefish are active.

patterns.name: Del Brown's Permit Fly (Merkin)
patterns.description: Del Brown and guide Steve Huff's rug-yarn crab, tied with spun yarn legs, rubber-strand claws, and lead eyes that flip the hook point upward — the definitive permit crab. Brown used it to land a record 513 permit. Sinks quickly to meet feeding permit on the bottom; the weedless hook rides point-up through turtle grass. The benchmark permit pattern on Keys, Bahamas, and Yucatan flats.
patterns.image_source: Orvis product photo — Merkin Crab permit fly, clean white background professional shot

regional_usage.notes: Andros South lodge recommends Merkin-style crab patterns for permit encountered on the southwest cays and ocean flats; Del Brown's original rug-yarn crab design sinks quickly to the bottom where Andros permit feed.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Angler Adventures lists the Merkin as a core permit pattern for the Bahamas including out-island destinations; Acklins permit are found on deeper flat edges where this sinking crab excels.

Designed by Del Brown and guide Steve Huff from the Lower Keys; the rug-yarn crab has helped Brown catch a record 513 permit and is the benchmark crab pattern for the permit-rich flats around Key West and the Content Keys.
Shallow Tails guide (Miami) recommends 'small merkin crab' for Biscayne Bay bonefish and permit; the Merkin's crab silhouette matches the numerous small crabs that live in the bay's seagrass beds.
Yarn crab with weighted eyes sinks hook-point-up to imitate a fleeing blue crab; Blue Bonefish Belize lodge lists it as the permit pattern that has accounted for the most permit caught globally.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
