regional_usage.notes: Standard permit crab in the Yucatán fly box; Palometa Club recommends lead-eye versions for the deeper permit channels around Ascension Bay.
The weedless Merkin-style crab is a critical Pamlico Sound red drum pattern; drum tailing on grass flats in the sound respond aggressively to crab patterns dropped ahead of their nose.

Weighted Merkin crabs in tan and olive on size 2 hooks are listed in multiple Los Roques tackle guides for permit on the outer flats; the large, fast-sinking profile suits the 20-40 lb class permit that inhabit the deeper edges at Los Roques.
Standard permit crab for the occasional permit encountered on Bimini flats; also eaten by large bonefish feeding on crabs over grassy patches.
Permit are present on T&C flats, particularly near stingray feeding craters; the Merkin is a standard crab presentation for both permit and crab-feeding bonefish.
Permit are confirmed on Bonaire flats (Fishing Adventures Bonaire); Merkin crab on a sinking presentation is the standard approach when permit are spotted.
The original crab pattern for Mexico's palometa (permit); standard at Boca Paila Lodge and throughout the Sian Ka'an for tailing permit on grass flats.

Listed explicitly by Fly Fishing Caribe (Guanaja Lodge, Honduras) as a core permit crab pattern; the classic yarn-and-weighted-eye crab is the standard permit fly across Honduras's grass-and-sand flats.

patterns.name: DMA (Dark Marabou Anchovy)
patterns.description: Dark marabou streamer imitating the Atlantic anchovy baitfish that concentrate at Gabon's estuary mouths during tarpon season. Created by Conrad Botes circa 2015 as a Sette Cama staple alongside Spongebobs and Tarpon Toads. The marabou tail breathes and pulses on a slow strip. Sinking-line presentation in deep channel mouths draws explosive Atlantic tarpon and giant African threadfin strikes.
patterns.image_source: No specific DMA image found; pattern referenced in The Mission Fly Fishing Magazine and Tourette Fishing but no product photography retrieved

regional_usage.notes: A Gabon-specific dark marabou anchovy streamer referenced alongside Spongebobs and Tarpon Toads as a Sette Cama staple in The Mission Fly Fishing Magazine; imitates the Atlantic anchovy baitfish that concentrate in Gabon's estuary mouths.

patterns.name: Dogtooth Tuna Tube Fly
patterns.description: A large 20–30 cm tandem-hook tube fly in white/chartreuse or pink/white, built to imitate the flying fish and large baitfish dogtooth tuna pursue over deep reef drop-offs. Fished on full-sinking Di7 lines with fast, erratic strips in the Maldives, Madagascar's Leven Bank, and Solomon Islands seamounts. The tube format allows hook replacement after hard strikes.
patterns.image_source: flyfishingmaldives.com — tube fly product for Maldives dogtooth tuna fishing

regional_usage.notes: Large (20–30 cm) tandem-hook tube fly in white/chartreuse or pink/white; dogtooth tuna are a premier target in the Maldives (Aug–Oct peak) and require fast-sinking, large-profile flies cast to deep channel edges and reef drop-offs on 12 wt outfits.

Large 20–30 cm tandem-hook tube fly in white/chartreuse or pink/white on 12 wt; dogtooth tuna at Nosy Be average 60 lb with fish to 220 lb recorded; deep presentations over reef drop-offs at Castor Bank and Leven Bank are the primary method.

Large tandem tube fly for the giant dogtooth tuna of Solomon seamounts (Matikai seamount near Wilderness Lodge); dogtooth here are described as some of the most intact tuna stocks on Earth and are a primary fly fishing draw.

patterns.name: Drum Beater
patterns.description: A weighted bottom-crawling crab pattern designed to imitate the blue and mud crabs that dominate the forage base on Louisiana oyster reefs and Texas Laguna Madre grass flats. Its weedless hook and chenille or foam legs dig into shell and substrate near feeding drum. Cast ahead of a rooting fish and let it sink; available from Umpqua Feather Merchants.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants official product photo — clean white background, clear side profile

regional_usage.notes: A bottom-crawling crab pattern tied specifically to imitate the blue and mud crabs abundant on Louisiana's oyster reefs, where black drum and redfish root along the shell.
A bottom-crawling crab pattern favored for the large black drum schools that move the Laguna's sandy flats during spring; its weedless presentation digs into the substrate near feeding drum.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Purpose-built crab pattern for tailing black drum on the Mosquito Lagoon / IRL grass flats where drum can be found alongside redfish — already in library.
Targeted crab/shrimp for the occasional black drum mixed in with GA schools of redfish on oyster-shell and mud-flat areas — already in library.

patterns.name: EP Anchovy
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's translucent EP-fiber anchovy is sized to match the dense bay anchovy schools that false albacore, bonito, and stripers pin to the surface each fall. Sparse layered fibers over an epoxy head create a clear, slim 2–3-inch profile. Fast, erratic strip retrieve; deadly at Cape Cod, Rhode Island, and Montauk in September–October.
patterns.image_source: Trident Fly Fishing shop — EP Anchovy Fly product photo, professional full-resolution

regional_usage.notes: Puglisi's fiber-wing anchovy imitation excels at Cape Lookout where albies, Spanish mackerel, and little tunny chase dense schools of bay anchovies along the inlet shoals in fall.

patterns.name: EP Backcountry Baitfish
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's inshore-specific baitfish uses EP fibers stacked in lateral layers to create a translucent, breathing 3-4 inch profile that pulses on a slow retrieve. Tan, brown-orange, and olive color schemes match Everglades backcountry forage. Preferred by Everglades guides for snook along mangrove points and rolling backcountry tarpon in tidal creeks.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com product photo of EP Backcountry Baitfish in brown/orange on white

regional_usage.notes: Everglades Fly Fishing Charters lists 'Enrico Puglisi's Back Country Baitfish' as a primary Everglades snook fly; Puglisi's inshore-specific EP pattern is sized and profiled for the brackish backcountry baitfish forage of snook and tarpon.

Medium-sized EP Fiber baitfish imitation designed for inshore backcountry and estuarine species; well-matched to Costa Rica's river-mouth and mangrove-channel fishing for cubera snapper and large Pacific snook.
EP fiber baitfish in white/chartreuse or olive/white is a premier snook and backcountry species pattern for Boca Paila's mangrove-creek and lagoon environments.

patterns.name: EP Baitfish
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's early-1990s synthetic-fiber baitfish built from layered EP fibers that shed water instantly for long casts. Its translucent, three-dimensional profile collapses on the strip then breathes open on the pause. Tied in mullet, sardine, or pilchard colors depending on target species. Standard tarpon, snook, and barracuda presentation in South Florida and Caribbean waters.
patterns.image_source: Feather Craft Fly Fishing — Enrico Puglisi Baitfish Imitations product photo

regional_usage.notes: Puglisi's synthetic-fiber baitfish profile sheds water cleanly for long Andros casts; fished fast for barracuda on the flats and slower for tarpon in the creek systems.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Puglisi's synthetic baitfish is the standard search pattern for the barracuda and jacks that patrol out-island flats alongside bonefish; fished on wire with a stinger for cuda.
Puglisi's synthetic-fiber baitfish profile shed water for Keys-style long casts and is a modern standard for tarpon subsurface presentations; especially effective when mullet are the dominant forage.

Everglades guide Capt. Buddy Ferber (Everglades Fly Fishing Charters) lists EP Baitfish as a primary Everglades snook and tarpon pattern; Puglisi's home waters in the New York area are very different but his synthetics dominate South Florida.
Synthetic fiber baitfish pattern with lifelike translucency; effective for JDR's opportunistic species and the large tarpon that key in on small baitfish around the cays.
EP fiber baitfish patterns are standard in Hawaii GT and omilu boxes for their translucency and lifelike profile when stripped through reef channels and points.

EP synthetic fiber baitfish patterns in white, chartreuse, and blue/silver are effective for the predatory tarpon and barracuda that patrol the channel edges; the lightweight, water-resistant material casts well in the persistent trade winds.
EP fiber sardine/mullet profile matches the baitfish on which queenfish mount spectacular pack attacks at Shuwaymiyah and the Hallaniyat reef edges.
EP sardine/mullet profile is the standard baitfish fly for dredging Bazaruto's offshore pinnacles and surface casting during queenfish pack attacks at the reef edges.
Synthetic fiber baitfish with translucent movement; effective for both tarpon and large snook when fish are keyed on mullet in the Tortuguero canals and Río Colorado river mouth.

Synthetic fiber baitfish with translucent movement; recommended by Tapam Lodge itineraries as a medium baitfish (11–13 cm) for clear-water lagoon tarpon that are laid up and require a smaller, more subtle presentation.

Multiple EP Puglisi wet fly variants named in the Fly Fishing Caribe Bocas del Toro fly list (Brown, Blue/Red, Green Sardine, Blue Sardine, Sunshine) in sizes 1/0–4/0; the translucent synthetic fibers present a lifelike baitfish profile for Bocas's big-rolling tarpon.
Water-shedding EP-fiber baitfish described by Yellow Dog as a 'modern-day classic' for Southwest Florida snook from mangroves to beach fishing — already in library.

Medium to large EP baitfish (white/olive or blue/white) for mixed-pelagic targeting at the offshore FADs and reefs of the Solomons, where a wide range of species including GTs, dogtooth tuna, and mackerel respond to quality baitfish imitations. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'EP Baitfish'.

patterns.name: EP Crab
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's synthetic fiber crab imitation, built with EP brush fibers that produce a lifelike translucent profile and micro-movement in current. Realistic enough to fool permit in the clear shallows of Belize and Yucatan. Equally effective as a slow-sinking crab for Louisiana marsh redfish and sheepshead feeding on oyster reefs; fished with a dead-drift or gentle short strips.
patterns.image_source: TackleDirect — Enrico Puglisi EP Permit Crab, white background professional product photo

regional_usage.notes: Synthetic fiber crab with lifelike translucent movement; listed on both El Pescador and Blue Bonefish Belize permit fly lists for its realistic profile in shallow clear-water situations.
Enrico Puglisi's EP fiber crab imitation sinks slowly and presents well on the oyster-reef and grass-flat edges that define Louisiana marsh structure.
The Laguna Madre hosts abundant swimming crabs and mud crabs that form a primary food source for black drum, sheepshead, and tailing redfish along the sabalo grass flats.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: EP-fiber crab with weedguard covers the fiddler-crab and blue-crab forage central to IRL redfish and black drum feeding — already in library.
Weedguard-equipped EP-fiber crab that imitates the blue crabs and mud crabs central to Lowcountry redfish diet on exposed flats — already in library.
Weedguard crab pattern used by Golden Isles guides for tailing reds on low-tide mud flats and hard-bottom exposed areas — already in library.

patterns.name: EP Ghost Shrimp
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's translucent synthetic shrimp pattern built with sparse EP fibers over a bead-chain or lead-eye system. Its ghostly, semi-transparent profile closely matches the glass shrimp prevalent on Bahamian hard-sand flats. Lightweight enough for a quiet water entry critical on spooky fish; strip slowly along bottom or allow to flutter on a dead sink.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com product listing — clean side profile photo of EP Ghost Shrimp in tan

regional_usage.notes: Puglisi's lifelike sparse synthetic shrimp in tan is a lodge-recommended staple for Andros; its translucent body and quiet entry work well on the large hard-sand flats where bonefish can be picky.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Puglisi's spare synthetic shrimp is recommended by the Delphi Club (Abaco) supplier GuideFlies.com as part of the core shrimp/crab/baitfish selection for Abaco's hard-sand and mangrove-marl flats.
Tan EP Ghost Shrimp recommended by Deep Water Cay guides for cautious Bahamas bonefish; very sparse profile lands quietly and sinks on bead-chain eyes.
Recommended by Deep Water Cay (Grand Bahama) guides — an identical fishery context to T&C; tan colorway matches Caicos Bank sand-flat shrimp.
Tan EP Ghost Shrimp in #6-#8 with bead-chain eyes is well-suited to Bonaire's crystal-clear water and mixed-sand flats; sparse profile avoids spooking fish in gin-clear conditions.

patterns.name: EP GT's Sardina
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's oversized sardine imitation tied on 5/0–8/0 hooks with layered EP fibers and 3D eyes for giant trevally, roosterfish, and large dorado. The broad, iridescent profile displaces significant water on the strip. Fished with fast, aggressive retrieves that match the desperate flight of a sardine being herded by pelagic predators.
patterns.image_source: Salt Fly Pro shop — EP GT's Sardina 8/0, high-resolution product photo on white

regional_usage.notes: Enrico Puglisi's 5/0 GT-sized sardina pattern is documented as a similar alternative to the EP Roosterfish Mullet for targeting Baja species; its large profile suits the biggest roosters and dorado chasing substantial bait.

Library pattern (existing #55); EP's large sardina-style baitfish pattern is documented by Hastings Fly Fishers Australia as a top-tier GT fly alongside the Black Brush and GT Semper; included as regional tag.

patterns.name: EP Micro Crab
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's small crab imitation uses EP fiber legs and a sparse flat body to replicate juvenile crabs in sizes 6–10. Minimal splash on entry makes it ideal for tailing bonefish in skinny water and permit rooting in turtle grass. Lead or bead-chain eyes in varying weights match different flat depths. Used across Bahamas, Belize, and the Florida Keys.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com product photo of EP Micro Crab, clear side profile on white background

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Small crab pattern listed by the Acklins guide sources as essential for tailing bonefish in mangroves; the Acklins flybox guidance specifically calls for 'small and light crab flies with rubber legs' for mangrove tailing fish.
Small crab profile for bonefish and permit; particularly useful on the Middle Keys turtle-grass flats where permit root for small crabs alongside bonefish in shallow water.
Recommended for skinny-water tailing oio on Hawaiian flats in tan, dark brown, and olive; guides often remove weed guards for spooky fish.

patterns.name: EP Minnow / Mullet
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's EP-fiber minnow in finger-mullet or scaled mullet colors — olive/white or tan/gray with distinct lateral flash. Larger profile (3–5 inches) than basic EP baitfish; swims with a breathing, collapsing action. Effective on Outer Banks red drum sight-casted in Pamlico Sound, and for Spanish mackerel blitzing finger mullet along inlets. Cast ahead, strip-pause.
patterns.image_source: Trident Fly Fishing — EP Mullet Fly clean product photo

regional_usage.notes: Puglisi's larger EP fiber minnow in mullet colors is a proven Pamlico Sound pattern for sight-casting red drum and also works for Spanish mackerel blitzing finger mullet along OBX inlets.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Mullet are year-round forage in the IRL and this EP-fiber baitfish is a go-to summer pattern when reds shift off crabs and onto finger mullet schools — already in library.

patterns.name: EP Mullet
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's EP-fiber mullet imitation, layered to create a hollow, translucent baitfish profile matching juvenile and finger mullet. Tied in 3–6-inch versions in silver-white or gray. Covers the dominant forage species across Laguna Madre, Louisiana marshes, and Baja beaches. Cast into feeding lanes and stripped at medium pace — the EP-fiber tail breathes between strips; irresistible to roosterfish and large trout.
patterns.image_source: Trident Fly Fishing — EP Mullet Fly, large professional product photo

regional_usage.notes: Enrico Puglisi's EP-fiber mullet imitation matches the abundant finger mullet that school throughout Louisiana's marshes, triggering predatory strikes from larger redfish and trout.
Mullet are the dominant baitfish throughout Laguna Madre, and Puglisi's EP-fiber imitation in silver-and-white is a primary baitfish pattern for large trout and bulls feeding in the passes.

A standard mullet imitation deployed across Baja's beach fishery; Magdalena Bay snook guides use the EP Mullet in smaller sizes to match the finger mullet that gather near mangrove shorelines. Enrico Puglisi's 5.5-inch EP-fiber mullet imitation is the single most commonly recommended pattern for Baja roosterfish; it matches the juvenile mullet and sardines that roosterfish herd against the beach.

Large mullet imitation in natural/tan using EP Fibers; highly effective for roosterfish on the Costa Rica Pacific beaches where mullet schools are a primary forage, and equally proven for large snook in tidal estuaries.

Large mullet-imitation EP pattern in natural/tan; mullet schools are a key prey item at Bocas del Toro's river mouths and the EP Mullet's neutral profile matches the forage that concentrates both tarpon and snook in the mixing zones.
Mullet is the primary forage across Tampa Bay and Pine Island Sound; the EP Mullet is recommended by Yellow Dog as an essential snook fly for mangrove and beach presentations — already in library.

patterns.name: EP Peanut Butter
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's EP Fiber baitfish imitation built from layered synthetic fibers that taper to a translucent tail, creating a lifelike profile and soft undulation in the water. Works as a universal small baitfish across species — roosterfish, dorado, yellowfin tuna, and jack crevalle. Fished with medium-speed strips on an intermediate or floating line in Costa Rica's inshore and offshore grounds.
patterns.image_source: tridentflyfishing.com — professional fly shop commercial product photo, white background, correctly labeled EP Peanut Butter Fly

regional_usage.notes: EP Fiber baitfish imitation proven on roosterfish, dorado, and GT-class fish worldwide; the unique taper and soft-fiber movement makes it one of the most effective generic baitfish patterns for Costa Rica's varied inshore and offshore species.

All Points Fly Shop Cuba guide specifically recommended EP Peanut Butter as 'also a preferred snook fly for the location' at Cayo Largo, in addition to its effectiveness for tarpon in the bait-rich channels.

patterns.name: EP Spawning Shrimp
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's realistic synthetic spawning shrimp tied in multiple colors and eye weights to cover shallow flats through deeper cuts. Its EP fiber body produces lifelike translucency that mimics shrimp in spawn — a trigger for permit and bonefish alike. Sink it to the bottom on turtle-grass and sand; fished in Belize, Mexico's Ascension Bay, and beyond.
patterns.image_source: Yellow Dog Flyfishing product photo — EP Spawning Shrimp (Presentation Lead) in tan, clean square image

regional_usage.notes: Described by Blue Bonefish Belize as a 'confidence fly for all guides in Belize' that can be fished effectively in both deep water and on shallow flats for permit and bonefish alike.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Palometa Club specifically names Enrico Puglisi's Spawning Shrimp as the best-tied pattern in multiple colors and eye weights for the varying depths and bottom types of Ascension Bay.
Widely recommended by Hawaii guide Jesse Cheape (Hi Tide Fishing) in size 4 with heavy dumbbell eyes for the deeper, rockier Hawaiian flats.
Listed as a top Bahamas/T&C flat fly by Soul Fly Lodge; EP fiber profile moves naturally in the water and sinks efficiently to the 2-4 ft Caicos Bank depths.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Sparse, translucent EP-fiber shrimp that excels in the IRL's clear water where spooky fish can see and inspect a fly before eating — already in library.
Sparse EP shrimp matches the large brown and white shrimp that flood SC tidal marshes in summer and autumn, triggering school-redfish feeding frenzies at low tide creek mouths — already in library.
Matches the grass shrimp and brown shrimp abundant in GA tidal creeks in fall; reliable September–November pattern for reds shifting off crabs toward shrimp — already in library.

patterns.name: Fatboy
patterns.description: Bulky Australian saltwater fly with a voluminous synthetic or EP-fiber body generating maximum water displacement. Listed by SWOFFA as a core Cape York barramundi pattern. The pushed-water signature is critical in turbid Gulf of Carpentaria conditions where barramundi and GT rely on the lateral line to locate prey at night or in low visibility.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; Australian regional pattern not commercially photographed

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Bulky Australian saltwater fly listed by swoffa.com as one of the core Cape York barramundi patterns; the profile pushes water and is effective in turbid Gulf conditions where big barramundi and GT respond to displaced water more than flash.

patterns.name: Flaming Lamborghini
patterns.description: Large, vivid coral-grouper-profile baitfish fly tied on Gamakatsu SL12 6/0 by Fulling Mill. Orange-red brushy body mimics the reef baitfish GTs crush around coral heads and rubble flats. Fished on a fast 12-weight with an aggressive strip-pause retrieve at Exmouth, Raja Ampat, PNG, and the Maldives. Recomended by The Flyfisher Australia in their curated GT selection.
patterns.image_source: Salt Fly Pro (saltflypro.com) — Flaming Lamborgini GT Fly #6/0, Fulling Mill product listing

regional_usage.notes: Coral-grouper imitation designed to fish around coral heads and reef structure; tied on Gamakatsu SL12 and recommended by The Flyfisher (Australia) in their curated GT selection; part of the standard Exmouth GT fly box.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Coral-grouper baitfish imitation recommended in The Flyfisher Australia GT selection; effective around the snag-heavy structure of Cape York estuaries and reef formations in the Coral Sea.

Coral-grouper baitfish imitation effective around coral structure; PNG's Bismarck reefs and Portlock Reef systems are heavily structured with coral heads where this pattern's grouper coloration triggers reaction strikes.
Coral-grouper profile designed for structure fishing; Raja Ampat's coral-rich limestone karst islands provide ideal structure habitat matching this fly's coral-reef-dweller imitation.

Bright orange/red GT streamer designed to match the vivid reef baitfish found in Indian Ocean coral environments; recommended by Seychelles-experienced guides as a GT attraction fly when standard darks fail on tough days.

patterns.name: Flashtail Whistler
patterns.description: Dan Blanton's classic cone-head streamer built around a prominent bead-chain or lead-eye head, bucktail collar, and a long Flashabou tail. The rattling, flashy profile imitates injured baitfish and draws reaction strikes. Red/white and orange/yellow are standard colors for snook in Everglades passes and Biscayne Bay; also works for tarpon and jacks.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants product photo — Flashtail Whistler in red/yellow, clean white background

regional_usage.notes: Listed by Everglades snook guides as an all-around search pattern; red/white with flash Whistlers work for snook along mangrove shorelines and in the passes of the 10,000 Islands where current concentrates bait.
A deep-diving Hawaiian guide classic for reef channel species; heavy bead-chain eyes and bucktail body probe the rocky bottom structure where papio and GT hold.

Bead-chain-eye hackle-and-flash streamer that generates vibration in colored water; guides in turbid jungle river mouths rely on the Whistler's sound signature to attract tarpon that cannot visually locate a fly.

Vibration-producing bead-chain eye streamer that works in the turbid, high-tannin water of Nicaragua's main river channels where sound and pressure wave detection are more reliable triggers than visual cues.

Listed by Fly Fishing Caribe as 'Wet Fly Whistler Fly #1/0, 2/0, 3/0' for Bocas del Toro; bead-chain-eye pattern that generates vibration in the turbid, nutrient-rich mixing zone where tarpon of 20–200 lbs feed aggressively.

The Flashtail Whistler's bead-head rattle and flash-forward wing make it an effective mid-water pattern for queenfish and mixed trevally species that school over shallow coral pinnacles at Nosy Be. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Flashtail Whistler'.

The Flashtail Whistler is referenced in the Solomon Islands lagoon environment as an effective attractor for mixed trevally species feeding over coral heads; the rattle head triggers reaction strikes from the multiple trevally species present. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Flashtail Whistler'.

patterns.name: Flashy Profile
patterns.description: A wide-body synthetic streamer built with layered flash material and a broad lateral silhouette designed to reflect maximum light. Used primarily in Baja bluewater teaser-and-fly sequences where hookless teasers are used to raise billfish — the Flashy Profile is then presented on the drop. Its lateral-line-triggering flash profile also works on dorado and yellowfin tuna.
patterns.image_source: The Mission Fly Mag article photo of Howe-style Flashy Profile fly, clear image of finished pattern

regional_usage.notes: A wide-body synthetic streamer with heavy flash material; the lateral-line-stimulating flash profile is used when daisy-chaining Baja billfish brought to the transom with hookless teasers before fly presentation.
High-flash synthetic baitfish profile that excels in blue-water conditions when tuna and dorado are keyed on cigar-minnows and sardines in bait balls off Los Sueños and Quepos.

patterns.name: Fleeing Crab
patterns.description: Barred tan-and-white craft-fur crab with orange rubber legs, bead-chain eyes, and a flat profile that sinks slowly hook-point-up. Minimal bulk lands softly and presents a convincing fleeing posture. Listed by Alphonse Fishing Co. as a top-three Seychelles bonefish fly; also draws permit and triggerfish on open sand and turtle-grass flats.
patterns.image_source: Salt Fly Pro — Umpqua Cathy's Fleeing Crab professional product photo

regional_usage.notes: Simple barred tan-and-white crab imitation with orange rubber legs listed by Alphonse Fishing Co. as a top-three bonefish fly; also effective for permit and triggers on open sand and turtle-grass flats.

Barred tan/white fleeing crab variant; an Alphonse Fishing Co. standard that applies identically to the hard white sand and broken coral flats of St Brandon's Atoll. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Fleeing Crab'.

Lead-eye crab that dives quickly and mimics a panicked fleeing crab — the Cathy's Fleeing Crab variant is widely cited by SC and GA flood-tide guides alongside Fiddlestick Crab and Merkin — already in library.
Cathy's Fleeing Crab is cited alongside the Fiddlestick and Merkin as a standard Georgia and South Carolina flood-tide crab selection — already in library.

patterns.name: Flexo Crab
patterns.description: The InTheRiffle team's soft-body crab built around expandable mesh tubing (flexo mesh) over a weighted core, producing a realistic carapace that collapses and re-inflates on the sink. The top triggerfish pattern at Christmas Island and the Seychelles; also used for permit at Jardines de la Reina. Presented to feeding fish and allowed to free-sink, triggering inspection-and-eat responses.
patterns.image_source: Ashland Fly Shop — Flexo Crab permit fly pattern, high-resolution clean background

regional_usage.notes: Fishmaster (Finland) lists the Flexo Crab alongside the Avalon fly as a primary permit pattern for Jardines de la Reina; flexible-body crab that presents naturally in deeper water.
Small crab imitation using expandable mesh tubing; the Fulling Mill variant is documented as the top trigger pattern at Christmas Island after extensive on-site testing by guides.

The mesh-tubing ancestor of the Alphlexo; the permit-fisher's go-to pattern on Seychelles flats where permit refuse sparser flies; the Fulling Mill Flexo is considered the benchmark trigger pattern in multiple sizes and colors.

Listed directly in the Fulling Mill Los Roques fly selection in tan and olive in sizes 2-6; international guides 'demand' this mesh-body crab on trips to Los Roques (Ole Florida Fly Shop), and it is widely used by Italian-guided operations who bring it from European fly shops for permit and triggerfish on the coral flats.
Original Flexo body with rubber legs; widely carried as a backup trigger crab and recommended by Christmas Island and Nubian guides alike when Alphlexo is unavailable.
Standard backup crab for Oman permit and bluefin trevally when the heavier Alphlexo risks spooking fish in clear, calm conditions around the rocky points.
Xcalak-area guides list Flexo Crab as a top permit pattern for Sian Ka'an flats; olive, tan, and white in #2-#4 with rubber legs and quick sink rate.

Listed as a primary permit pattern for Cuban destinations; the flexible-body crab sinks well and presents naturally on the deeper permit flats of Cayo Cruz where fish often follow stingrays in 2–3 ft of water.

patterns.name: Flymen Sailfish Fly (Tandem Pink/White Tube)
patterns.description: Flymen Fishing Company's commercially produced tandem two-hook tube fly in the standard pink-and-white billfish color scheme. Tied in the round on linked tubes with layered bucktail, hackle, and Flashabou. Stocked by Yellow Dog Flyfishing and used widely on Costa Rica Pacific charter boats as a proven, accessible alternative to custom Cam Sigler builds for Pacific sailfish.
patterns.image_source: yellowdogflyfishing.com — authoritative fly travel retailer, product photo of Flymen Sailfish Fly in white/pink tandem tube configuration

regional_usage.notes: Commercially available tandem two-hook tube fly in the standard pink/white billfish color scheme; stocked by Yellow Dog Flyfishing and widely used on Costa Rica Pacific charter boats as an accessible Cam Sigler alternative.

patterns.name: Gabon Surf Clouser
patterns.description: The Clouser Deep Minnow tied heavy — large lead dumbbell eyes, 3/0–4/0 hooks — in olive/white or chartreuse/white for fast-sinking presentations through Gabon's ripping beach surf at Sette Cama. Developed as a reliable all-rounder across multiple species; referenced in trip reports as the go-to fly when tarpon, Senegal kob, and leerfish are crashing bait in the shore break.
patterns.image_source: saltwaterflies.com — Clouser Deep Minnow olive/white saltwater pattern

regional_usage.notes: Clouser Deep Minnow tied heavy (large lead eyes, 3/0–4/0) in olive/white or chartreuse/white for fast-sinking presentations in Gabon's ripping beach surf; referenced across multiple Sette Cama trip reports as a reliable all-rounder. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Clouser Deep Minnow'.

patterns.name: Game Changer
patterns.description: Blane Chocklett's multi-segment articulated fly uses Chocklett's Articulated Shanks linked by loops, each dressed with EP fibers or craft fur, creating a continuously S-curving swimming action. Sized 4–8 inches for trophy stripers chasing bunker and herring. The lifelike swimming profile triggers big fish that ignore conventional bucktail patterns.
patterns.image_source: House of Fly — Chocklett's Feather Game Changer, retail product photo showing articulated profile

regional_usage.notes: Chocklett's articulated jointed baitfish has been adopted by OBX guides for large Pamlico Sound red drum and trophy winter stripers, where its swimming action imitates the mullet that drum root after.
Articulated multi-joint swimmer gives a lifelike undulation that provokes strikes from giant GTs that have seen conventional brush flies repeatedly; best used for reluctant fish in clear conditions.
Articulated swimmer fished on a sinking line over deep Bazaruto pinnacles imitates the large mullet and bream that dogtooth tuna and big GTs target in the offshore current seams.

Library universal (existing #66); the segmented-articulated construction with life-like swimming action is one of the few Western patterns proven on Niugini black bass; Rock Expeditions PNG notes that bass respond to large, lifelike swimming profiles in the current-seams of jungle rivers.

Large articulated multi-section fly that mimics a live mullet with swimming body action; recommended for deep-water sinking-line presentations when tarpon are holding in the 30–50 ft channels of the Río Colorado mouth.

Large articulated baitfish with realistic swimming action; guides at Tapam Lodge use heavy flies of this class on sinking lines when tarpon are concentrated in 20–40 ft channels feeding actively on mullet schools.

All Points Fly Shop reports 'Worked great on channel tarpon with sinking lines' at Cayo Largo; note that due to weight when wet it can be difficult for flats sight-casting, so it is reserved for blind-casting in channels.

patterns.name: Gartside Gurgler
patterns.description: Jack Gartside's 1988 design uses a folded foam back strip over a bucktail or craft-fur body to create a low-riding surface fly. On the strip, the foam lip dips and pushes water creating a gurgling sound; at rest it floats hook-point-up. Highly versatile — worked slowly for snook and redfish, stripped fast to draw topwater strikes from stripers and bluefish.
patterns.image_source: Charlie's Fly Box clear product photo of Gartside's Gurgler, side profile on white

regional_usage.notes: Jack Gartside's foam-lip surface fly creates commotion that draws explosive topwater strikes from redfish and trout working the shallow, calm grassy ponds of the Louisiana marsh.
The foam Gurgler creates visible wakes and sound on calm Laguna mornings, drawing explosively visual strikes from redfish and large speckled trout working the shallow grass edges.

The Gurgler stripped fast along Baja's sandy beaches creates the surface commotion that roosterfish use to locate panicked baitfish; guides favor chartreuse-and-white versions during low-light beach runs.

Jack Gartside's foam-back surface fly is listed by Everglades guide sources as effective for snook and tarpon; the Gurgler's low-riding surface action triggers explosive strikes from snook holding along mangrove edges.
Gartside's foam-lip surface fly is a primary Pamlico Sound red drum pattern fished over grass flats and shoal edges where bull redfish chase mullet and menhaden in calm conditions.
The gurgler's surface wake draws aggressive trevally and papio strikes in Hawaiian channels and reef edges; local anglers use it as a topwater alternative to hard poppers.
Fish-Bones lists a Gurgler as a top Cayman tarpon and snook fly; the Central Mangrove Wetlands and shoreline cuts on Grand Cayman hold both species.
Surface gurgler is extremely effective for Boca Paila snook ambushing baitfish along mangrove edges and for juvenile tarpon in the Sian Ka'an lagoon channels.
Surface-wake fly that creates a gurgling disturbance effective for snook in mangrove channels and baby tarpon rolling near vegetation in the Tortuguero canal system.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Small gurglers are a documented early-morning tactic on Mosquito Lagoon to locate and draw surface strikes from scattered reds and trout before the sun gets high — already in library.
Popping-foam surface fly used to locate and trigger aggressive reds on flooded Lowcountry flats at dawn; the commotion draws fish from distance in flat, calm marsh conditions — already in library.
Surface disturbance fly used at dawn on calm GA marsh flats to locate and trigger tailing reds before light allows sight-fishing — already in library.

Topwater foam gurgler is a primary surface fly for West Florida snook in the mangroves; the 'Hot Lips' variant (Capt. Steve Huff) is cited as a top mangrove snook fly in North Florida and the Everglades — already in library.

patterns.name: Generic Baitfish Pattern (Needlefish / Offshore)
patterns.description: Long slim synthetics in 1/0–4/0 replicating needlefish, ballyhoo, and slender forage around Christmas Island reef edges and channel drop-offs. Built 4–8 inches with EZ Body, craft fur, or EP fibers over a flash core. Retrieve fast with long strips to match erratic needlefish movement. Triggers large GT and queenfish on a reaction strike.
patterns.image_source: Salt Fly Pro — Beech's Garfish (Needlefish) fly product photo, clean side profile

regional_usage.notes: Large synthetic needlefish and baitfish streamers in 1/0–4/0 are recommended for offshore and channel shots at GTs and queenfish around the outer reef at Christmas Island.

patterns.name: Ghetto Super Fly
patterns.originator: Makani Christensen (Fly Fish Hawaii / Keawe Adventures)
patterns.description: Hawaii's most effective bonefish fly, tied by Makani Christensen of Fly Fish Hawaii, imitates a mantis shrimp in multiple color variations with adjustable bead-chain weight for different reef depths on Oahu. The fly's low profile and soft material movement trigger bonefish feeding on coral sand and mixed rubble flats. Considered the go-to pattern by local guides across the island chain.
patterns.image_source: instagram.com — originator's own account showing Ghetto Super Fly 10-pack product; Instagram source, no commercial shop photo found

regional_usage.notes: Described as Hawaii's top bonefish fly by local guides; a mantis shrimp imitation tied in multiple colors with adjustable weight for varying reef depths on Oahu.

patterns.name: Golden Knight
patterns.description: Bonefish shrimp pattern developed by Alphonse Fishing Co. guides. Gold/tan Crystal Chenille or UV-dubbed body with bead-chain or tungsten eyes and a sparse craft-fur wing. Available in multiple weights for shallow sand to coral rubble. The FlyzInc-produced version is a standard Seychelles and Maldives guide-box fly for tailing bonefish and Indo-Pacific permit.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; Alphonse/FlyzInc guide fly with limited commercial photography

regional_usage.notes: Alphonse Fishing Co. guide-developed bonefish shrimp/Gotcha variant with a golden/tan body, available in tungsten bead and bead-chain weight options; official Seychelles assortment bonefish staple and applicable to Maldives bonefish on atoll flats.
Official Alphonse/Seychelles guide bonefish pattern transferable to St Brandon's flats; multiple accounts describe bonefish behaviour on these atolls as nearly identical to Alphonse.

patterns.name: Got Milk (Rio)
patterns.description: RIO Products' neutral-buoyancy synthetic foam plankton imitation designed specifically for surface-feeding milkfish. The foam body and sparse hackle mimic the small organisms milkfish sip from the surface film. Dead-drifted or given a micro-twitch in a milkfish feeding lane; used widely in the Maldives and Seychelles where tailing or surface-feeding milkfish present one of fly fishing's hardest targets.
patterns.image_source: No product image found for Rio Got Milk in retail fly shop databases (farbank.com, SaltFlyPro, BigTimeFLies, Orvis) — may be discontinued or catalog-only

regional_usage.notes: Rio Products' neutral-buoyant synthetic foam milkfish fly; recommended specifically for Indo-Pacific milkfish including Maldives and Seychelles destinations; a floating plankton imitation for feeding shoals on the surface.

patterns.name: Grand Slam Crab
patterns.description: A foam or deer-hair crab pattern tied to imitate the small crabs that permit and bonefish root for on shallow turtle-grass flats in Belize and Caribbean destinations. Its realistic profile and weedless hook design allow presentations into the zones where permit are feeding. Cast two rod-lengths ahead of a tailing or cruising permit and let it sink to the bottom.
patterns.image_source: Orvis official product photo of Grand Slam Crab on clean white background

regional_usage.notes: Named for Belize's Grand Slam fishery; listed on El Pescador's permit fly recommendations for the country's shallow turtle-grass flats.

patterns.name: Greg's Flats Fly
patterns.description: Greg Miheve's versatile Bahamian bonefish pattern pairs an iridescent body with split calf-tail claws that can pass as either shrimp or crab depending on retrieve speed and depth. Documented in Dick Brown's Bonefish Fly Patterns. Lightweight with minimal splash on entry; works across sandy, grassy, and hard-bottom Bahamian out-island flats.
patterns.image_source: Dakota Angler & Outfitter blog — Greg's Flats Fly editorial photo, excellent detail

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Documented in Dick Brown's 'Bonefish Fly Patterns' and tested on Bahamian flats; its iridescent body and split calf-tail claws can imitate shrimp or crab depending on retrieve, making it versatile across the varied out-island bottoms.

patterns.name: Grim Reaper
patterns.description: A dark-profile tarpon streamer in black and purple built with palmered feathers or marabou to maximize movement in low visibility. Listed by Pesca Maya for Ascension Bay backcountry lake tarpon. The high-contrast silhouette cuts through tannin-stained water where lighter flies go unseen. Strip-and-pause retrieve; the full profile pulses on the drop.
patterns.image_source: The Fly Fishers shop product photo of Pat Ehlers' Grim Reaper, clear side profile

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Named in Pesca Maya's tarpon fly list for the Ascension Bay backcountry lakes; dark profile effective in stained water conditions November–March.

patterns.name: Grocery Fly
patterns.description: Locally developed Baja baitfish streamer in tan-and-white matching the sardine silhouettes roosterfish key on in the surf zone. Tied 4–6 inches with synthetic fibers or bucktail for durability. Stripped fast near the surface along rocky points and beach breaks. A staple East Cape and La Paz guide fly for roosters, dorado, and jacks.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com — Enrico's Roosterfish Sardina baitfish, closest match to Grocery Fly profile

regional_usage.notes: A locally tied Baja baitfish pattern popular with East Cape and La Paz guides; tied in tan-and-white to match the specific baitfish silhouettes local roosters key on when feeding in the surf zone.

patterns.name: GT Brush Fly
patterns.originator: Tim Babich / FlyCastaway (Tan variant originator); broader GT brush tradition via South African Indian Ocean guides
patterns.description: A large, 4–6-inch EP-brush baitfish imitation tied on 4/0–6/0 hooks in black, purple, red, or tan, designed to push water and create a strong silhouette in the clear flats water where giant trevally hunt. Standard subsurface GT fly at Christmas Island and the Seychelles; fast, aggressive long strips mimic a fleeing baitfish. The bulk and movement of EP-brush fibers trigger the explosive predatory response that defines GT fly fishing.
patterns.image_source: Ashland Fly Shop — Giant Trevally GT Brush Fly, high-resolution clean background

regional_usage.notes: Large EP-brush baitfish imitation in black, purple, red, or tan that is the go-to subsurface fly for GTs on Christmas Island; Fulling Mill versions in sizes 6/0 are standard.

Standard large EP-brush baitfish imitation confirmed by Superflies field testing on Alphonse, Farquhar, Astove, and Cosmoledo; purple, red, and tan color variants outperform in varying light conditions.

Black and tan craft-fur brush flies on 6/0–8/0 Gamakatsu SL12S hooks are the single most-cited GT pattern for Indian Ocean fisheries including Sudan; imitates mullet and squid prevalent on the coral edges.
The primary fly for monster-GT targeting at Hallaniyat; 8/0 versions are mandatory when 50-kg-plus fish are the quarry — anything lighter risks straightening the hook on the initial run.
Standard GT fly for Mozambique's reef edges and channel mouths; chartreuse-and-white and black variants are carried by guides at Benguerra Island and Bazaruto lodge operations.

Library universal (existing #74); explicitly described as the standard Ningaloo subsurface GT fly in FlyLife Magazine with guide Brett Wolf recommending 6/0 and 8/0 black and black-and-purple versions around reef and mangrove edges.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Library universal (existing #74); standard GT subsurface fly also used on Cape York and Gulf flats; black and olive-white variants are most common for the turbid Gulf conditions.

Library universal (existing #74); the standard Indo-Pacific GT subsurface pattern; PNG GT guides (Fly Odyssey, Rock Expeditions) use the same heavy-tackle brush-fly system on PNG reefs as elsewhere in the Indo-Pacific.

Library universal (existing #74); subsurface GT standard used across all Indo-Pacific destinations; Raja Ampat's mangrove-fringed bays and reef passes concentrate GTs responding well to this pattern's baitfish profile.

The benchmark Indo-Pacific GT streamer; dark colourways (black/purple, red/black) dominate in Maldives surf-reef fishing where contrast is key, lighter tan versions for sandy flats. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'GT Brush Fly'.

St Brandon's is documented to have GT specimens exceeding 100 lb; standard Indo-Pacific GT brush flies in tan and dark colourways are the benchmark big-game pattern. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'GT Brush Fly'.

The primary GT streamer for Nosy Be reef-edge and coral pinnacle fishing; dark colourways (black/purple, red/black) effective against the corals and deep-blue water of Madagascar's outer banks. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'GT Brush Fly'.

The foundation GT pattern across all Indo-Pacific fisheries; in the Solomon Islands the fishery is lightly pressured enough that even modest presentations draw aggressive response, with dark colourways particularly effective around the coral bommies of Marovo Lagoon. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'GT Brush Fly'.

patterns.name: GT Bus Ticket
patterns.description: A Fulling Mill-produced open-flats baitfish pattern in lighter neutral colours designed to imitate small schooling baitfish over white sand and coral. The streamlined profile casts easily on 10–12 wt rods and maintains a lifelike swimming action at retrieve speed. Listed as a best-seller by Australian retailers and confirmed in curated Indo-Pacific GT fly boxes for Ningaloo and beyond.
patterns.image_source: fullingmill.com — official Bus Ticket S6/0 product photo

regional_usage.notes: Open-flats GT pattern in lighter colors mimicking baitfish over white sand; described as a best-seller by multiple Australian retailers and confirmed in GT fly boxes curated for Indo-Pacific destinations.

patterns.name: GT Flashy Profile
patterns.description: High-flash baitfish streamer in chartreuse/white or white/silver on 3/0–5/0 tied with Flashabou and synthetic fiber. Explicitly listed in The Flyfisher Australia staff-curated GT fly selection. Stripped fast across flats or through current seams, flash triggers aggressive GT feeding. Secondary target species include queenfish, Spanish mackerel, and golden trevally.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; generic Australian GT fly type without commercial identity

regional_usage.notes: High-flash baitfish streamer in chartreuse or white that is explicitly listed in The Flyfisher Australia's staff-curated GT fly selection; effective on both Ningaloo and Gulf-side flats for GTs and pelagics.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Flash-profile GT baitfish in chartreuse listed in Australian staff-curated GT boxes; effective in the clearer inshore water on the east Cape York side where visibility allows flash-reactive strikes.
High-flash chartreuse baitfish; effective on Indonesian pelagics including queenfish and mackerel that school over the coral pinnacles and current lines of Raja Ampat's offshore waters.

patterns.name: GT Mullet
patterns.description: Broadside mullet-profile baitfish fly on 6/0, created by Alphonse guide James Christmas. Slim EP-fiber construction delivers an enticing flank silhouette while remaining aerodynamic enough to throw on a 12-weight GT rod. Primarily stripped fast across tropical flats to trigger GT, queenfish, and bluefin trevally attacks. Used at Ningaloo, Raja Ampat, and Alphonse Island's sand-flat feeds.
patterns.image_source: Salt Fly Pro (saltflypro.com) — GT Mullet #6/0, James Christmas / Fulling Mill product listing

regional_usage.notes: Broadside baitfish profile designed by Alphonse/Christmas Island guide James Christmas to imitate mullet on tropical flats; slim and aerodynamic enough to cast on heavy GT rods, widely used across Indo-Pacific GT destinations including Ningaloo.
Slim mullet imitation by James Christmas; effective on the sand and rubble flats of Raja Ampat's shallow bays where mullet schools concentrate GTs on feeding tides.

patterns.name: Gummy Minnow
patterns.description: Blane Chocklett's translucent baitfish imitation built from Sili-Skin or similar flexible film material, creating a lifelike minnow profile with near-neutral buoyancy. Mimics sardina and small baitfish. The go-to Los Roques bonefish pattern in pearl and grey, sizes 2 and 6, retrieved steadily through sardina-feeding flats.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com product photo — clean side-profile shot on white/neutral background

regional_usage.notes: Routinely cited as the #1 bonefish fly for Los Roques by multiple outfitters (Feather Craft, Salar Flies) because Roques bonefish actively hunt sardina schools in shallow water rather than feeding solely on crustaceans — behaviour unique in the Caribbean and perfectly matched by this soft Sili-Skin baitfish; sizes 2 and 6, pearl and grey are standard.

Named explicitly in Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras tarpon fly list; the soft-plastic-look Gummy Minnow works for tarpon in the clear-water channels and on jacks that follow migrating baitfish along the Mosquitia coast.

patterns.name: Gym Sock
patterns.description: A translucent mullet-imitating streamer by Fulling Mill built with hollow synthetic fibres that collapse when wet, producing a lifelike mullet silhouette with minimal water resistance. Listed as a top-five must-have GT and roosterfish pattern by Big Y Fly Co and Australian retailers. Stripped fast through GT feeding lanes at Ningaloo, Exmouth, and Indo-Pacific reef systems.
patterns.image_source: bigtimeflies.com — Gym Sock 4/0 product photo

regional_usage.notes: Translucent mullet-imitating streamer listed among top-5 must-have patterns for GTs and roosterfish by Big Y Fly Co; recommended by multiple Australian fly shops for tropical Indo-Pacific GT fishing.

patterns.name: Half and Half
patterns.description: Bob Clouser's hybrid of his Clouser Minnow front and a Deceiver rear — dumbbell eyes up front flip the hook point skyward while rear bucktail and hackle trail like a large baitfish. Sinks quickly in current, ideal for big stripers holding in deep rip seams at Monomoy, Montauk, and Cape Hatteras. Strip in long, fast pulls to trigger predatory strikes.
patterns.image_source: Orvis News editorial photo of the Half and Half — clean, well-lit angled view

regional_usage.notes: Clouser's hybrid pattern in menhaden colors is an effective all-rounder for OBX winter stripers and bluefish in the Cape Hatteras surf, and for false albacore working Cape Lookout rips.

Combines the profile of Lefty's Deceiver with the sinking jigging action of the Clouser Deep Minnow; a go-to multi-species saltwater baitfish pattern covering all of Costa Rica's inshore species from roosterfish to tripletail.

Combines Deceiver profile with Clouser jigging action; used for tarpon and snook in the mixed-depth canal systems of Tortuguero and Parismina where variable water depth requires a fly that works at multiple levels.

Multi-species baitfish that combines Deceiver profile and Clouser jigging action; recommended by Bocas del Toro guides for both tarpon and the large snook that hold in the mangrove-and-coral channel edges of the archipelago.

patterns.name: Heavy Gabon Deceiver
patterns.description: Lefty's Deceiver scaled for Gabon's powerful surf and estuary currents. Extra-long white/olive saddle hackles, Flashabou lateral line, and lead-wrap or tungsten core on 4/0–6/0 achieve the sink rate needed in the Sette Cama surf. Targets Atlantic tarpon, giant threadfin, and cubera snapper; the undulating tail remains effective in strong current.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants — Deceiver HD Salt

regional_usage.notes: Lefty's Deceiver profile tied on 4/0–6/0 with extra-long saddle hackle and lead wraps or tungsten core; the extreme surf and deep estuary channels of Sette Cama demand heavier construction than standard Caribbean tarpon Deceivers. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Lefty's Deceiver' — Gabon heavy variant noted.

patterns.name: Hollow Fleye
patterns.description: Bob Popovics's hollow bucktail construction technique stacks loose clumps of hair in a layered cone around the hook shank, building a large, air-trapping body that collapses and re-inflates on each strip. Despite matching a 6–8-inch bunker profile, it casts lighter than it looks. Dominant striper fly from the Canal to Montauk; also fished for Baja tuna and billfish.
patterns.image_source: All Points Fly Shop — Bucktail Hollow Fleye editorial product photo, sharp and well-lit

regional_usage.notes: Popovics's large-profile hollow fly on 4/0–6/0 hooks is among the few castable patterns suited for school-class bluefin tuna encountered off Cape Hatteras when they surface on bunker and herring.

Bob Popovics's hollow synthetic baitfish pattern casts easily despite its large profile and holds its shape under repeated strikes; a go-to pattern for teased billfish and bluewater tuna off Baja's Pacific and Sea of Cortez coasts.

Large (15–20 cm) Hollow Fleye in white/olive or sardine colours on 4/0–6/0; the Hollow Fleye's wide body profile and minimal drag make it effective when cast to crashing GT schools over Nosy Be's offshore banks. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Hollow Fleye'.

Large white/olive Hollow Fleye for GT and dogtooth tuna around Pacific seamounts and reef drop-offs; the Solomons' exceptionally pristine marine environment supports very large fish that respond to substantial baitfish profiles. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Hollow Fleye'.

patterns.name: Hot-Legs Crazy Charlie
patterns.description: Cayman Islands variant of the classic Crazy Charlie, developed by Fish-Bones Fly Fishing (Grand Cayman). Distinguishing feature is orange-tipped rubber legs that add movement in the micro-currents of sand-and-grass flats. Sparse body and bead-chain eyes ensure a fast, quiet sink for bone-sensitive fish. The go-to pattern for Cayman's resident bonefish, particularly in mixed-substrate conditions.
patterns.image_source: No specific Hot-Legs Crazy Charlie image found; Fish-Bones Cayman website not accessible; generic Crazy Charlie available but not an exact match

regional_usage.notes: Cayman-specific variant of the Crazy Charlie with orange-tipped rubber legs for mixed sand-and-grass flats; sparse body ensures fast sink and soft landing.

patterns.name: Indo-Pacific Triggerfish Crab
patterns.description: A small (size 4–6), low-profile coral-rubble crab imitation with a point-up keel hook, rubber legs, and suede claws, designed to land softly on sand without spooking. Fished on a dead-drift to tailing titan, Picasso, and yellow-margin triggerfish on Maldives flats at Huvadhoo Atoll and similar Indo-Pacific reef systems. The keel hook minimises snag on coral substrate.
patterns.image_source: flyfishingmaldives.com — crab fly for Maldives triggerfish and permit

regional_usage.notes: Small (size 4–6), low-profile coral-crab imitation with keel hook (point-up), rubber legs, and suede claws; the Maldives hosts multiple triggerfish species (titan, Picasso, yellow-margin) that are a signature fly fishing target on sandy and coral flats at Huvadhoo Atoll.

patterns.name: Isla Blanca Killer
patterns.description: Locally tied Honduras crab imitation for permit on the Bay Islands' clear-water sand and coral flats. Rubber legs, foam or hard body in tan/olive, and bead-chain eyes on #2–#6 produce a slow fall. Photographed in the Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras fly box gallery. Presented ahead of tailing permit, then stripped slowly across the bottom.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; Honduras local guide pattern not commercially photographed

regional_usage.notes: Listed in the Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras fly box photo gallery as 'Crab Fly Isla Blanca Killer #2, 4, 6'; a locally tied crab pattern used for permit on the clear-water sand and coral flats of the Bay Islands.

patterns.name: James Sand Prawn
patterns.description: Large sand-prawn imitation on #4 hook by Alphonse guide James Christmas, featuring a mono loop-and-bead weedguard and sound-generating bead clacker. The rattle and bulk attract multiple bonefish simultaneously on schooling fish. Classified as a Seychelles bonefish and permit staple, it translates directly to Maldivian and Rodrigues flats where similar sand prawns dominate forage.
patterns.image_source: No specific James Sand Prawn product image found in retail databases (SaltFlyPro, BigTimeFLies, Flycastaway) — specialist Alphonse pattern with limited commercial distribution

regional_usage.notes: Large sand-prawn imitation on #4 with mono loop/bead weed guard and sound-generating features; designed by Alphonse guide James Christmas; classified as a Seychelles staple that transfers directly to Maldives flats where similar sand prawns are key bonefish forage.

Large sand-prawn pattern widely recommended for the big bonefish of St Brandon's; the sound-generating bead loop feature is particularly effective for attracting multiple bonefish simultaneously on schooling fish.

patterns.name: KIFF Pop Star
patterns.originator: KIFF Flies (designed for Seychelles guides, c. 2018)
patterns.description: A large foam-and-PVC rattle popper designed by KIFF Flies at the request of Seychelles GT guides, prioritising easy casting over maximum head size. The internal rattle chamber adds sound displacement to the surface commotion. Listed in the Complete Seychelles Fly Assortment and directly applicable to Maldives GT and Madagascar queenfish in choppy Mozambique Channel conditions.
patterns.image_source: nervouswater.com.au — KIFF PopStar Poppers official product photo

regional_usage.notes: Large foam/PVC rattle popper designed at Seychelles guide request for easy casting and maximum water displacement; directly applicable to Maldives GT fishing and listed in the Complete Seychelles Fly Assortment; highly castable on 8 wt.
High-visibility rattle popper used by Indian Ocean GT guides on both the Seychelles and Madagascar; the extra water-moving action suits the choppier conditions of the Mozambique Channel.

patterns.name: Kinky Muddler (large sand eel/baitfish)
patterns.description: A muddler-style baitfish pattern tied with kinky synthetic fiber (Kinky Fibre or similar) over a spun deer-hair head. Tied large on 4/0–6/0 hooks to imitate sand eels or adult bunker for bluefin tuna and stripers. The muddler head pushes water and creates turbulence. Cast into breaking fish or trolled to the transom on bluewater runs.
patterns.image_source: California Fly Fisher magazine at-the-vise feature photo of finished Kinky Muddler

regional_usage.notes: Large kinky-muddler-style flies on 4/0–6/0 hooks tied to imitate sand eels or bunker are a verified bluefin tuna pattern for the OBX winter fishery, as documented by Cape Cod and Outer Banks tuna fly anglers.

patterns.name: Kraken Crab
patterns.originator: Alphonse Fishing Company / Blue Safari guides (Seychelles)
patterns.description: Crustacean imitation covering crabs, hermit crabs, and coral invertebrates for Indian Ocean reef species. Marabou or rubber legs in olive, dark brown, tan, or white on #2–#4 with a sculpted foam carapace. Developed by Alphonse Fishing Co./Blue Safari guides as a cross-over triggerfish, bonefish, and permit pattern. Presented dead-drift or with a slow creeping retrieve.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; Seychelles guide fly with limited commercial distribution

regional_usage.notes: Unspecific crustacean imitation that covers crabs, hermit crabs, and coral invertebrates in olive, dark brown, tan, and white; cross-over Indian Ocean trigger/bonefish pattern carried by Nubian-bound anglers.

patterns.name: Kung Fu Crab
patterns.description: Rubber-legged crab on #2–4, listed by Fly Fishing Caribe Guanaja as a dedicated permit pattern for the Bay Islands. Articulated rubber legs produce constant movement with minimal angler input — essential for spooky Honduras permit. Fished with a dead-sink presentation ahead of tailing fish in the Bay Islands and Mosquitia region.
patterns.image_source: No product image found; Fly Fishing Caribe website returned no imagery; not present in US retail fly shop databases searched

regional_usage.notes: Specifically listed on the Fly Fishing Caribe Guanaja Honduras fly image gallery as a dedicated permit pattern on #4 and #2 hooks; the Kung Fu Crab's rubber-leg mobility is well-suited for the active permit schools of the Bay Islands.

patterns.name: Kwan
patterns.description: Steve Farrar's hybrid shrimp-crab tied with craft fur and palmered hackle that lands with an ultra-soft splash ideal for spooky fish. Extremely slow sink rate suits the ultra-shallow Laguna Madre and Louisiana duck ponds. Present to tailing redfish and let it settle; hackle fibers flutter naturally without stripping. The defining Lower Laguna Madre sight-fishing pattern.
patterns.image_source: Orlando Outfitters — Foxy Kwan variant product photo on white background

regional_usage.notes: A cross between a shrimp and crab tied with craft fur and palmered hackle; its slow sink rate and soft landing make it ideal for skinny-water marsh fishing in Louisiana's duck ponds and oyster reefs.

The defining pattern of the Lower Laguna Madre sight-fishing game; its super-slow sink rate and minimal splash on landing are ideal for presenting to tailing redfish on the hyper-saline, gin-clear Laguna flats.
A go-to staple recommended by Bonefish Hawaii guides; its crab/shrimp hybrid silhouette represents Hawaiian bonefish food well across varied bottom colors and depths.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Low-profile shrimp/crab hybrid that sinks slowly and lands quietly, ideal for spooky Mosquito Lagoon reds on ultra-clear flats — already in library.
Quiet-landing, slow-sink shrimp/crab that presents perfectly to tailing reds on hard-bottom SC flood-tide flats — already in library.
Quiet-landing shrimp/crab that presents cleanly to GA tailing reds in shallow water; functions well in both muddy and clear-water GA tidal conditions — already in library.

patterns.name: Large Mullet Imitation (White/Tan Baitfish)
patterns.description: A 15–18 cm (6–7 inch) white or tan baitfish tied on heavy 4/0–5/0 hooks to imitate the finger mullet that Costa Rican and Nicaraguan tarpon crash at the surface. Craft fur, bucktail, or synthetic over a wide hook gap with flash underwing. Confirmed by Pointer Fly Fishing and Tapam Lodge as the primary surface pattern when jungle tarpon are visibly busting mullet schools.
patterns.image_source: No specific named-pattern photo found; pattern is a descriptive category rather than a named commercial fly

regional_usage.notes: When tarpon are in a mullet-feeding frenzy at Barra del Colorado, guides recommend 15–18 cm (6–7 inch) white or tan baitfish flies on heavy hooks — Pointer Fly Fishing / Tapam Lodge trip reports confirm these as the primary pattern class when fish are visibly busting bait at the surface.

Pointer Fly Fishing / Tapam Lodge reports confirm that 15–18 cm (6–7 inch) white/tan baitfish with flash are the primary pattern when Nicaragua's Río Indio tarpon are visibly crushing mullet schools near the surface.

patterns.name: Large Pink Shrimp
patterns.description: Oversized shrimp imitation 12–15 cm in pink/coral on 2/0–4/0 matching the large shrimp species in Nicaragua's Río San Juan system. Tapam Lodge guides cite pink as the top color in clear water. Fished on intermediate lines with strip-pause retrieve; Nicaragua tarpon feed heavily on large shrimp in current-swept Atlantic-outlet channels.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; Nicaragua regional guide pattern not commercially photographed

regional_usage.notes: Pointer Fly Fishing Tapam Lodge reports specifically cite pink as the favorite shrimp color in clear water and black/purple in colored water; Nicaragua's shrimp are 5–6 inches long, requiring a much larger pattern than typical flats shrimp flies.

patterns.name: LC Fiddler (Lowcountry Fiddler Crab)
patterns.description: EP-fiber fiddler crab imitation designed by John H. Holbrook (Beaufort, SC, circa 2007) specifically for flood-tide tailing redfish on Lowcountry hard-bottom flats. The EP body captures the fiddler's distinct asymmetric claw silhouette. Holbrook's primary spring-to-summer pattern, dead-dropped or barely twitched ahead of tailing reds gorging on flats-edge fiddler crabs.
patterns.image_source: No specific LC Fiddler image found; local Beaufort SC guide pattern with minimal commercial photography or retail listings

regional_usage.notes: EP-fiber fiddler crab imitation developed in Beaufort, SC specifically for flood-tide tailing reds on Lowcountry hard-bottom flats; Holbrook's go-to from spring through summer when crabs dominate stomach contents.
The SC-originated Holbrook fiddler crab is used throughout Georgia coastal waters by guides who follow identical spartina-flat fiddler-crab fishing tactics.

patterns.name: LC Shrimp (Lowcountry Shrimp)
patterns.description: Designed by John H. Holbrook in Beaufort, SC (c. 2006), the Lowcountry Shrimp uses a root-beer bucktail wing over an Estaz chenille body to imitate the grass shrimp abundant in South Carolina marshes during late summer and fall. Fished on an erratic strip-and-pause through spartina grass edges and oyster bar margins for redfish and spotted seatrout.
patterns.image_source: YouTube — Low Country Shrimp fly tying tutorial video still

regional_usage.notes: Root-beer bucktail and Estaz shrimp designed in Beaufort, SC to match late-summer and fall grass-shrimp abundance in SC marshes; complements the LC Fiddler Crab in Holbrook's four-fly seasonal rotation.

patterns.name: Lee's Ghost Shrimp
patterns.description: Dron Lee's translucent ghost-shrimp imitation designed specifically for the clear, sight-fishing conditions of Abaco's Marls. Built with sparse, pale synthetic fibers over bead-chain eyes, the fly lands softly and sinks slowly — critical for Abaco's notoriously spooky bonefish. Fished on a dead-slow strip-pause retrieve ahead of tailing or cruising fish; the translucent body vanishes in the water column the way real ghost shrimp do.
patterns.image_source: SaltyFlyTying.com — Bonefish Flies Abaco eBook chapter preview

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Verified Abaco-specific pattern in the 'Bonefish Flies Abaco' ebook by tier Dron Lee; a translucent ghost-shrimp imitation suited to the clear-water, sight-fishing conditions of Abaco's Marls.

patterns.name: Lefty's Deceiver
patterns.description: Lefty Kreh's late-1950s non-fouling bucktail-and-hackle baitfish pattern — the foundational saltwater fly. Long saddle hackle tails extend the profile while the bucktail collar prevents fouling. Tied from size 2 to 5/0 in dozens of color schemes for every saltwater species from bonefish to sailfish. Strip at any speed; the go-to searching pattern on every saltwater flat and rip.
patterns.image_source: Wikipedia Commons — high-resolution photo of Lefty's Deceiver, clean white background, classic example

regional_usage.notes: Kreh's foundational baitfish imitation is a go-to for Andros barracuda and jack crevalle on the flats, and works as a searching pattern for juvenile tarpon in creeks; its non-fouling design is essential for windy Andros conditions.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: On Acklins and Long Island the Deceiver tied on heavy-wire hooks with a stinger loop is the standard for the large resident barracuda population; Getaway Fly Fishing recommends baitfish flies for cuda and sharks on these flats.

Kreh spent formative years guiding Keys waters where this pattern became the universal baitfish imitation; the yellow-over-red Deceiver is a classic Keys tarpon search fly and reliable for barracuda and jacks.

The Deceiver's non-fouling design makes it ideal for casting under mangroves in the Everglades backcountry; a standard searching pattern for snook and juvenile tarpon in the 10,000 Islands and Whitewater Bay.
Universal baitfish pattern listed for tarpon, jacks, and barracuda at El Pescador and Turneffe Flats; white/chartreuse and blue/white are the dominant Belize colors.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Pesca Maya recommends Deceivers in contrasting colors as subsurface tarpon and snook patterns; white/chartreuse effective for baby tarpon in the Sian Ka'an mangrove lagoons.
Fishmaster recommends Deceivers on hooks 1/0–3/0 in tan, chartreuse, black, and purple for JDR tarpon and snook; versatile baitfish profile effective across Cuba's species.
A versatile baitfish imitation for OBX species; in olive-over-white it imitates the mullet and menhaden that draw large red drum into Pamlico Sound and stripers to the Cape Hatteras surf in winter.
Lefty Kreh's classic bucktail-and-hackle streamer imitates the pogies and mullet that congregate in Louisiana's marsh passes and river mouths, triggering aggressive redfish and trout strikes.
Tied in mullet and shad color schemes, the Deceiver covers the pass and jetty structure along the Texas coast where big trout, redfish, and jacks ambush migrating baitfish.
Tied large (3/0 to 5/0) in white-and-tan sardine colors, Lefty's Deceiver remains a proven beach-fished roosterfish pattern in Baja, covering the full range of baitfish sizes roosters target.
Used throughout Hawaii for reef and blue-water edge species; large white-and-yellow Deceivers are standard GT and barracuda searching patterns.

Crocodile Bay Resort specifically recommends big Bucktail Deceivers for roosterfish targeting sardine-bait schools near rocky structure; also the primary fly for large Pacific snook in tidal river mouths.

Universal Caribbean baitfish imitation; white and chartreuse/white are standard for barracuda and jacks along reef edges and channels, while larger versions (sizes 2/0-4/0) are carried for tarpon shots in the channels off Gran Roque.
Large white-and-blue Deceivers match the sardine schools that pile up against the Hallaniyat cliffs; queenfish in particular are aggressive surface strikers on this classic streamer.
Large white-and-chartreuse Deceiver for bait-and-switch sailfish on fly during Bazaruto's winter sailfish season (May–September); also effective on queenfish and GT over the channel reefs.

Library universal (existing #81); Hastings Fly Fishers Australia list Deceivers among core GT flies, and Australian saltwater guides routinely carry 4/0–6/0 versions in white and chartreuse for queenfish and mahi in the Ningaloo bluewater.

Library universal (existing #81); the Deceiver in large 4/0–6/0 sizes is a standard carry on PNG GT skiffs targeting reef-edge GTs, dogtooth tuna, and the mangrove jack found around PNG's coastal mangrove systems.

Library universal (existing #81); large 4/0–6/0 Deceivers are standard on Indo-Pacific GT fly lists; documented as an effective bluewater baitfish imitation for dogtooth tuna and pelagic GT around Raja Ampat's offshore reef drops.
Standard cuda and tarpon baitfish presentation for Cayman reef edges; the Fish-Bones site confirms barracuda and tarpon as key Cayman species alongside bonefish.
Versatile baitfish pattern for the barracuda, tarpon (occasionally), and jack crevalle that share Bonaire's lagoons and reef edges with bonefish.
White/chartreuse Deceiver is a standard snook and barracuda pattern for Boca Paila mangrove channels and lagoon drop-offs; also takes juvenile tarpon.

Versatile baitfish profile used for tarpon and large snook in the Río Colorado and Parismina river mouths; white/chartreuse is the dominant color for mullet-imitating presentations in turbid Caribbean water.
Versatile baitfish profile used for both tarpon and large snook; Tapam Lodge guide notes confirm tan/white and chartreuse/white Deceivers as standard for Nicaragua's clearer water lagoon episodes.

Named explicitly in Fly Fishing Caribe's Bocas del Toro fly image list as 'Wet Fly Deceiver #2/0, 3/0, 4/0'; essential for the large tarpon in the river mouths of the Changuinola, San San, and Sixaola rivers that border Costa Rica.

Multi-species baitfish used for tarpon, snook, and cubera snapper at Cayo Cruz; the hotel channel at Cayo Romano has daily tarpon and jack schools within casting range of the dock, where Deceivers in white/chartreuse produce effectively.
All-round baitfish deceiver used throughout Tampa Bay for pass snook, tarpon on the beaches, and schooling jacks; white/chartreuse is the standard SW Florida color — already in library.

patterns.name: Longfin Jack Streamer
patterns.description: Medium baitfish streamer (8–12 cm) in white/olive or tan imitating engraulids that sustain Gabon's jack and tarpon populations. CF Blend or bucktail on 2/0–3/0 with minimal dressing for a slim, fast-sinking profile. Cast into crashing bird schools over the Ndogo lagoon; retrieved fast with short, sharp strips to imitate a fleeing baitfish.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; Gabon regional streamer without commercial identity

regional_usage.notes: Medium-sized (8–12 cm) CF-Blend or bucktail streamer in white/olive or tan, cast into bait-crashing bird schools in the Ndogo lagoon where longfin and crevalle jacks are primary targets alongside the tarpon program.

patterns.name: Los Roques Minnow
patterns.description: Destination-specific sardina imitation sold by Fulling Mill for Los Roques bonefish in grey and green, sizes 2 and 6. Mimics the small baitfish that Los Roques bonefish actively hunt in shallow water — an unusual predatory behavior for Caribbean bonefish. Stripped steadily to imitate fleeing sardina through sandy flats.
patterns.image_source: Fulling Mill official product photo — clean neutral-background studio shot of the named pattern

regional_usage.notes: A named destination-specific fly sold commercially by Fulling Mill expressly for Los Roques in grey/pearl in sizes 2 and 6; designed to imitate the sardina baitfish that Roques bonefish hunt, reflecting the unique predatory baitfish-feeding behaviour of bonefish at this location that differs from most Caribbean destinations.

patterns.name: Los Roques Tarpon Minnow
patterns.description: Larger companion to the Los Roques Minnow, sized 1/0, sold by Fulling Mill in their Los Roques destination fly selection. Imitates the sardina baitfish on which resident tarpon and jacks feed in deeper channels and flats around Gran Roque. Fished with a fast strip in channels and around current edges.
patterns.image_source: Fulling Mill UK official product photo — clean studio shot of the named Los Roques Tarpon Minnow pattern

regional_usage.notes: Larger companion to the Los Roques Minnow (size 1/0), sold by Fulling Mill in their Los Roques destination selection specifically for targeting tarpon in the channels and deeper flats around Gran Roque; the upscaled baitfish profile matches the small sardina on which resident tarpon feed.

patterns.name: Lowcountry Fiddler Crab (Felt Crab)
patterns.originator: Capt. David Edens (St. Simons Island, GA)
patterns.description: Felt-bodied fiddler crab developed by Capt. David Edens (St. Simons Island, GA) for Georgia marsh fishing. The soft felt body absorbs water to sink slowly and lands nearly silently on ultra-shallow flats — critical for spooky flood-tide redfish within inches of the grass edge. Effective on both flood-tide tailers at St. Simons and Jekyll Island and low-tide edge reds.
patterns.image_source: No image found; local Georgia guide pattern not in commercial retail databases or editorial photography

regional_usage.notes: Felt-bodied fiddler crab developed by Capt. Edens specifically for GA marsh fishing; the soft felt lands nearly silently on ultra-shallow flats and works on both flood-tide and low-tide reds at St. Simons and Jekyll.

patterns.name: Magnetic Minnow
patterns.description: A slim-profile synthetic minnow built with translucent fibers over a weighted shank, designed to be extremely castable into wind. The broad, flat-sided body creates a wide visual profile without bulk. Popular on GT surf opportunities at Seychelles atolls for maximum castability at distance and as a mullet imitation along Baja beaches for roosterfish and jacks.
patterns.image_source: Superflies.com product photo of Magnetic Minnow GT fly, clean background, clear side profile

regional_usage.notes: Slim-profile synthetic minnow praised for castability; field-tested on Alphonse, Farquhar, and Cosmoledo as one of the easiest GT flies to present at distance during fast-moving surf opportunities.

A translucent synthetic mullet pattern with a broad profile that sheds water quickly; documented by Baja guides and anglers as one of the most effective patterns when roosters and jacks are corralling mullet against the shore.
Weighted baitfish pattern cast to cruising GTs and bluefin trevally on deeper flat edges in Sudan; the erratic sink-and-dart action triggers reaction strikes from reef predators.
Weighted EP-style minnow cast into baitball feeding frenzies; the compact profile outcompetes conventional sardine imitations to trigger Oman's aggressive predators.
Compact weighted minnow for the Bazaruto channel edges where fast-moving trevally species ambush baitfish; the fast-sinking profile beats brush flies when fishing deeper water columns.
