Slim-profile synthetic baitfish that casts easily in wind and current; directly applicable to Madagascar's GT and queenfish over reef edges — referenced by Superflies as effective across Indian Ocean GT fisheries including Lakshadweep and Seychelles. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Magnetic Minnow'.
Slim-profile easy-casting GT fly; effective in the strong channel currents of Marovo Lagoon where bulkier brush flies can be hard to control. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Magnetic Minnow'.

patterns.name: Mangrove Jack Deceiver
patterns.description: A medium-weight Lefty's Deceiver variant tied in red/orange or white/red on 1/0–3/0, scaled to match the small baitfish that mangrove jack and spot-tail bass ambush in Solomon Islands river systems. The long saddle hackle tail breathes on the pause and folds tight on the strip. Best presented with a splash-down alongside shaded fallen timber and undercuts in the Varea, Kumabusi, and Gevala rivers.
patterns.image_source: jacksonholeflycompany.com — red/white Deceiver saltwater fly

regional_usage.notes: Medium-weight (1/0–3/0) Deceiver in red/orange or white/red for mangrove jack and spot-tail bass in the Varea, Kumabusi, and Gevala rivers; these river predators smash baitfish patterns stripped through shaded overhangs and fallen structure.

patterns.name: Mantis Shrimp
patterns.description: Imitation of the powerful mantis shrimp, a primary forage on hard-bottom Belize and Yucatan flats. Tied with a segmented dubbed body, articulated claws, and bead-chain eyes. Fish slow and deep; permit tip up and inhale a mantis presented directly ahead of them. Critical for both permit and large bonefish in the Sian Ka'an biosphere.
patterns.image_source: Fish Tales Fly Shop — Ray's V Mantis Shrimp clean product shot on white

regional_usage.notes: Listed in El Pescador and Turneffe Flats fly lists for both permit and bonefish; mantis shrimp are a key food source on Belize's hard-bottom flats.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Palometa Club states mantis shrimp patterns are critically important for Ascension Bay permit as mantis shrimp are a staple food source in the Sian Ka'an biosphere.

patterns.name: Marabou Fleeing Crab
patterns.description: Marabou-wing crab imitation developed by FlyCastaway guides for St Brandon's Atoll. Named in the official FlyCastaway brochure as a signature pattern. Marabou wings breathe and pulse on each strip, imitating a crab paddling to escape. Tied on #2–#4 in tan, olive, or white; highly effective on large, wary Indo-Pacific permit across ultra-clear white sand flats.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; proprietary FlyCastaway guide pattern with no commercial photography found

regional_usage.notes: Named in the official FlyCastaway St Brandon's brochure as a signature St Brandon's pattern; marabou-wing fleeing crab variant developed for the ultra-clear white sand flats and large, wary permit of the atoll.

patterns.name: Marsh Creature
patterns.originator: Capt. Conner Bryant (Tidal Waters Guide Service)
patterns.description: Simple dark-profile streamer of black-and-purple rabbit strip with bead-chain eyes, created by Capt. Conner Bryant (Tidal Waters Guide Service). Designed for summer Lowcountry redfish in stained marsh water where the high-contrast silhouette triggers aggressive strikes in low visibility. Stripped in short erratic pulses along spartina edges and oyster-bar cuts. A low-complexity, high-effectiveness workhorse.
patterns.image_source: No image found; local SC guide pattern not commercially photographed or in retail databases

regional_usage.notes: Simple black-and-purple rabbit-strip attractor with bead-chain eyes, designed specifically for summer Lowcountry reds in stained marsh water where dark profiles trigger aggressive eats.

patterns.name: McCrab
patterns.description: A foam-and-rubber-leg crab pattern with a dense, round profile and articulated legs that undulate on the sink. Listed consistently among permit and bonefish flies by El Pescador lodge for Northern Belize flats. The foam body controls sink rate for shallow turtle-grass presentations; rubber legs provide motion at rest, making the fly convincing when permit circle it before committing. Presented ahead of moving fish and allowed to sink to the bottom.
patterns.image_source: Salty Fly Tying blog — The McCrab fly tying recipe, finished fly photo

regional_usage.notes: Foam-and-rubber-leg crab pattern consistently listed among permit flies by El Pescador lodge on the flats of Northern Belize.
Named by Fly Fishing Caribe in the Guanaja Honduras fly list; foam-and-rubber crab that sits inverted with hook point up, effective for the tailing permit on Honduras's shallow sand-and-grass flats.

patterns.name: McVay Gotcha
patterns.description: Jim McVay's 1980s Bahamian shrimp imitation, a Charlie-variant tied with crystal flash or carpet fiber body and signature pink thread head. Its weighted eyes sink hook-point-up; cast ahead of tailing bonefish and strip with short twitches. The most widely used bonefish pattern across the Bahamas and a standard throughout the Caribbean from the Keys to Cuba and Belize.
patterns.image_source: Finham fly shop product photo — McVay Gotcha in Pink, clear side profile against clean background

regional_usage.notes: Pink-nosed pearl-body bonefish shrimp pattern listed by El Pescador and Turneffe Flats lodges; fishes well in the gin-clear, shallow flats of Northern Belize.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Palometa Club explicitly lists Gotchas among the standard bonefish fly selection for Ascension Bay in sizes #6–#8 for varying bottom structure.

Fishmaster lists the Gotcha alongside Crazy Charlie as a standard Cuba bonefish pattern; Cuba Fishing Outfitters notes it was previously the author's top Cuba bonefish choice before the Ververka Mantis Shrimp.

A universally trusted bonefish shrimp imitation that Christmas Island guides consistently recommend alongside the CXI Special; heavier lead-eye versions work well in the deeper channels near lagoon outlets.

Tied with carpet fibers from an Andros-bound taxi by Jim McVay, this Charlie variation with its signature pink thread head became one of the most widely fished bonefish patterns across all Bahamian flats including Andros.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Angler Adventures describes the Gotcha as 'one of the most effective and most frequently used patterns from Acklins to Abaco'; the pink-nosed Charlie variant is the number-one producer on the big hard-sand flats of these out islands.

A universal Bahamian pattern that translates directly to Keys bonefish on the oceanside flats of Marathon and the Lower Keys; guides use the standard pink-nosed Gotcha alongside more presentation-focused patterns.
Miami-based guide Capt. Raul Montoro (Shallow Tails) lists the Gotcha as a key Biscayne Bay bonefish pattern; the Charlie variation works well on the bay's sandy and grass-bottom flats.
Universally used by Hawaii-bound bonefish anglers as a proven starter pattern; the pearl body and small bead-chain eyes land softly on spooky Hawaiian flats.

Confirmed as the single most reliable bonefish pattern at Los Roques by multiple outfitters and trip reports; the pearl-and-gold version on a size 6 hook fished with a strip-strip-pause retrieve dominates the pancake flats — larger sizes (4) are appropriate for the above-average bonefish averaging 4-8 lb.
Arguably the single most-recommended Bahamas bonefish fly; pearl mylar body and pink nose excel on Bimini's light sand bottom in sizes #2-#4 for big fish.
Explicitly recommended by The Sands resort and multiple T&C guides as the single best fly for Provo bonefish — tan and pink colorways in #2-#6.
Cayman fish have seen heavy Gotcha pressure on guided flats; still effective on fresh fish and in deeper water where presentation distance reduces spooking.
The most recommended DIY bonefish fly worldwide; tan and pearl variants in #4-#6 with varied bead-chain weight are the essential Bonaire flat staple.
Standard flat-fly across all Yucatan bonefish venues; tan, pearl, and pink variants in #4-#8 with bead-chain eyes are the reliable first choice for Boca Paila bonefish.

Standard bonefish shrimp listed by Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras alongside the Crazy Charlie; pearl-body pink-nosed design effective for the large resident bonefish that patrol Guanaja's extensive flats.

Standard Gotcha variant (tungsten and bead chain) in tan/pink confirmed in the Seychelles Fly Assortment for Indian Ocean bonefish; direct transfer to the large, eager St Brandon's bonefish population. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'McVay Gotcha'.

patterns.name: Meko Special
patterns.description: Created by Grand Bahama guide Omeko Glinton, the Meko Special uses a neutral tan body with a palmered hackle collar that triggers over both light sand and dark marl without switching flies. The versatile profile suits Bimini's mixed flats and Turks & Caicos DIY anglers covering multiple bottom types. Fished with short erratic strips in the 'shot-and-drop' bonefish presentation style.
patterns.image_source: globalflyfisher.com — Meko Special bonefish fly pattern photo

regional_usage.notes: Created by Grand Bahama guide Omeko Glinton; neutral tan body with palmered hackle works across dark and light bottoms without switching flies — well-suited to Bimini's mixed flats.
Designed to work across all bottom colors without fly changes — ideal for DIY T&C anglers moving between sand flats, turtle grass, and marl.

patterns.name: Merkin Crab (Long Arm)
patterns.description: Del Brown's Merkin — the original Florida Keys permit crab — uses clipped wool or yarn trimmed to a disk shape with rubber-hackle legs and weighted bead eyes. The Long Arm variant extends one or two legs for added movement and visual cue. Allows a slow, controlled sink. Fished dead-drift ahead of tailing permit on sandy and grass flats in Cuba and the Keys.
patterns.image_source: Orvis product photo — Merkin Crab permit fly, clean professional image on white

regional_usage.notes: Fishmaster lists the 'Merkin long arm crab' as one of the core permit patterns for JDR; weighted yarn crab works well on Cuba's varied sandy and grass flats.

patterns.name: Milkfish Plankton Fly
patterns.description: Algae-and-plankton imitation by Saltwater Flies Australia for surface-feeding milkfish. Tied on #4–#8 in green/chartreuse with UV-reactive thread and sparse hackle fibers imitating zooplankton. Presented well ahead of a cruising milkfish on Exmouth Gulf or Cape York west coast flats; held stationary or barely twitched in the surface film.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants — Milkfish Snack (Gerbec)

regional_usage.notes: Algae-and-plankton imitation in green tones with UV hotspot produced by Saltwater Flies Australia specifically for Australian milkfish; Exmouth Gulf has documented milkfish populations on the flats.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: SWFA-produced algae-plankton imitation documented for Cape York milkfish; The Flyfisher Australia references milkfish at Cape York's west coast and this is the most commercially available Australian-produced milkfish fly.

patterns.name: Milkfish Snack
patterns.description: An algae and plankton imitation distributed by Umpqua Feather Merchants for Hawaii's surface-feeding milkfish (awa). Built with Krystal Flash and sheep's fleece to mimic floating algae mats. Near-neutral buoyancy keeps it in the feeding zone. Fished dead-drift or with minimal movement in harbor and bay feeding areas where awa school at the surface.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants official product photo — clean white-background product shot of the named pattern

regional_usage.notes: A Krystal Flash and sheep's fleece algae/plankton imitation with near-neutral buoyancy; suited to Hawaii's surface-feeding awa schools in harbors and bays.

Near-neutrally-buoyant plankton/algae imitation dead-drifted in the current; Mozambique's Bazaruto channels and scum-lines hold milkfish seasonally and this Umpqua-tied pattern is the most commercially available option.

patterns.name: Milky Dream
patterns.description: Arno Matthee's milkfish-specific algae imitation, tied in olive, green, and chartreuse with UV flash strands to mimic the copepod-rich algae mats milkfish filter feed on. One of a handful of proven milkfish patterns globally. Fished dead-drift or with the slowest possible strip in feeding lanes. Endorsed by Alphonse Fishing Co. for Seychelles milkfish.
patterns.image_source: Mt. Yonder Fly Fishing product photo of FS Milky Dream, clean white background, excellent profile view

regional_usage.notes: Olive, green, and chartreuse algae imitation with strands of UV flash to mimic copepods; one of the few proven patterns for the milkfish that cruise outside the Christmas Island lagoon.

Top-tier milkfish pattern endorsed by IGFA and Alphonse Fishing Co.; the olive-green-chartreuse algae body with UV flash imitates the copepod-rich algae beds that Seychelles milkfish actively feed on.
The definitive milkfish fly worldwide; a plankton/algae foam-and-CDC imitation used wherever awa are surface-feeding in Hawaiian harbors, bays, and windward flats.
Olive-green-chartreuse algae imitation; the most-referenced milkfish pattern for Indian Ocean flats including the Nubian Shambaya flat where milkfish are encountered tailing through turtle-grass.
Fly Odyssey exploratory trips confirmed huge milkfish in the Hallaniyat weed lines; the Milky Dream, pioneered in the Seychelles, is the baseline algae-imitation pattern for these fish worldwide.

The standard plankton/algae-imitating milkfish fly for the Indian Ocean; used across Maldives, Seychelles, and Christmas Island for surface-feeding milkfish schools. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Milky Dream'.
Milkfish are present at St Brandon's Atoll; the Milky Dream plankton imitation is the standard fly used across Indian Ocean milkfish fisheries. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Milky Dream'.

patterns.name: Millhouse Tarpon Shrimp
patterns.description: Andy Mill's shrimp-profile tarpon fly, produced commercially by Fulling Mill in tan and olive on a 1/0 hook. Larger, water-moving profile serves as a low-light and early-morning alternative to the Tarpon Toad on Florida Keys flats. Fished with a strip-pause retrieve before tailing or rolling fish.
patterns.image_source: Fulling Mill official product photo — clean studio shot showing the Millhouse Tarpon Shrimp Tan pattern

regional_usage.notes: Andy Mill's shrimp-profile tarpon fly, used as a low-light alternative to his toad pattern, with a larger profile that moves water effectively and excels early in the morning on Keys flats.

patterns.name: Millhouse Tarpon Toad
patterns.description: Andy Mill's tournament-proven Tarpon Toad variant, commercially tied by Fulling Mill on a Gamakatsu SL12s. Features a palmered foam and synthetic toad body that pushes water and breathes on the strip. Favored by the most decorated Gold Cup Tarpon Tournament winner for clear-water Florida Keys flats presentations.
patterns.image_source: Red's Fly Fishing shop product photo — named Millhouse Tarpon Toad by Fulling Mill, clear fly photo

regional_usage.notes: Andy Mill's tournament-proven version of the Tarpon Toad, tied on a Gamakatsu SL12s and commercially produced by Fulling Mill; favored by Mill — the most decorated Gold Cup Tarpon Tournament winner — for clear-water Keys flats.

Toad variant tied for the Tampa Bay rolling-school tarpon fishery; the bulky profile displaces water and produces side-to-side swimming action that provokes reaction strikes from large migratory tarpon — already in library.

patterns.name: Mushmouth
patterns.description: Dave Skok's soft-silicone baitfish creating a translucent, jelly-like silhouette that matches small bay anchovies precisely. No hard body or flash — the subdued profile unlocks lock-jawed false albacore keyed on tiny baitfish. Fish on an intermediate line with a steady two-inch strip. The go-to Cape Cod and Montauk albie fly when fish refuse flashier patterns.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants — Mushmouth official product photo on white background

regional_usage.notes: Oversized Mushmouth-style flies on heavy hooks are among the accessible bluefin tuna fly patterns for the winter OBX offshore fishery when tuna are feeding near the surface on sand eels or bunker.

patterns.name: Needlefish
patterns.description: A long, slender baitfish imitation in fluorescent green, yellow, or white, tied to replicate the profile of actual needlefish — primary forage for barracuda in Caribbean and Cuban waters. Typically rigged with a short wire trace to prevent bite-offs. Stripped at maximum speed along reef edges and channels; the fast, straight retrieve imitates a fleeing needlefish and triggers the barracuda's reflexive ambush strike.
patterns.image_source: Reel Flies — Needlefish Fly Aqua Green, clean product photo

regional_usage.notes: Fluorescent green/yellow slender profile needlefish imitation; El Pescador recommends it for Turneffe's abundant barracuda when stripped very fast to trigger predatory strikes.
Long, slender white or green/yellow profile pattern for JDR's abundant barracuda; typically rigged with a short wire trace and stripped at high speed along the reef edges.
Slender green/white profile fly for the jacks and cubera snapper that cruise the coral reef edges of the Bocas del Toro archipelago; stripped fast along structure to trigger reaction strikes.

patterns.name: Norman's Crab
patterns.description: Simple rabbit-fur and Sililegs crab or mantis shrimp imitation developed by Dr. Aaron Adams (Bonefish & Tarpon Trust). Endorsed by Hawaii flats guides for Hawaiian bonefish and permit. Produces subtle leg movement with minimal retrieve, matching the bottom-hugging crabs and shrimp that Hawaiian bonefish forage on.
patterns.image_source: BonefishHawaii.com — video still specifically captioned 'Norman's Crab' in context of Hawaii bonefish flies

regional_usage.notes: A simple rabbit-and-Sililegs crab/mantis imitation endorsed by Hawaii guides as effective on Hawaiian flats due to its subtle movement with minimal stripping action.

patterns.name: Nubian Spaghetti
patterns.originator: Robert Pljuscec / Wild Sea Expedition (December 2020, Shambaya Flat, Sudan)
patterns.description: Ultra-chenille worm with dumbbell eyes and rabbit-fur tail born on Shambaya Flat, Sudan (December 2020) during a Wild Sea Expedition milkfish session. Originator Robert Pljuscec pivoted after a failed milkfish attempt; on first morning use, the Spaghetti proved immediately deadly on tailing yellowmargin and titan triggerfish. Slow strip across rubble and sand; also attracted milkfish.
patterns.image_source: No image found; brand-new regional pattern from a single expedition with no commercial photography or retail presence

regional_usage.notes: Born on the Nubian flats during a failed milkfish session; an ultra-chenille worm with dumbbells and rabbit fur that proved immediately deadly on tailing triggers — and attracted milkfish — on its first outing the next morning.

patterns.name: NYAP (Not Your Average Popper)
patterns.description: Guide James Christmas's high-impact foam popper engineered specifically for giant trevally on Indo-Pacific atolls. Its domed foam head creates maximum surface disturbance on each strip while remaining aerodynamically castable on large rods. Black is the preferred color for Christmas Island and Seychelles GT. Strip with fast, aggressive pulls along reef edges and flat margins.
patterns.image_source: Bear's Den Fly Fishing Co. product photo — NYAP popper on clean white background, clear profile

regional_usage.notes: Designed by Alphonse/Christmas Island guide James Christmas, this foam popper creates maximum surface disturbance while remaining easy to cast; black is the preferred color for Christmas Island GTs.

Designed on the outer Seychelles atolls by Alphonse guide James Christmas; revolutionized GT popper fishing by combining castability with maximum surface disturbance, now a standard on all Seychelles GT skiffs.

Fulling Mill's simple foam popper is documented as effective for Baja roosterfish in the 'Light' color variant; its durable, aggressive profile triggers reaction strikes from surface-hunting roosters working beach breaks.
Black is the preferred color for GT in Hawaii, matching the dark-background reef environment; the foam popper creates the surface commotion needed to draw aggressive ulua strikes.

Large foam-faced popper with foam collar; excellent for teasing roosterfish on Costa Rica Pacific beaches — roosterfish can be raised to a hookless teaser popper in the same fashion as billfish, then switched to the fly.
Foam popper for surface-crashing GT sessions on the coral reef crests and island points of Sudan; queenfish and bluefin trevally also harass surface patterns aggressively at these locations.
Oman's GT fishery was built on surface presentations; a large foam popper replicates conventional GT poppers for anglers who want to bring topwater energy to a fly rod.
Surface popper for GT and queenfish during baitball pack attacks in Bazaruto's deeper reef zones; the visual strike on a surface fly is among the most spectacular experiences this destination offers.
Universal GT surface popper, already in the library (existing #96); included here as a regional tag to confirm it is a standard fly carried on Ningaloo GT skiffs.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Library universal (existing #96); included in the curated GT selection by The Flyfisher Australia and used across all Australian GT destinations including Cape York.

Library universal (existing #96); documented as one of the go-to GT surface poppers for Indo-Pacific destinations including PNG; the aggressive popping action of PNG GTs makes surface poppers essential.

Library universal (existing #96); the surface popper standard for Indo-Pacific GT; Raja Ampat's tropical flats and reef edges hold large GT populations where surface poppers are particularly effective during feeding-tide pushes.

The dominant GT surface popper across all Indo-Pacific GT fisheries; Maldives on the Fly operators recommend it specifically for reef-edge and channel-mouth presentations. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'NYAP'.
Standard Indo-Pacific GT popper; GT at St Brandon's run 40+ inches and the NYAP's large water-displacing profile is essential for aggressive reef-edge presentations. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'NYAP'.

Standard large GT popper; effective on the rocky reef points and lagoon entrances around Nosy Be and the Mitsio Archipelago where surface GT action is the signature experience. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'NYAP'.

Large GT surface popper; with light fishing pressure the Solomon Islands GTs are highly responsive to surface poppers around reef edges, channel points, and bommie drop-offs. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'NYAP'.

patterns.name: Openshaw's Ghost
patterns.description: A translucent mullet imitation produced by Saltwater Flies Australia with a clear silicone body and pale grey-and-white synthetic wing that becomes nearly invisible when wet — hence 'Ghost.' Named and sold by SWFA, explicitly recommended by FlyLife Magazine guide Brett Wolf for Ningaloo Reef GTs and queenfish. The ghostly wet profile is especially effective in the crystal-clear flats of Raja Ampat.
patterns.image_source: saltwaterfliesaustralia.com — Openshaw's Ghost Fly official product photo

regional_usage.notes: Translucent mullet imitation with silicone head that becomes nearly ghostly when wet; named by and sold by Saltwater Flies Australia, explicitly recommended for Ningaloo Reef GTs and queenfish on the flats by FlyLife Magazine guide Brett Wolf.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Translucent Australian mullet imitation (Saltwater Flies Australia); effective on Cape York GT and queenfish on open flats where the ghostly profile matches the small baitfish schools the fish key on.

Australian-produced translucent mullet imitation; the clear-water flats of Raja Ampat's protected bays make the ghost-like profile particularly effective for sight-casting to GTs and bluefin trevally.

patterns.name: Palolo Worm
patterns.description: Jack Gartside's foam-topped palolo worm imitation tied in red or rust-orange on a 1/0–2/0 hook. Designed to ride just below the surface, matching the annual palolo worm hatch on Lower Florida Keys ocean-side flats where tarpon sip worms at the surface. Fished with a dead-drift or very slow creep.
patterns.image_source: jackgartside.com — the originator's own website, specifically titled 'Jack Gartside's Palolo Worm'

regional_usage.notes: A foam-topped subsurface palolo worm imitation tied on a 1/0–2/0 hook in red or rust-orange, designed to match the infamous annual palolo worm hatch on Lower Keys ocean-side flats where tarpon sip worms at the surface.

patterns.name: Paradise Cockroach
patterns.description: A lodge variant of the Cockroach tarpon fly, tied with grizzly and orange saddle hackles over a tan or natural bucktail body on a 1/0–3/0 hook. Designed for baby tarpon in the stained freshwater lakes at Pesca Maya lodge, Ascension Bay. Fished with a slow strip in low-visibility conditions from November through March when tarpon stage in the jungle lagoons.
patterns.image_source: Tail Fly Fishing Magazine — Tarpon Cockroach, high-quality editorial photo of finished fly

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Named tarpon pattern from Pesca Maya lodge's own recommended fly list for baby tarpon in the freshwater lakes at Pesca Maya during November–March stained-water conditions.

Larger, more heavily dressed version of the standard Cockroach with extra grizzly hackle for increased movement; the Atlantic tarpon of West Africa are significantly larger than Caribbean fish and an upsized profile is standard practice at Sette Cama. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Paradise Cockroach'.

patterns.name: Pearl Brush Fly
patterns.description: Flash-heavy pearl EP-brush GT streamer with dense, reflective synthetic fibers creating an overwhelming flash profile in clear Seychelles water. Two-handed long-strip retrieve through the surf and coral edges. Pearl-and-flash outperforms matte colors when light and tide align on Alphonse and Farquhar. Documented by Superflies as an on/off killer for bluefin and giant trevally.
patterns.image_source: Superflies.com — Seychelles GT flies editorial showing pearl/brush flies in context

regional_usage.notes: Flash-heavy pearl EP-brush GT fly documented by Superflies as an on/off killer on Seychelles atolls; when flash conditions align, it outfishes all other patterns on Alphonse and Farquhar.
White / pearl GT brush fly used for bright-light midday conditions on the Nubian outer reef edges where GTs ambush baitfish schools.
White/pearl baitfish brush fished over sardine baitballs matches the natural prey that draws Oman's monster GT into feeding frenzies alongside queenfish and golden trevally.
White/pearl brush fly matches the abundant baitfish (sardines, mullet) that draw GT and queenfish into the Bazaruto channels on the outgoing tide.

patterns.name: Pencil Popper
patterns.description: A slim, cylindrical hard-foam or cork surface popper with a small cupped face, imitating a wounded or fleeing baitfish at the surface. Lighter disturbance than wide-cup poppers — ideal for jack crevalle and barracuda hunting in clearer water off Turneffe's reef edges. Stripped with sharp short pops followed by pauses; the pencil profile creates a subtler splash pattern that doesn't over-spook fish in clear conditions.
patterns.image_source: Louisiana Sportsman editorial photo — Pencil Popper fishing lure/fly

regional_usage.notes: Slim-profile surface popper listed by El Pescador for jack crevalle and provides explosive topwater strikes on Turneffe's reef edges.

patterns.name: Peterson's Spawning Shrimp
patterns.description: A highly realistic bonefish and permit pattern with a rabbit-fur body and extended knotted-fiber legs that simulate a swimming spawning shrimp. Its naturalistic silhouette and translucent materials fool both pressured bonefish and permit across Bahamas, Keys, and Abaco flats. Fish on a dead sink toward the bottom; originator credit is shared between Craig Mathews and Eric Peterson.
patterns.image_source: Red's Fly Fishing product photo of Peterson's Spawning Shrimp — clean side profile

regional_usage.notes: Rabbit-fur body with long extended legs creates exceptional realism; recommended by Andros South lodge in larger sizes for permit encounters and standard sizes for the big Andros bonefish population.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Listed in the SaltyFlyTying 'Bonefish Flies Abaco' ebook by Drew Chicone and Chico Fernandez as one of ten proven Abaco patterns; its rabbit-body realism matches the spawning shrimp prevalent on Abaco's hard-sand bottoms.
Orvis recommends the larger sizes of Peterson's Spawning Shrimp specifically for permit; widely used in the Lower Keys near Key West where permit flats overlap with tarpon migration corridors.
High-confidence Bahamas pattern with reports of 19-fish days; rabbit-fur wing pulses at rest, effective on both Bimini bonefish and the occasional permit.
Effective for both large T&C bonefish and occasional permit; the egg-sac trigger is particularly potent on large, selective bones common on North/Middle Caicos.
Rabbit-fur wing provides natural pulse on shallow weed flats; effective on sight-feeding Bonaire bonefish and carries the egg-sac trigger that consistently produces multiple-fish days.
Effective for both Boca Paila bonefish and permit; the spawning-shrimp trigger is especially relevant in spring and early summer when Caribbean shrimp spawn on Sian Ka'an flats.

Named as 'Peterson's Spawning Crab #1, 2, 4, 6' in the Fly Fishing Caribe Bocas del Toro fly list; the egg-sac shrimp/crab hybrid works for the permit that cruise the clear-water flats away from the turbid river mouths in the archipelago.

patterns.name: Peyote Palolo
patterns.description: Drew Chicone's modern foam palolo worm imitation for Florida Keys tarpon. Creates a visible near-surface wake and skittering action mimicking live worms. Fished year-round on oceanside flats with a two-handed strip retrieve. Also effective in Everglades mangrove channels where tarpon feed opportunistically on worm-like forage.
patterns.image_source: Florida Keys Outfitters shop product photo — clean square-format product image of the named Peyote Palolo Worm

regional_usage.notes: A modern foam palolo worm imitation by Drew Chicone that creates a visible wake and the distinctive near-surface skittering motion of live worms, fished year-round on Keys oceanside flats with a two-handed strip retrieve.

Also fished in the Everglades backcountry for juvenile and migratory tarpon; the foam body and two-handed strip retrieve work effectively in mangrove channels where tarpon feed opportunistically on worm-like forage.

patterns.name: Pillow Talk
patterns.description: Alphonse Island guide Wayne Haselau designed this shrimp pattern to land softly and sink slowly over the vast tidal flats of the Seychelles. A puffy EP-fiber or craft-fur body with bead-chain eyes and a splayed fiber tail reads as a translucent shrimp in the water column. Accounts for the majority of bonefish landed at Alphonse; also taken by BFT and permit.
patterns.image_source: Flymen Fishing Company — Pillow Talk product photo, clean 1:1 white background

regional_usage.notes: Designed by Alphonse guide Wayne Haselau; accounts for the largest proportion of bonefish caught at Alphonse Island and is carried by every Alphonse/Astove/Cosmoledo guide as their primary bonefish fly.

The premier bonefish shrimp pattern for Alphonse/Seychelles and directly applicable to the large-bonefish white sand flats of St Brandon's Atoll; available in tungsten bead (deep) and bead-chain (shallow) versions. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Pillow Talk'.

patterns.name: Pink Mini Puff
patterns.description: A small, soft-hackle attractor in the Charlie family tied with a pink or pale-pink marabou or craft-fur wing and bead-chain eyes. The puff-style body lands quietly and sinks slowly. Particularly favored on the Andros Marls where bonefish key on pale, sparkly presentations in shallow, clear water. Twitched on the bottom or fished on a slow strip-pause retrieve.
patterns.image_source: Red's Fly Shop product photo of RIO's Mini Puff bonefish fly, clean background

regional_usage.notes: A classic Charlie-family puff pattern in pink and white; the 'Delphi Daddy' and similar puff-style flies have proven highly effective on the Andros Marls where pale, sparkly, slightly pink patterns outperform realistic imitations.

patterns.name: Pink Thing
patterns.description: Australia's most iconic saltwater fly, originated by Darwin tier Graham White in the early 1980s as a barramundi pattern. Pink-and-white saddle hackle over a bucktail underwing on 2/0–4/0 imitates a distressed baitfish. Stripped with long pulls across tidal edges. Multi-species mainstay across northern Australia for barramundi, GT, threadfin salmon, and mangrove jack.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; iconic Australian pattern not commercially catalogued internationally

regional_usage.notes: Seminal Australian saltwater fly originated by Darwin tier Graham White in the early 1980s originally as a barramundi fly; now a multi-species pattern proven on GT and queenfish across northern Australian flats including Exmouth.

regional_usage.region: Australia — Cape York / Gulf of Carpentaria
regional_usage.notes: Originated by Darwin tier Graham White in the early 1980s as a barramundi fly; remains the single most iconic Australian tropical saltwater fly and is named in every Cape York / Gulf barra and GT fly list; pink-and-white is the original, black and yellow variants also standard.

The foundational Australian tropical fly is carried by Australian and PNG guides into PNG freshwater and estuarine systems targeting barramundi, Niugini black bass, and mangrove jack; its hackle-and-bucktail construction handles the brutal structure encountered in PNG jungle rivers.

patterns.name: Pink/White Pacific Billfish Streamer
patterns.description: Generic category of large 6–10 inch synthetic-material streamers in pink/white — the near-universal color for Pacific billfish. Multiple variants tied by Costa Rican mate-riggers and captains for bait-and-switch teaser programs. Cast to raised Pacific sailfish, blue marlin, and striped marlin after pulling them off the teaser.
patterns.image_source: Salt Fly Pro shop product photo — pink/white marlin and sailfish fly, clean studio shot matching the described color class

regional_usage.notes: Generic category of large 6-10 inch synthetic-material streamers in pink/white — the near-universal color for Pacific billfish; multiple variants are tied by local Costa Rican mate-riggers and offshore captains for the bait-and-switch teaser program.

patterns.name: Popper (Big Game Crease / Pop Star)
patterns.description: Large foam crease-style or hard-foam popper on 3/0–5/0 in blue-and-white or green-and-white for reef-edge GT action. Thrown on a 12-weight to uninhabited offshore island edges in the Solomons, where pristine fishery pressure means aggressive GTs will charge surface disturbance from distance. Fished with a loud, stop-and-go retrieve; also draws queenfish and Spanish mackerel attacks.
patterns.image_source: No specific 'Big Game Crease / Pop Star' brand image found; generic crease fly available (Spratz Popper) but not this specific pattern

regional_usage.notes: Large foam/crease-style popper for the reef-edge action around uninhabited offshore islands in the Solomons; the fishery is described as pristine enough that loud surface presentations draw GTs from distance.

patterns.name: Pretorius Semper Squid
patterns.description: Christian Pretorius's Seychelles GT fly built on the Semper platform with oversized 3D eyes and a bulky squid silhouette. Designed for Indian Ocean surf zones where GTs ambush baitfish in churned white water. Cast into the break and strip fast and hard. Superflies documents it as an absolute GT killer when squid dominate the forage.
patterns.image_source: Superflies.com — Pretorius Semper Squid official product photo, clean background

regional_usage.notes: A Seychelles-specific twist on the Semper Fly by Christian Pretorius featuring oversized eyes; proven over years of use on Seychelles flats and described by Superflies as an absolute GT killer in the surf.
Squid-profile fly effective on GTs hunting the deeper reef edges off Sudan's outer islands; GTs in the Red Sea feed heavily on small squid escaping coral heads.
Squid imitation for the deeper offshore rock piles and drop-offs around the Hallaniyat Islands where GTs ambush squid pushed up by upwelling currents.
Squid are a major forage species on Bazaruto's offshore drop-offs; the Semper Squid fished on a fast-sinking head over the pinnacles accounts for dogtooth and large GTs.

patterns.name: Puglisi Diver
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's EP-fiber diver pattern with a stacked, multi-layer profile that pushes water and creates a diving action on the strip-pause retrieve. Tied in white, black/purple, and black/red for Belize tarpon. The bulky EP-fiber head traps air and displaces water on each strip, creating a V-wake and subsurface pressure wave that triggers tarpon to eat; effective in both lagoon and flat-edge situations.
patterns.image_source: Bear's Den — Enrico Puglisi EP Diver, clean white background product photo

regional_usage.notes: EP synthetic fiber diver pattern in white, black/purple, and black/red; El Pescador lists it specifically for Belize tarpon alongside the classic streamer patterns.

patterns.name: Puglisi Sardine
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's synthetic EP fiber sardine imitation tied in silver, white, and olive to match Pacific sardines schooling along Baja beaches. Its slender hollow-fiber body creates natural gill-and-flank flash on the strip-pause. Cast into corralling bait schools ahead of roosterfish and dorado; strip continuously at medium speed to match a fleeing sardine. Essential for Baja beach-and-panga fishing.
patterns.image_source: Fin and Fire product photo — EP Roosterfish Sardina on clean white background, detailed side view

regional_usage.notes: The EP Sardine pattern in silver-and-white replicates the schooling Pacific sardines (Sardinops sagax) that are the primary roosterfish forage in Baja, essential when fish are seen corralling bait against the beach.
Hyper-realistic EP sardine imitates the baitfish shoals that drive pack attacks by Bazaruto's queenfish and GT; also used as a teaser-and-switch fly for bait-and-switch sailfish on fly.

patterns.name: Puglisi Shrimp
patterns.description: Enrico Puglisi's EP-fiber shrimp mimics brown and white shrimp species with layered synthetic fibers, a curved shrimp profile, and bead-chain eyes that orient the hook point up for weedless presentation. Slow-sink, short-strip retrieve over Louisiana marsh grass and Texas Laguna Madre flats. Takes redfish, speckled trout, and sheepshead year-round.
patterns.image_source: Fat Fingered Fly Tyer — EP Shrimp fly step-by-step, finished product clearly shown

regional_usage.notes: Enrico Puglisi's lifelike EP-fiber shrimp matches the prolific brown and white shrimp populations that make Louisiana's marsh one of the most productive shrimp nurseries on the Gulf Coast.

The Laguna Madre is one of the most productive shrimp nurseries on the Texas coast, and Puglisi's EP-fiber shrimp in grass shrimp colors is a critical imitation for sight-fishing trout and redfish on clear flats.

patterns.name: Purple Death
patterns.description: A high-contrast tarpon streamer in purple and black, using saddle hackles or marabou tied Deceiver-style over a monofilament loop. The dark color combination creates a bold silhouette in Cuba's clear-water conditions, triggering aggressive inspection from large tarpon. Named by Cuban guides and listed by Fishmaster specifically for Jardines de la Reina tarpon and snook.
patterns.image_source: Custom Saltwater Flies product photo of Andino Tarpon in Purple Death color, clear fly profile

regional_usage.notes: Fishmaster specifically names Purple Death as a Cuba tarpon and snook pattern for JDR; the purple/black combination is considered a high-contrast trigger for Cuba's clear-water giant tarpon.
Purple/black tarpon streamer variant used in stained water; confirmed effective alongside Black Death in the turbid jungle river environments of Nicaragua's Río San Juan / Río Indio system.

High-contrast purple/black tarpon streamer listed in the Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras tarpon selection; the purple silhouette is effective for the 100 lb+ resident tarpon that cruise the deeper channels of the Mosquitia coast.

patterns.name: Purple/Black Pacific Billfish Streamer
patterns.description: Dark-silhouette synthetic streamer in purple/black for Pacific billfish in low-light or overcast conditions. High-contrast profile targets Pacific sailfish and blue marlin when standard pink/white slows. Used in Costa Rica's bait-and-switch offshore program; cast to billfish that have been raised and pulled off a teaser.
patterns.image_source: Salt Fly Pro shop product photo — EP-style black/purple offshore fly in clean studio format, representative of this color class

regional_usage.notes: Dark-color alternative for low-light conditions and overcast days; silhouette-heavy fly relied upon by experienced Costa Rica guides when standard pink/white slows.

patterns.name: Purple/Black Shrimp (Large)
patterns.description: A large 4/0 purple-and-black shrimp on a heavy-wire hook is the benchmark deep-water jungle tarpon fly for Costa Rica's Río Colorado and Nicaragua's Río Indio system. The dark silhouette registers strongly in tannin-stained water at 10–40 ft depth on a sinking line. Christiaan Pretorius documented a 50 lb Tapam Lodge tarpon on the first strip of this exact colour combination.
patterns.image_source: No specific named commercial pattern found; search returned similar but not identical patterns

regional_usage.notes: A large 4/0 purple-and-black shrimp pattern on a heavy hook is the iconic deep-water jungle tarpon fly confirmed by multiple Río Colorado / Tapam-area guides; the dark profile registers strongly in colored water at 10–40 ft depth when combined with a sinking line.

Documented by Christiaan Pretorius on the Río Indio/Tapam Lodge system as the first-choice tarpon fly; a 4/0 purple-and-black shrimp pattern on the first strip produced a 50 lb tarpon — confirms its effectiveness in the stained jungle lagoon waters.

patterns.name: Queenfish Crease Fly
patterns.description: Folded-foam popper in silver/blue or white on 2/0–4/0 imitating a distressed baitfish. The V-shaped foam body creates an irregular skipping action when stripped sharply. Proven on queenfish schooling over shallow reef edges around Madagascar's Mitsio Islands and on bluefin trevally. Originated by Joe Blados; fished on floating line with aggressive strip-and-pause.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants — Crease Fly (Black)

regional_usage.notes: Medium (2/0–4/0) crease fly in silver/blue or white targeting queenfish that school over shallow reef edges around the Mitsio Islands; queenfish respond aggressively to surface presentations and the Crease Fly's erratic skipping action triggers explosive strikes. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Crease Fly'.

patterns.name: Raghead Crab
patterns.description: Jan Isley's Yucatan permit crab, named the single most important permit fly by Palometa Club guides at Ascension Bay. Spun and clipped deer-hair or synthetic rag-head body creates a flat crab profile with inverted hook. Drop ahead of a feeding permit, let it sink to the bottom, and wait for the take without stripping.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants — Rag Head Crab official product photo on white

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Designed on the flats of the Yucatan specifically for permit; the Palometa Club names it the single most important permit fly for Ascension Bay guides and stocks it exclusively.

Tan and olive Raghead Crabs on size 2 hooks are specified for permit by the Explore Yachts Los Roques guide; the yarn-body construction sinks fast and flat, ideal for presenting to tailing permit on the exposed outer flats.

Fly Fishing Caribe Guanaja Honduras fly list names the Rag Head as a primary permit pattern; its sparse hackle-fiber crab silhouette performs well on the mixed sand-and-coral flats of the Bay Islands.

patterns.name: Ratliff's Fiddlestick Crab
patterns.description: Custom-tied articulated fiddler crab favored by Southeast US coastal guides for flood-tide redfish. The articulated claw arm gives a bolting, tumbling action as the crab falls — closely mimicking a fiddler crab scurrying across exposed hard sand ahead of the tide. Documented as a top flood-tide pattern at St. Simons and throughout the Georgia and South Carolina marsh coast.
patterns.image_source: No image found; regional SE US guide pattern not in commercial retail databases; Ratliff is a guide-tier not a commercial brand

regional_usage.notes: Custom-tied fiddler-crab imitation widely cited by SE US coastal guides as a top flood-tide pattern; the articulated claw movement mimics a fiddler bolting across a hard sand flat.
Documented as a top flood-tide fiddler crab pattern used at St. Simons, Ga. and throughout the SE marsh coast where big-tide flood-tide fishing drives fiddler-crab eating frenzies.

patterns.name: Rattlesnake
patterns.description: An attractor-style saltwater fly incorporating a glass or plastic rattle chamber in the body, generating audible clicks on each strip. Designed for Louisiana marsh fishing where dingy, low-visibility water makes scent and sound more important than visual profile. The rattle produces low-frequency vibrations that mimic a distressed prey item; effective on red drum and speckled trout in dark, tannin-stained bayous and grass flats.
patterns.image_source: Fat Fingered Fly Tyer — Redfish Rattle Fly step-by-step, finished fly photo on clean background

regional_usage.notes: A noisy attractor-style pattern that incorporates a rattle chamber; the auditory stimulus is particularly valuable in Louisiana's dingy, low-visibility marsh water where sound triggers reaction strikes.

patterns.name: Rattling Fat Boy
patterns.description: Produced by Saltwater Flies Australia in sizes SL12 2/0–6/0, the Rattling Fat Boy incorporates an internal rattle chamber inside a bulky synthetic baitfish body. The sonic vibration combined with a wide profile triggers GT, queenfish, and golden trevally in the turbid water of Australian tropical flats. Available in multiple colour variants including chart/black and white/olive.
patterns.image_source: saltwaterfliesaustralia.com — Rattling Fat Boy Fly SL12 product photo

regional_usage.notes: Rattle-chamber baitfish pattern produced by Saltwater Flies Australia in sizes SL12 4/0–6/0; the sonic-rattle version is targeted at tropical predators in Australian flats and is listed on their site as a GT and tropical species fly.

patterns.name: Redfish Crack
patterns.description: A loud shrimp-attractor pattern known for its bulky front hackle collar — also called the Redfish Cracklin — that pushes water and creates turbulence visible to redfish in stained Louisiana marsh and upper Texas coast flats. Fish slow with a strip-pause in murky water; its high-contrast silhouette and collar wake trigger reaction strikes where visibility is limited.
patterns.image_source: Royal Treatment Fly Fishing shop photo of Redfish Crack fly — clean close-up on white

regional_usage.notes: Also called Redfish Cracklin or Redfish Ritalin; the large front collar excels in the stained, tannin-colored water common in Louisiana's brackish marshes.

The large front collar and contrasting colors are particularly effective on the stained upper-coast Texas flats; the pattern was reportedly developed with Texas/Louisiana conditions specifically in mind.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Universal SE flats shrimp pattern; especially productive for schooling IRL reds in clear water on natural/tan colorways — already in library.
Universal SE shrimp/crab hybrid; one of the most consistent producers when SC reds transition from fiddler crab feeding to grass-shrimp feeding in late summer and fall — already in library.
Core SE flats shrimp pattern applicable throughout the Georgia Golden Isles for schooling reds and seatrout on tide-driven grass flats — already in library.
Standard SE shrimp/crab attractor for the Pine Island Sound and Matlacha backcountry redfish and snook that share grass-flat habitat with intermingled schools — already in library.

patterns.name: Redfish Worm
patterns.description: A long, slender fly imitating polychaete and tube worms that emerge from Gulf Coast marsh sediment. Typically tied with craft fur, marabou, or thin synthetic fibers on a size 2–1/0 hook. Fished near the bottom during spring worm hatches on calm morning tides. Particularly effective for tailing Louisiana redfish and black drum rooting in soft-bottom marsh ponds.
patterns.image_source: JackGartside.com — Jack Gartside's Redfish Worm, originator's site, direct fly photo

regional_usage.notes: A long, slender fly imitating the tube worms and polychaetes that emerge from Louisiana's marsh mud and sediment, particularly effective during spring worm hatches on calm morning tides.

The worm fly imitates the numerous polychaetes and sea worms that burrow in the Laguna's sandy substrate; effective for blind-casting to black drum and redfish over sandy bottom in low-vis conditions.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Long, dark worm-profile fly worked slowly in front of tailing black drum and rooting redfish on IRL turtle-grass flats where marine worms are abundant forage — already in library.

patterns.name: Reef Popper (Coral Reef GT)
patterns.description: Compact foam popper on 2/0–4/0 with a cupped face and body under 6 cm—sized for precision delivery into tight coral structures at Nosy Be's Serpent Bank and Grand Entry Bank. GTs hold tight against coral heads requiring slower pop-and-pause presentations than open-flat fishing. Retrieved with sharp 30 cm strips; works bluefin trevally as well.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants — Saltwater Popper (Red/White)

regional_usage.notes: A smaller, more compact foam popper (2/0–4/0) suited to casting into tight reef structures at the Serpent Bank and Grand Entry Bank; GTs at Nosy Be frequently sit tight against coral heads requiring more precise, shorter-range presentations than open-flat GT fishing.

patterns.name: River Monster (Captain Sullivan's)
patterns.description: Captain Jason Sullivan's Everglades tarpon pattern uses black ostrich herl over an EP Foxy Brush body to create a dark, heavily breathing mullet silhouette. Designed specifically for tannin-stained backcountry creek tarpon in Florida Bay where contrast and movement matter more than realism. Documented by Orvis News as a primary tool for resident Everglades tarpon year-round.
patterns.image_source: Orvis News editorial article — '3 Guide-Tested Patterns for Everglades National Park'

regional_usage.notes: Orvis News-documented guide pattern; Captain Sullivan's black ostrich/EP Foxy Brush mullet imitation is specifically designed for Everglades resident tarpon in dark-water tannin creeks and the murky backcountry channels of Florida Bay.

patterns.name: Ruoff's Laid-Up Tarpon Fly
patterns.description: Natural tan/chartreuse fly with subdued coloration designed by Keys guide Rick Ruoff for finesse presentations to motionless laid-up tarpon. Ruoff's marine biology background informed the low-contrast tones suited to resting fish. Delivered softly on a long leader, dead-drifted or given a single slow strip when the fish reacts.
patterns.image_source: Florida Keys Outfitters shop product photo — named 'Laid Up Tarpon Fly, Ruoff', clean product shot

regional_usage.notes: A natural tan/chartreuse fly with subtle coloration designed for finesse presentations to motionless laid-up tarpon by Keys guide Rick Ruoff, who applied his marine biology background to match the low-contrast tones that appeal to resting fish.

patterns.name: Sailfish Fly (Tandem Tube)
patterns.description: Large pink-and-white tandem tube fly on 6/0, presented to free-swimming or teased Indo-Pacific sailfish. The tube design allows the hook to swing freely, dramatically improving hookup rates on billfish that slash at the fly. Used throughout the Mozambique Channel — especially off Nosy Be, Madagascar — where sailfish numbers peak in season. Flymen Fishing Co. popularized the tandem tube format.
patterns.image_source: Salt Fly Pro (saltflypro.com) — Sailfish Fly Pink #6/0 Tube Fly product listing, Flymen Fishing Company

regional_usage.notes: Madagascar is renowned for its sailfish numbers passing through the Mozambique Channel; large pink/white or blue/white tandem tube fly presented to free-swimming or teased sailfish. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Flymen Sailfish Fly (Tandem Pink/White Tube)'.

patterns.name: Schminnow
patterns.description: Norm Zeigler's lightweight saltwater baitfish pattern tied with marabou and crystal chenille over a short-shank hook, imitating small silversides or glass minnows. The fly sinks slowly and breathes on a dead drift or micro-strip — critical when false albacore and little tunny at Cape Lookout and the Outer Banks are feeding on suspended 1-inch bait and refusing faster-sinking patterns. Originator is Norm Zeigler of Sanibel.
patterns.image_source: Baxter House Fly Fishing — Schminnow #4 baitfish fly, clean background product photo

regional_usage.notes: Zeigler's lightweight marabou-and-crystal-chenille pattern imitating small silvery baitfish is used along the OBX surf and at Cape Lookout when albies and little tunny are feeding on small, slow-sinking bait.

The non-crystal base Schminnow (marabou, monofilament eyes) is tied lighter for daytime beach-trough snook presentations where the Crystal Schminnow might spook fish in ultra-clear Sanibel-beach conditions — already in library.

patterns.name: Seaducer
patterns.description: Homer Rhodes's 1940s all-hackle streamer tied with long front and rear hackle collars that create a near-neutral buoyancy in the water column. Its pulsing hackle fibers simulate a wounded baitfish or swimming shrimp at slow retrieve speeds. Fish just below the surface film on a floating line with a steady or erratic strip; an enduring design for snook, redfish, and trout in shallow structure.
patterns.image_source: Orlando Outfitters product photo of Seaducer in tan — clean white background, clear side profile

regional_usage.notes: Homer Rhodes's all-hackle streamer lands with a near-neutral buoyancy that glides just below the surface film, making it an outstanding choice for shallow Louisiana marsh presentations.
Homer Rhodes's lightweight all-hackle streamer excels along the Laguna's back-lake snook habitat in the lower Arroyo Colorado drainage and near the Rio Grande delta.
The Seaducer's all-hackle construction creates a near-neutral buoyancy ideal for Magdalena Bay snook presentations along mangrove edges, and its pulsing action draws roosterfish working the surf.

Classic hackle-and-bucktail tarpon and snook fly listed by fishcostarica.com as a recommended pattern for Costa Rica Caribbean jungle tarpon; its slow sink and undulating hackle work especially well in the tannin-stained riverine conditions of Tortuguero.

Classic slow-sinking hackle-and-bucktail pattern used in the calmer lagoon and backwater areas of the Río Indio system; the seductive hackle-breathing action is effective when tarpon are laid up and not actively chasing.

Fly Fishing Caribe recommends 'Seducer' style flies alongside Toads and Deceivers as the core tarpon fly type for Bocas del Toro; the hackle-and-bucktail profile works in the layered freshwater/saltwater column of the river mouths.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Classic hackle-and-feather streamer that lands softly and sinks slowly — ideal for presenting to laid-up snook on IRL canal edges and under dock lights — already in library.
Soft-landing, slow-sinking hackle pattern for Sanibel beach and mangrove snook when a quiet presentation over clear sand bottom is needed — already in library.

patterns.name: Semper Fly
patterns.description: Bob Popovics's flowing GT pattern pairs a marabou collar with thin schlappen hackle fibers for a baitfish-squid hybrid that pulses on every pause. Olive-red and black-purple colorways dominate for Seychelles and Christmas Island giant trevally. Retrieved in aggressive long strips along coral drop-offs; the large silhouette and water-pushing action register on GT's lateral line at distance.
patterns.image_source: Into Fly Fishing — Semper fly step-by-step, professional finished fly photograph

regional_usage.notes: Schlappen-hackle and marabou construction gives this baitfish-squid hybrid irresistible water movement; olive-and-red and black-and-purple color combinations are most productive for Christmas Island GTs.

Alphonse Fishing Co. ranks the Olive and Red Semper as their second-choice GT fly; marabou collar and thin hackle tail deliver lifelike squid-baitfish movement irresistible to cruising Seychelles GTs. Black and purple Semper variant is documented among top Cosmoledo and Astove GT patterns; the large profile and flowing action in the Seychelles surf zone is highly effective during low-light and dawn patrols.
Olive and black-purple Semper variants are the standard GT baitfish pattern on the reef edges of Sudan; Aardvark McLeod lists it alongside GT brush flies as a primary Indian Ocean GT choice.
Olive and black-purple Semper flies are the standard articulated baitfish pattern for Hallaniyat GT and queenfish, particularly when sardine baitballs push predators to the surface.
Olive Semper is the default baitfish pattern when GTs push mullet and baitfish into the Bazaruto Archipelago's shallow back-channel areas on the flooding tide.

Library universal (existing #120); marabou-and-schlappen squid-baitfish hybrid documented as a top GT fly across all Indo-Pacific destinations including PNG's Portlock, Eastern Fields, and Bismarck reef systems.

Library universal (existing #120); olive-red and black-purple Semper variants documented across all Indo-Pacific GT destinations; the marabou tail movement is particularly effective in Raja Ampat's current-rich reef passes.

The versatile Indo-Pacific shrimp pattern is a confirmed effective bonefish and small trevally fly in Maldives atoll fisheries; Alphonse guides list it alongside Clousers and poppers as an all-rounder for the flats. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Semper Fly'.

A versatile Indo-Pacific shrimp/crab hybrid that performs across all Indian Ocean flats fisheries including St Brandon's; noted in Alphonse Fishing Company guides alongside Clousers and crabs as a general flats pattern. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Semper Fly'.

patterns.name: Senegal Kob Shrimp
patterns.description: A weighted tan/olive shrimp tied on 1/0–2/0, designed to target Senegal kob (Pseudotolithus senegalensis) — an estuarine sciaenid that feeds heavily on shrimp in Gabon's lagoon mouths and river channels at Sette Cama. Fished with a slow, twitching retrieve near bottom structure alongside Atlantic tarpon and leerfish. A recommended secondary fly-box addition for West Africa.
patterns.image_source: No specific named pattern photo found for this regional Gabon specialist fly

regional_usage.notes: Weighted shrimp pattern in tan/olive tied on 1/0–2/0; Senegal kob (Pseudotolithus senegalensis) feed heavily on estuarine shrimp and are a secondary target at Sette Cama alongside the tarpon; guide-recommended secondary fly box addition.

patterns.name: Shaughnessy's Nyacca Baitfish
patterns.description: Developed by FlyFishMex founder James Shaughnessy for Baja bluewater species, this layered-feather-tail baitfish uses multiple saddle hackle layers over a synthetic body to create a lifelike swimming profile. Tied in sardine, mullet, and needlefish colors on 2/0–4/0 hooks. One of the most trusted East Cape roosterfish and sailfish patterns produced by Montana Fly Company.
patterns.image_source: Bear's Den Fly Shop product photo of MFC Shaughnessy's Nyacca Baitfish in yellow, clean white background

regional_usage.notes: Developed specifically for Baja by FlyFishMex founder James Shaughnessy, this layered-feather-tail baitfish pattern is one of the most trusted local patterns for roosterfish, billfish, and bluewater species off East Cape and La Paz.

Developed by a Baja California guide; large synthetic baitfish with mullet profile sold in Tan/Cotton Candy and Olive/White — effective for roosterfish keyed on sardines and equally proven on blue-water dorado and tuna off Costa Rica.

patterns.name: Shrimpy (Captain Sullivan's)
patterns.description: Capt. Jason Sullivan's Everglades shrimp tied with brown, tan, and orange craft fur for ultra-shallow Florida Bay and Whitewater Bay sight-fishing. Soft landing and neutral sink match tailing redfish and laid-up snook in inches of water. Documented by Orvis News as an Everglades-specific pattern. Strip slowly or dead-drift once in the feeding zone.
patterns.image_source: Orvis News — Captain Sullivan's Shrimpy guide fly, editorial Everglades pattern feature

regional_usage.notes: Verified Everglades-specific pattern documented by Orvis News; Capt. Jason Sullivan's guide-developed brown/tan/orange craft-fur shrimp is optimized for tailing redfish and laid-up snook in ultra-shallow Florida Bay and Whitewater Bay.

patterns.name: Simple Shrimp
patterns.description: Bonefish shrimp developed by Fish-Bones Fly Fishing (Grand Cayman) as the heavier companion to The Usual. Splayed rubber legs, rust/tan dubbed body, and orange tail on #2–#4 imitate a defensive posture on the sandy Cayman flats bottom. Rust with orange tail is the top Cayman tailing-bonefish color; presented and stripped with short, gentle pulls.
patterns.image_source: No specific photo found; proprietary Fish-Bones Cayman pattern not found in commercial databases

regional_usage.notes: Heavier companion to The Usual, designed for a defensive splayed-leg posture on the bottom; rust with orange tail is the top Cayman tailing-bonefish color.

patterns.name: Simram
patterns.description: A bonefish shrimp pattern built with a crosscut rabbit body over a pearlescent shell-back, creating a sculpted, lifelike swimming profile. The rabbit fiber undulates naturally on the sink and strip, imitating a shrimp scooting along the bottom. Most effective in the deeper tidal channels that border Andros's shallow sand flats; fish on a slow strip-pause near the bottom.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com dedicated Simram product page — clear side profile of the Simram fly

regional_usage.notes: Angler Adventures lists the Simram as a very effective deep-water Bahamian bonefish fly; its rabbit crosscut body and pearlescent shell-back produce a lifelike swimming action in the deeper channels surrounding Andros's flats.
Lead-eye deep-water Bahamas pattern featured by Angler Adventures; the rabbit-strip wing and shrimp silhouette are effective when Bimini bones hold in deeper channel edges.

patterns.name: Snapper Bunker (Cubera Pattern)
patterns.description: Large dark olive-and-purple bunker/menhaden-profile fly on 4/0–6/0. Cubera snapper at Gabon's Sette Cama estuary respond to a big, dark, slow-moved profile near mangrove edges and channel drop-offs, especially with a sinking line. The wide, compressed bucktail or EP body pushes water and gives off low-frequency vibration. Also intercepts Atlantic tarpon staging in the same structure.
patterns.image_source: No specific Snapper Bunker (Cubera Pattern) image found; a category description rather than a named commercial pattern

regional_usage.notes: Large bulky bunker/menhaden-profile fly on 4/0–6/0 in dark olive and purple; structure-dwelling cubera snapper at Sette Cama respond to a large, dark profile worked slowly near mangrove edges and channel drop-offs with heavy sinking line.

patterns.name: Snook Slider
patterns.description: A cupped or bullet-head deer-hair or foam surface fly that pushes water without hard popping. The hook rides point-up in a weedless configuration for working mangrove tangles and root systems. Used with a slow walk-the-dog surface retrieve. Critical for Lower Laguna snook and the Magdalena Bay mangrove fishery where hard poppers catch too much structure.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com — Snook Slider in chartreuse/red, clean side profile on white

regional_usage.notes: A surface-riding slider that pushes water with a cupped foam or deer-hair head; essential for the Lower Laguna and Rio Grande snook fishery where fish hold in mangrove root systems and along bank structure.
A critical pattern for Magdalena Bay's snook fishery, where fish hold in dense mangrove tangles; the slider's weedless, surface-pushing profile draws snook from structure without fouling on roots.

Foam-head slider fly that pushes a wake and creates subtle sound vibration ideal for presenting to large Pacific snook in Costa Rica's tidal river mouths and estuary channels at night or early morning.
Foam-head surface-wake slider effective for the large fat snook and common snook that hold in mangrove edges and tidal channels throughout the Tortuguero canal system.

Surface wake fly for the large snook populations in the mangrove margins of the Río Indio and tributary channels; Nicaragua's snook respond aggressively to surface presentations early morning in flat-calm conditions.

Surface-wake presentation for the snook that patrol the quiet mangrove-margin channels of Bocas del Toro at dawn; Cuban Fishing Centers notes that snook respond best to bright-colored or high-flash flies with short, stout leaders.
Foam-headed subsurface slider that skates across the surface film on the retrieve — designed for casting tight to mangrove snags and pilings for laid-up West Florida snook — already in library.

patterns.name: Snook-A-Roo
patterns.description: A surface slider with a foam or clipped deer-hair head that creates a wide pushing wake without diving underwater. Fished with sharp strips followed by long pauses in mangrove creek tidal channels. The slow-sink wake pattern is one of Pesca Maya's recommended surface presentations for snook in Ascension Bay's backcountry, where snook ambush from structure.
patterns.image_source: The Fly Shop Belize guide article photo of Snook-A-Roo, high-quality clear side profile

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Pesca Maya lists the Snook-A-Roo as a recommended surface pattern for snook in the back mangrove creeks; snook key on surface patterns in Ascension Bay's tidal channels.
Feather-and-bucktail pattern with wide-gap hook developed for Sanibel and Southwest Florida snook; designed to be cast into mangrove pockets and retrieved through structure — already in library.

patterns.name: Spam & Eggs
patterns.description: Mantis shrimp imitation developed by Oahu guide Coach Duff specifically for Hawaiian flats where mantis shrimp dominate bonefish diet. Signature spider-like legs radiating from the head create irresistible leg-action. Fished on short hops with brief pauses on sand and rubble flats targeting bonefish, permit, and papio jacks.
patterns.image_source: SSFlies.com shop product page — clean photo labeled 'Spam & Eggs', good side-profile of the named pattern

regional_usage.notes: Developed specifically for Oahu flats where mantis shrimp dominate the bonefish diet; spider-like legs off the head are the signature feature.

patterns.name: Spawning Shrimp
patterns.description: Eric Peterson's rabbit-fur shrimp with a prominent orange egg sac at the bend, imitating egg-bearing shrimp on the flats. Egg sac flash triggers permit, bonefish, and triggerfish. Palometa Club guides rank it a top Ascension Bay fly — Lee Haskin caught seven permit in one week on his own variant. Fish slowly along grass edges.
patterns.image_source: Fly Fish Bonehead — Peterson's Spawning Shrimp fly tying feature, clean pattern photo

regional_usage.notes: Egg-sac shrimp imitation; listed on both El Pescador and Turneffe Flats permit fly recommendations as a versatile pattern for bonefish and permit.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Guide Lee Haskin reported catching all seven of his Espíritu Santo Bay permit in one week on his own Spawning Shrimp variant; spawning shrimp are abundant in the biosphere and a dominant forage.
Rabbit-fur body with orange egg-sac triggers aggressive takes from Christmas Island bonefish; its larger profile also entices the yellowmargin triggerfish that share the flats.

One of Alphonse Fishing Co.'s top three bonefish flies; the large, realistic shrimp profile provokes aggressive reactions from Seychelles bonefish, which tend to run larger than their Pacific counterparts.
Shrimp patterns in tan, pink, and white are effective in Pamlico Sound channels and grass edges where red drum and winter stripers feed heavily on crustaceans during tidal movements.

Listed alongside Merkin crabs and Raghead Crabs for permit fishing in the Explore Yachts Los Roques tackle recommendations; the large, pink-tinted shrimp imitation matches the outsized shrimp present on the richer Caribbean flats.
Named explicitly by Oliver White (Fly Fisherman) as one of his top-two Sudan trigger patterns; bead-chain eyes keep it in the feeding zone on the flats without spooking fish.

Widely cited as a tournament-winning bonefish pattern across the Caribbean; the realistic spawning shrimp profile is effective in the prolific crustacean habitat of Bonaire's mangrove-fringed lagoons.

Guide Frankie at Cayo Largo (All Points Fly Shop) called it 'the tried-and-true all a-rounder'; rarely refused by either permit or bonefish on mixed sand-and-turtle-grass flats, particularly in #4–#6 sizes.

patterns.name: Spongebob Threadfin Slider
patterns.description: Conrad Botes' 2015 creation for Sette Cama's giant African threadfin: a large 14–16 cm bucktail-and-schlappen streamer on a slider head tied on 4/0–6/0. The slider head makes it surf current seams without diving. Fished on Di5–Di7 sinking lines through Gabon estuary channels, it also draws Atlantic tarpon and jack crevalle. Featured in The Mission Fly Fishing Magazine tying guide.
patterns.image_source: The Mission Fly Fishing Magazine — Sponge Bob Slider tying article photo

regional_usage.notes: Large (14–16 cm) bucktail-and-schlappen slider-head streamer on 4/0–6/0, developed specifically at Sette Cama for trophy-size giant African threadfin; fished on Di5–Di7 sinking lines through estuary current seams.

patterns.name: Spoon Fly
patterns.description: A weedless mylar-wrapped fly tied to mimic the wobbling flash of a metal spoon, with a hook-point-up configuration on a single or double hook. Standard tailing redfish pattern in the Everglades, Louisiana marsh, and Lower Laguna Madre. Fished on a slow strip-pause over grass flats, the mylar body pulses and flutters, producing the low-frequency vibration that draws feeding redfish by lateral-line detection before they see it.
patterns.image_source: Salt Water Sportsman editorial — Rainy's Spoon Flies for Redfish, multiple flies displayed

regional_usage.notes: Florida Keys and Everglades guide sources list spoon flies as a top redfish pattern; the weedless silver-mylar design is particularly effective for tailing redfish in the shallow Everglades grass flats and mud banks.
A weedless mylar spoon imitation that emits flash and low-frequency vibration; deadly on Louisiana redfish tailing in murky, grass-laden marsh flats.
The weedless spoon fly is a staple of Lower Laguna Madre guides; its fluttering action during a slow strip-pause retrieve is irresistible to redfish cruising the open sand and grass flats.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Weedless mylar spoon fly excels for schooling Mosquito Lagoon reds pushing shrimp and baitfish on grass flats — already in library.
Weedless spoon fly for casting to schooling reds moving along spartina edges on lower tides in Bulls Bay and Cape Romain drainages — already in library.

patterns.name: Squimp
patterns.description: A squid-shrimp hybrid attractor pattern tied with rubber legs and a translucent synthetic body in tan, olive, or pink. Its combination of shrimp-like profile and squid-like tentacle appendages triggers bonefish and permit feeding across varied flat types. Fish on a slow sink to the bottom ahead of a feeding fish; listed consistently on El Pescador's Belize flat-fly recommendations.
patterns.image_source: Saltwater Edge fly shop product photo of the Squimp — clean well-lit image

regional_usage.notes: Squid-shrimp hybrid attractor in tan; consistently appears on El Pescador's Belize fly recommendations for its triggering action on mixed flats.

Requested by Cayo Largo guide Frankie (All Points Fly Shop trip report); the squid-shrimp hybrid attractor works on Cuba's mixed bottom flats and is also used in Belize, confirming its regional applicability.

patterns.name: St. Simons Scampi
patterns.originator: Capt. David Edens (St. Simons Island, GA)
patterns.description: Shrimp imitation created by Capt. David Edens of Fly Cast Charters (St. Simons Island, GA). Gold-dubbed body, root beer flash tail, gold dumbbell eyes, and gold flash wing on Mustad 34007 size 2. Cited by Sea Island Fly Fishers as a proven pattern for tailing Georgia Lowcountry redfish and spotted seatrout in the Golden Isles salt marshes.
patterns.image_source: Sea Island Fly Fishers — Dave Edens St. Simons Scampi RedFish Fly

regional_usage.notes: Shrimp pattern designed by Capt. David Edens for Golden Isles conditions; the St. Simons Scampi Red Fish Fly is cited by the Sea Island Fly Fishers club as a proven local shrimp pattern for GA reds and trout.

patterns.name: Strip Tease (Sparkplug)
patterns.description: Semi-translucent UV-body shrimp with rubber legs and an orange mouth, attributed to Dick Brown, recommended by Fish-Bones Grand Cayman for deep 'white hole' flats on flood tides. The UV-reactive materials glow in depth, and the compact profile sinks quickly to the feeding zone. Particularly effective when Cayman bonefish key on sand fleas and small crabs in deeper channel-adjacent water.
patterns.image_source: No specific Strip Tease / Sparkplug image found; Fish-Bones Cayman site not accessible; Dick Brown boneflystore.com no longer operational

regional_usage.notes: Recommended by Fish-Bones for deep 'white holes' on flood tides when Cayman bones key on sand-fleas and crabs; semi-translucent UV body with rubber legs and orange mouth.

patterns.name: Strong Arm Merkin
patterns.description: Dave Skok's 2019 Keys innovation replaces the Merkin's traditional hackle legs with a single prominent rubber-band or silicone crab claw — a visual trigger arm that hangs below the crab body as it sinks. Introduced to Key West guide Nathaniel Linville, the pattern took first or second in 8 of 11 Florida Keys permit tournaments after its debut.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants — Strong Arm Merkin product photo, white background

regional_usage.notes: Introduced by tier Dave Skok to Capt. Nathaniel Linville in Key West around 2019; the single crab-claw appendage replacing the Merkin's hackles has produced first or second place in 8 of 11 Keys permit tournaments since its debut.
Recommended by Xcalak guides for Yucatan permit; natural-color crab with rubber legs sinks quickly to meet tailing permit before they move off the flat.

The first fly All Points Fly Shop Cuba guide Frankie requested from the fly box when fishing Cayo Largo to Isla de la Juventud; a Merkin variant with a prominent chenille claw described as 'a fleeing crab' that has become a popular permit pattern throughout Cuba and Belize.
Yarn-and-rubber-leg crab with weedguard; the weedless, slow-sinking profile makes it essential for presenting in the spartina grass at flood tide for tailing SC reds — already in library.
Merkin-style yarn crab named at GA flood-tide sessions alongside Fiddlestick and Fleeing Crab as an essential weedless pattern for tailing marsh reds — already in library.

patterns.name: Stu Apte Tarpon Fly
patterns.description: Stu Apte's iconic Keys tarpon fly uses orange and red saddle hackles wound palmered-style over a short shank, creating a compact, dense profile. Featured on a 1991 U.S. postage stamp. The bright orange/red color triggers strikes from migratory tarpon in the clear water of the Lower Keys from April through July. A foundational pattern of the Florida Keys guiding tradition.
patterns.image_source: Tie the Flies recipe page photo of Stu Apte Tarpon Fly, high-resolution clear side view

regional_usage.notes: Apte's classic orange-and-red tarpon fly was featured on a 1991 U.S. postage stamp; a staple for Keys migratory tarpon season (April-July) and a foundational pattern in the Keys guide tradition.

Listed directly in the Fly Fishing Caribe Honduras tarpon fly selection (alongside Black Death, Purple Death, Cockroach, Gummy Minnow) for the 40–100+ lb tarpon sight-cast in clear water around the Bay Islands.

Named by All Points Fly Shop Cuba guide alongside the Tarpon Bunny for Cayo Largo tarpon fishing in black/purple and chartreuse; effective for the 30–90 lb tarpon at Cayo Cruz that feed in the clean, shallow channels between flats.

patterns.name: Surf Candy
patterns.description: Bob Popovics's epoxy-body baitfish matching bay anchovies and silversides with a hard-coat durable enough to withstand bluefish teeth. Sparse bucktail and flash under clear epoxy or UV resin create a glassy baitfish head. Fish on intermediate line with a sharp strip-pause through Cape Cod and Montauk rips. The benchmark Northeast silverside imitation for three decades.
patterns.image_source: Orvis — Surf Candy Saltwater Baitfish Fly official product photo on white

regional_usage.notes: Popovics's slim epoxy pattern imitating silversides and anchovies is highly effective for the finicky false albacore working the rips off Cape Lookout during the Harkers Island fall season.

Bob Popovics's epoxy-coated silicone baitfish pattern is a standard inshore Baja pattern for sierra mackerel and bonito near rocky points; its slim profile and realistic flash match anchovy and sardine baitballs.

patterns.name: Tarpon Bunny
patterns.description: A rabbit-strip tarpon streamer in which a long zonker strip provides continuous pulsing action even when the fly is stationary. Available in white, chartreuse, black/red, olive, and tan for varied light and water conditions. Effective for both rolling migratory tarpon in the Florida Keys and baby tarpon in Andros creek systems, Belize lagoons, and Cuba's flat edges.
