The material's movement at rest is its key advantage over sparser flies on slow, laid-up fish.
patterns.image_source: Tie the Flies — Tarpon Bunny fly recipe, high-resolution finished fly photo

regional_usage.notes: Rabbit-strip tarpon fly recommended by Andros South lodge for baby and resident tarpon in Andros's creek systems; the material's lively pulse at rest keeps the fly moving even on a slow retrieve.

Rabbit-strip tarpon patterns are listed by fishing.news as 'commonly used across tarpon grounds' including the Florida Keys; the material's movement at rest is useful for Keys laid-up tarpon that need slow presentations.
Rabbit-strip streamer in white, chartreuse, black/red, olive, and tan; El Pescador's tarpon list notes it for its pulsing action in Belize's lagoon and flat-side encounters.
Fishmaster lists a 'tarpon bunny' in tan, chartreuse, black, and purple as a core JDR tarpon pattern; rabbit-strip action particularly effective for Cuba's rolling and laying-up tarpon.

Rabbit-strip tarpon fly confirmed for Los Roques channels by Jean-Baptiste Vidal (Fishing.news, 2025); the lively swimming action of the strip in warm Caribbean current makes this an excellent alternative when fish are shy of stiffer feather patterns.
Rabbit-strip streamer in black/red, purple, olive, and chartreuse; widely used at Barra del Colorado and Tortuguero for its pulsing undulation in current-fed river mouths where tarpon stage to feed.
Rabbit-strip streamer in purple/black and chartreuse; confirmed by Tapam Lodge guides as effective for Nicaragua tarpon and double as a snook pattern in mangrove channel edges along the Río Indio.

Listed in Fly Fishing Caribe Bocas del Toro fly selection as 'White Bunny #1/0, 2/0, 3/0'; rabbit-strip pulsing action is effective for both the large migratory tarpon in September–October and the resident snook in the archipelago's bays.

All Points Fly Shop guide Frankie recommended 'Tarpon Bunny and Stu Ape style patterns' in black/purple tied on 1/0–2/0 hooks for the channel tarpon at Cayo Largo; the Bunny's rabbit-strip action is effective for tarpon that lay up in channels between the cays.
Rabbit-strip Tarpon Bunny in black or purple is used for Tampa Bay bridge tarpon and Sanibel pass fish when a slow-sinking undulating profile is needed — already in library.

patterns.name: Tarpon Toad
patterns.description: Gary Merriman's Keys-developed tarpon pattern combining craft fur, rubber legs, and marabou in a wide-profile, neutrally buoyant body that swims forward rather than bobbing. Derived from the Merkin and Tasty Toad lineage, it presents a large silhouette without excessive weight. Swing or strip slowly under feeding tarpon on a floating or clear intermediate line; a top Keys migratory pattern.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants official product photo of Tarpon Toad on clean white background

regional_usage.notes: Developed in the Keys by Gary Merriman from Del Brown's Merkin and Capt. Harry Spear's Tasty Toad; the Toad's neutral-buoyancy, wide-body design swims like a real baitfish rather than bouncing, and is now a top Keys migratory tarpon pattern.

The Toad's neutral-buoyancy design was partially developed from Keys-era fishing and works equally well on Everglades resident tarpon where a slow-sinking, swimming presentation outperforms heavier sinking patterns in shallow backcountry.
Marabou-and-rabbit-strip unweighted tarpon fly in multiple colors; El Pescador lists it as a top tarpon pattern for Belize's lagoon and migratory fish.

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Versatile marabou tarpon pattern effective in the Yucatán mangrove lagoons; Palometa Club recommends standard Florida Keys tarpon patterns including the Toad for both juvenile and adult fish.
Cuba Fishing Outfitters identifies the Toad as one of three must-have Cuba flies; effective in black/purple, black/red, tan/olive, and chartreuse on the Gardens of the King tarpon flats.

Originally a tarpon pattern adapted for the Lower Texas Coast, the Tarpon Toad is now a standard option for the snook, large redfish, and jacks that inhabit the jetties and passes around Port Mansfield.
The Tarpon Toad's craft-fur bulk and rubber legs imitate the small mullet and mojarra that Magdalena Bay snook feed on in the estuary channels during flood tides.

Widely cited as an essential tarpon pattern for the Caribbean; the weedless, sub-surface swimming action of the Toad is ideal for the mangrove lagoon tarpon at Los Roques where a quiet, snag-resistant presentation is required.
Black-and-purple Tarpon Toad in 1/0 is a primary pattern for the juvenile tarpon (baby tarpon) that roll in Boca Paila Lagoon channels and mangrove cuts.

Marabou-and-rabbit tarpon fly in black/purple and chartreuse; recommended by fishcostarica.com for both river-mouth and canal fishing at Barra del Colorado where tarpon roll continuously through tidal cycles.

Marabou-based tarpon fly that undulates at slow retrieves; works in clear-water lagoon side channels of the Nicaraguan Mosquito Coast where tarpon lay up and feed less aggressively than in main-river situations.

Explicitly listed by Fly Fishing Caribe as their first recommended tarpon fly for Bocas del Toro in sizes 3/0–5/0 on TIEMCO 600SP or Gamakatsu SL15 hooks; the Toad's pulsing marabou is effective in the turbid mix-water river mouths of the Changuinola and Sixaola.

Specifically named by the All Points Fly Shop Cuba guide in both black/purple and chartreuse for Cayo Largo's flats and channel tarpon; Cuba Fishing Outfitters also cites the Toad as one of three must-have Cuba tarpon flies.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Small (#2–1/0) Tarpon Toad in black/purple or chartreuse is the standard juvenile tarpon fly for the IRL's backcountry creeks and is equally productive on snook — already in library.
Occasional tarpon — particularly in August and September off SC beaches and inlets — are targeted with large Toads; also works on schooling reds pushing baitfish — already in library.

Large Tarpon Toad (2/0–3/0) in black/purple or chartreuse is a Tampa Bay rolling-school tarpon standard; also used in small (#2) versions for Pine Island Sound backcountry juvenile tarpon and snook — already in library.

patterns.name: The Usual
patterns.description: Fish-Bones Fly Fishing's signature Cayman bonefish pattern, derived from the Veverka Mantis Shrimp and featured in Dick Brown's Bonefish Fly Patterns. Tied with a tan craft-fur body, rubber legs, and small bead-chain eyes, it matches the mantis shrimp and snapping shrimp of Cayman turtle-grass flats. Fished on a short-twitch retrieve to bonefish rooting in the grass.
patterns.image_source: fish-bones.com — The Usual Cayman bonefish fly official page photo

regional_usage.notes: Grand Cayman guide service Fish-Bones' signature fly, featured in Dick Brown's Bonefish Fly Patterns; derived from Veverka Mantis Shrimp and optimized for Cayman turtle-grass flats with short-twitch retrieve.

patterns.name: Toad
patterns.description: The Texas Toad — also called the Redfish Toad or Louisiana Toad — uses layered craft fur and palmered hackle with rubber legs to create a large, slow-sinking profile that lands with minimal splash. Fished on ultra-shallow Gulf flats with short strips or a slow crawl. An essential sight-fishing pattern for tailing redfish and speckled trout across the entire Gulf Coast.
patterns.image_source: Sight Cast Fishing Company — Texas Toad group product shot, multiple colorways clean white background

regional_usage.notes: Sometimes called the Redfish Toad or Texas Toad, this craft-fur-and-hackle pattern is an iconic Gulf Coast redfish fly whose slow sink rate and lifelike movement excel in shallow Louisiana marsh flats.

Known in Texas as the Texas Toad, this craft-fur-and-rubber-leg pattern is a cornerstone of the Lower Laguna sight-fishing game; it lands softly enough to avoid spooking the wary redfish on ultra-shallow flats.

regional_usage.region: Mosquito Lagoon & Indian River Lagoon, FL
regional_usage.notes: Baitfish-profile subsurface pattern that catches virtually all IRL inshore species, particularly effective for schooling reds and backcountry snook — already in library.
Dark-color Toad (black/purple) is a Lowcountry flood-tide classic; its rubber-leg movement entices reds digging in spartina grass — already in library.
Black Toad is the documented go-to pattern for Georgia flood-tide reds; Capt. David Edens has used it for years as a primary fly in the Golden Isles marsh — already in library.

patterns.name: Turneffe Crab
patterns.description: A sparse, flat-profile crab tied in olive-cream or tan with rubber legs and lead or bead-chain eyes. Craig Matthews' design uses minimal materials for a fast-sinking, realistic crab silhouette that lands quietly. Sized #2–#6 for permit on clear-water tailing flats in Belize and Yucatan. The sparse tie lets the rubber legs flutter naturally with almost no retrieve.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com product photo of Turneffe Crab in olive/cream, clean side-profile view

regional_usage.region: Ascension Bay & Espíritu Santo Bay, Mexico (Yucatán)
regional_usage.notes: Listed by Pesca Maya's Ascension Bay permit fly recommendations; the pattern's sparse profile suits Yucatán's clear-water tailing permit situations.
Oliver White's other top Sudan trigger recommendation; lead eyes and heavy-wire hook put the fly on the bottom where tailing fish pin their prey before eating.
Listed in Fly Fishing Caribe's Honduras Guanaja permit fly recommendations; the sparse, hook-up Turneffe Crab is well-suited to the clear water and coral-bottom conditions of Honduras's Bay Islands.

patterns.name: Velcro Crab
patterns.description: Low-profile crab with a Velcro loop body that grips bottom debris, creating a convincing crab resting on the flat. Bead-chain eyes orient the hook up. Recommended by Orvis and Deep Water Cay for Bahamas permit; standard Keys technique is to let it settle on bottom and strip only when a permit tips down to feed.
patterns.image_source: Superflies.com — Velcro Crab tan/orange professional product photo

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Recommended by Orvis / Deep Water Cay lodge system for permit in the Bahamas; on out-island permit encounters the fly is allowed to settle to the bottom and stripped only on the take — a proven technique on Acklins permit.

A standard permit pattern for the Keys guides; effective for the large permit that cruise the edges of the channels and flats around the Content Keys and Marquesas where Del Brown did much of his record permit fishing.
Top Bahamas permit crab called out by Deep Water Cay guides; presented ahead of cruising permit with a bottom-sinking drift, also taken by big bonefish.
Velcro-body crab that resists grass pick-up and presents a realistic outline; widely used in SC/GA for flood-tide reds in spartina where weed-free retrieves are essential — already in library.
Weed-resistant crab that pushes cleanly through the thick spartina of Golden Isles flood-tide flats; standard supplement to the Toad and Fiddlestick in GA guide boxes — already in library.

patterns.name: Veverka Mantis Shrimp
patterns.description: Bob Veverka's soft-landing mantis shrimp imitation, tied with bead-chain eyes (not lead) for a slow, quiet entry that won't spook shallow bonefish. The segmented, mottled body imitates the distinctive profile of mantis shrimp found on Bahamian and Cuban flats. Considered by multiple outfitters the top bonefish fly for Jardines de la Reina; equally effective on Andros and Abaco where fish are accustomed to seeing large shrimp and often refuse smaller patterns.
patterns.image_source: SaltwaterFlies.com — Bob Veverka's Mantis Shrimp, product photo on plain background

regional_usage.notes: Cuba Fishing Outfitters reports a JDR guide pulling it from a fly box at Zapata and saying 'Put this on, and don't take it off'; now considered the top bonefish fly for Cuba by multiple outfitters.

Bob Veverka's soft-landing pattern with bead-chain eyes is productive year-round and is recommended by Andros-area lodges specifically because it presents softly to the notoriously spooky Andros fish.

regional_usage.region: Abaco & Bahamas Out Islands (Long Island, Acklins, Crooked Island)
regional_usage.notes: Recommended by the Deep Water Cay / Bahamas lodge system for its soft entry with bead-chain eyes; particularly important for the spooky Abaco Marls fish that refuse flies that hit the water hard.
Hawaii-designed mantis shrimp with individually tied articulated legs to mimic the abundant mantis shrimp on Hawaiian reef flats.

Mantis shrimp imitations are confirmed as part of the essential bonefish box for Los Roques by the Explore Yachts guide; the large, abundant mantis shrimp population in the turtle grass flats makes this a natural and highly effective choice for the above-average-sized bonefish.
Soft landing and realistic mantis-shrimp profile make it a top choice for cautious T&C fish; Soul Fly Lodge (Berry Islands) and Deep Water Cay guides both recommend it as a first-choice pattern.
The parent pattern of Fish-Bones' The Usual — bead-chain eyes provide gentle landing for pressured Cayman bones tailing in shallow turtle grass.
Soft entry and realistic mantis shrimp silhouette suit Bonaire's clear, calm Sorobon-lagoon conditions where sight-fishing is the norm.

Cuba Fishing Outfitters identifies this as 'the top bonefish fly for Cuba'; at Cayo Cruz it works particularly well for the large, unpressured bonefish that feed aggressively on mantis shrimp in the deeper mottled-bottom areas.

patterns.name: Wahoo Needlefish
patterns.description: Slim needlefish imitation 20–25 cm in white/silver built with EP fibers or mesh-tube body on 5/0–7/0 with wire bite tippet. Fished on 12-wt outfits with fast-sinking lines at Nosy Be's offshore FADs and seamount banks. Retrieved at high speed with fast 60 cm strips. Targets wahoo, king mackerel, and dogtooth tuna in current lines.
patterns.image_source: Umpqua Feather Merchants — Ka-Cudda (Barracuda/Needlefish pattern)

regional_usage.notes: Long (20–25 cm) slim needlefish imitation fished on 12 wt with fast-sinking line; wahoo and Spanish mackerel are regular targets at Nosy Be's offshore FADs and banks. EXISTS IN LIBRARY as 'Needlefish'.

patterns.name: Wayne's Milky Magic
patterns.description: Wayne Haselau's Alphonse Island milkfish fly tied with a chenille body that imitates crustacean egg sacs clinging to algae mats. Milkfish filter-feed on these sacs in tidal lagoons; the Milky Magic is dropped into the feeding lane and allowed to drift with the current on a long, light leader. One of the top-producing milkfish patterns across Seychelles and Christmas Island flats.
patterns.image_source: BigTime Flies product photo of Wayne's Milky Magic — clean close-up on white background

regional_usage.notes: Designed by the same Alphonse guide who created the Pillow Talk; the chenille body imitates the egg sacs of crustaceans in algae beds and is one of the top-producing milkfish patterns at Christmas Island.

Designed by Alphonse guide Wayne Haselau, who also pioneered milkfish fly fishing at St. Francois lagoon; the chenille body imitates crustacean egg sacs in algae and is a top milkfish fly across all Seychelles operations.

patterns.name: Weapon of Mass Destruction (WMD)
patterns.description: Alec Gerbec's Seychelles shrimp pattern features a thin rubber tail, sparse synthetic fiber body, and bead-chain eyes on a wide-gap hook. Designed to provoke reaction strikes from trigger-sensitive yellowmargin and titan triggerfish on Alphonse and Cosmoledo flats. Fished with a dead-drop presentation followed by tiny twitches — the fly triggers hits while still sinking.

regional_usage.notes: Developed by Umpqua's Alec Gerbec for Seychelles triggerfish; the rubber-tailed shrimp profile triggers violent reaction strikes and is documented to provoke hits while sinking on Alphonse and Cosmoledo trigger flats.

patterns.name: Webster's Shrouser
patterns.description: Lead-eye shrimp-and-crab hybrid that sinks quickly for deeper mottled-flat presentations, specifically requested by Cayo Largo guide Frankie (All Points Fly Shop) for Cayo Cruz's permit and bonefish. The Shrouser's rubberleg action and mixed shrimp-crab silhouette is versatile enough for both species. Fished with a slow hand-twist retrieve or dead drift on slightly deeper Cuban permit flats.

patterns.name: Whitlock's Sheep Fly
patterns.description: Dave Whitlock's sheep-hair streamer uses the unique texture of sheep/ram wool to create a densely fibered but water-permeable body that pulses and breathes on the retrieve. The natural oils in the wool give it lifelike action. Used in Ascension Bay for subsurface snook presentations in mangrove channels, typically retrieved with slow, irregular strips along shaded edges.
